details_text: HackSprint 3.0 — Build Bold. Ride Beyond. About the Event HackSprint 3.0 is a national-level, 36-hour hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, in collaboration with the Metaverse Association. HackSprint 3.0 brings together passionate developers, designers, problem-solvers, and innovators from across India to transform creative ideas into impactful, technology-driven solutions. It provides a platform to experiment with emerging technologies, collaborate with like-minded innovators, and tackle real-world challenges. Mode: Online Preliminary Round + Offline Final Round Final Venue: Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu Final Hackathon Duration: 36 hours Application Deadline: 28 December 2026 PPT Submission Template: Will be announced soon! How It Works Round 1: Online Idea Submission & Screening The first round will be conducted online. Interested teams must submit a PowerPoint presentation (PPT) outlining their proposed project idea before the application deadline. The presentation should explain: Problem Statement: What real-world problem are you addressing? Proposed Solution: How will your idea solve the problem? Innovation: What makes your approach unique? Feasibility: How can the solution be implemented? Expected Impact: Who will benefit from your solution? Team Portfolio: Relevant projects, technical skills, and previous work, where available. The organizing team will evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and relevant portfolio experience. Following the evaluation, selected teams will be shortlisted for the final round. Important: Submitting an application does not guarantee participation in the final hackathon. Only shortlisted teams will be invited to the offline round. Round 2: Offline Final Hackathon Shortlisted teams will participate in the 36-hour offline hackathon at Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore. Participants will develop their proposed solutions, build prototypes, test their implementations, and present their projects to the judging panel. Final evaluation will focus on innovation, technical implementation, functionality, feasibility, problem-solving, and overall impact. Final-round dates will be announced once confirmed. HackSprint 3.0 Tracks 1. Agrotech Leverage technology to address agricultural challenges through smart irrigation, precision farming, AI-enabled agriculture, resource optimization, and sustainable farming solutions. 2. MedTech Develop technology-driven healthcare solutions focused on diagnostics, remote healthcare, medical accessibility, patient monitoring, and improved healthcare delivery. 3. EduTech Reimagine education through digital learning platforms, adaptive learning systems, skill-development tools, inclusive education, and innovative teaching technologies. 4. WildVisionTech Explore AI- and ML-powered solutions for wildlife conservation, anti-poaching intelligence, environmental monitoring, and biodiversity protection. 5. Open Innovation Think without boundaries. Build creative, technology-driven solutions to meaningful real-world problems across any domain. What Awaits You? An opportunity to showcase your creativity and technical skills. A platform to transform ideas into practical solutions. Collaboration with passionate developers, designers, and innovators. An opportunity to present your work and receive feedback from the judging panel. Recognition for outstanding innovation and problem-solving. Prize details, partners, and additional opportunities will be announced through official HackSprint 3.0 communication channels. Rules & Regulations Idea Submission: Teams must submit their project proposal as a PPT before the first-round deadline. Screening: Teams will be shortlisted based on their ideas and relevant portfolios. Final-Round Eligibility: Only shortlisted teams may part

title: Aegython 2026
description: Official registration required: After registering on Unstop, every team member must complete the official AEGYTHON Google Form — only Google Form entries are considered for shortlisting:…
details_text: Official registration required: After registering on Unstop, every team member must complete the official AEGYTHON Google Form — only Google Form entries are considered for shortlisting: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeNfr0ah_d2yHuBzVZmRY87gkt7e4mGOcIB0IqczaUSl8ok9w/viewform Overview Organised by AeglysAI | Free Participation | Individual and Team Entries AEGYTHON 2026 is an AI/ML and Cybersecurity hackathon that challenges students, developers, engineers, and researchers to build practical, intelligent solutions for real-world problems. Participants will explore areas such as identity security, anomaly detection, API traffic monitoring, security alert explanation, outage prediction, and AI-powered solutions for everyday challenges. The focus is on working prototypes, technical understanding, responsible innovation, and reproducible results—not just ideas or presentations. Challenge Areas Participants can choose from six problem statements: Smart Login Guardian: Identify suspicious login attempts and explain potential risk signals. Find the Anomaly: Detect unusual patterns in synthetic data or system measurements. API Traffic Watch: Identify unusual API request patterns and traffic spikes using synthetic requests. Explain My Security Alert: Convert structured security alerts into clear explanations and safe recommendations. Predict the Outage: Analyse synthetic system metrics to identify early warning signs of possible outages. AI for Everyday Life: Build a practical AI/ML solution addressing a meaningful everyday problem. Eligibility Students, graduate students, early-career engineers, experienced practitioners, and researchers are the intended audience. Beginners and first-time contributors can explore the Foundation track; experienced participants may pursue more advanced engineering work. Participation is free. Every participant must complete the mandatory individual AeglysAI qualification and be selected before competing. Age and geographic eligibility must be confirmed in the final official event terms. Team Formation Participants may register individually. Teams may consist of 1–4 participants, including the team leader. Every team member must independently complete the qualification process and be selected. A team leader must submit the team roster for organiser verification and obtain a unique team ID. Participants cannot belong to multiple active teams. Team membership changes require organiser approval. Inter-college and inter-specialisation teams should be confirmed with the organisers before being advertised as permitted. Qualification Process Every participant must demonstrate basic familiarity with the AeglysAI project before selection. The qualification process involves: Registering individually through the official form. Forking the official AeglysAI repository into a personal GitHub account. Cloning the fork and demonstrating that the baseline builds or runs. Documenting the basic architecture and request/decision flow. Providing one meaningful technical observation, one realistic improvement idea, and a proposed validation approach. Submitting the required GitHub links and sanitised build evidence for organiser review. Completing qualification does not guarantee selection. Competition Format and Rounds Round 1 — Technical Screening Participants submit a working project, source code, a README with setup instructions, testing or validation evidence, and a demonstration video of no more than two minutes. Reviewers evaluate the solution's functionality, intelligent features, relevance, reproducibility, and video clarity. Round 2 — Finalist Demonstration Shortlisted finalists present their working projects live through Google Meet. Each finalist receives five minutes for the demonstration, followed by five minutes of technical questions and answers. Round 2 determines the final ranking. The two rounds are scored separately. details_text: Overview Krixov presents: AI for Operational Intelligence Case Challenge Build Real. Showcase Skills. Unlock Opportunities. About the Challenge: BUILD2RISE 2026 is an online, idea-based case challenge organized by Krixov. It invites college and university students to analyze real-world operational challenges and propose innovative, practical, data-informed, and responsible AI-enabled solutions. Participants will select one problem statement, analyze its root causes, define the intended users, design a feasible solution, and present their idea through a structured presentation. The challenge focuses on problem-solving, analytical thinking, product innovation, data-driven decision-making, and responsible use of AI. Whether your strengths are technology, business, analytics, design, operations, research, or communication, this is an opportunity to showcase your thinking and present an idea with real-world potential. Event Overview: Event name: BUILD2RISE 2026 Theme: AI for Operational Intelligence Format: Online Competition type: Idea / Case-study presentation Duration: 72 hours (3 days) Problem statements: 6 Participation: Individual or team Team size: 1–4 members Eligibility: Currently enrolled college/university students from any discipline and academic year Submission format: PDF or PowerPoint presentation Rounds: One submission and evaluation round Registration deadline: 15-11-2026 (11:59 PM) Challenge start: 16-11-2026 (12:01 AM) Submission deadline: 18-11-2026 (11:59 PM) Organizer contact: campus@krixov.com Rewards and Recognition: BUILD2RISE 2026 is designed to help students showcase their ideas, strengthen their portfolios, and explore potential career opportunities. 1st and 2nd Place — Top 2 Teams: Internship opportunities Consideration for professional recommendations Winner recognition Opportunity to showcase projects and solutions 3rd, 4th, and 5th Place — Next 3 Teams: Consideration for professional recommendations Recognition among the top-performing teams Opportunity to showcase projects and solutions Other Eligible Participating Teams: - Digital Certificate of Participation for eligible teams that complete the required participation and submission process. Important Reward Terms: Internship opportunities and professional recommendations are subject to eligibility, evaluation, availability, and the organizer’s applicable selection process. They are opportunities for consideration, not a guarantee of an internship, employment, or recommendation. No cash prize is being advertised in this listing. Problem Statements: Participants must select exactly one of the following six problem statements. Problem Statement 1: The Broken Handoff Problem Problem: Work is often delayed when tasks move between departments or team members without complete information, clear ownership, or a defined next action. Challenge: Design a solution that identifies incomplete handoffs, detects missing information, prioritizes tasks at risk of delay, and recommends actions to improve coordination. Expected solution: A workflow-management concept, intelligent checklist, handoff-risk dashboard, or another practical solution. Success measures: Reduced incomplete handoffs, less rework, clearer ownership, and shorter resolution time. Problem Statement 2: The Invisible Cost Detector Problem: Businesses may overlook avoidable operational costs caused by repeated work, unused software licenses, duplicate purchases, and recurring delays. Challenge: Propose a transparent system that identifies potential waste, ranks opportunities for investigation, and estimates possible savings using clear calculations. Expected solution: A cost-intelligence dashboard, expense-analysis system, duplicate-purchase alert, or related concept. Success measures: Better visibility into cost drivers, more reliable identification of potential waste, and transparent savings estimates. Important requirement: Participants must distinguish confirmed waste from uncertain opportunities

title: Agents that act. Systems that answer. | Free Virtual Agentic-AI Hackathon

details_text: About the Hackathon: Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by StudentChakra and co-hosted by Priyanshu Agarwal (founder of NextMove, organiser of Hackorizon). What You'll Build: An agentic AI system for a real person with a real task. Start with a person, not an industry: who are they, what do they hate doing, what does your agent do for them, and where does it break? Solo or in a team of up to 4. No experience required. How Projects Are Judged: We judge how your project behaves when things go wrong: Failure modes: how does it break? Human oversight: who stays in the loop? Intervention: can someone stop it? Reversibility: can a mistake be undone? Plus usefulness to a real person and the quality of your working build. Prizes: $680 in prizes: 1st place about $500 in Apify credits; 2nd and 3rd place Cursor subscriptions. Judges: Experts from AI governance, cybersecurity, venture and OpenAI, including Dr. Esona Fomuso (formerly VP of Technology, JPMorgan Chase), Dr. Aleem Khalid Alvi (Professor of Cybersecurity & Software Engineering, Sheridan College), Kunal Kapoor (Venture Continuity, Katha) and Priyanshu Agarwal (ChatGPT Lab, OpenAI India). Key Dates: Registration closes: Nov 27 Hackathon: Nov 28–30 (virtual) Final results: Dec 8 Who Can Join: Students worldwide, solo or in teams of 1–4. Free.

title: Operation Ward Zero
description: Build a Hospital That Fits Inside a Bedroom About the Hackathon: What if a patient's bedroom could function like a smart hospital ward? Hospitals have monitoring systems, trained healthcare professionals, and alert…
details_text: Build a Hospital That Fits Inside a Bedroom About the Hackathon: What if a patient's bedroom could function like a smart hospital ward? Hospitals have monitoring systems, trained healthcare professionals, and alert mechanisms to detect changes in patient conditions. At home, however, patients often depend on family members and caregivers who may not have access to continuous monitoring or early-warning systems. Operation Ward Zero is an online healthcare technology hackathon inviting innovators, developers, and problem-solvers to design intelligent home healthcare solutions. Participants will develop a working prototype demonstrating how IoT simulation, full-stack applications, and AI/ML can work together to monitor patient conditions, identify potential risks, and support timely caregiver responses. The central mission is: Sense → Understand → Predict → Alert → Respond Participants are encouraged to develop practical, affordable, scalable, and user-friendly solutions that address real-world home healthcare challenges. No physical hardware is required. Participants may use simulated sensors, synthetic patient data, mock devices, and software-based environments. Eligibility Criteria: Open to students, recent graduates, aspiring developers, and technology enthusiasts interested in healthcare innovation. Participants from engineering, computer science, information technology, data science, artificial intelligence, and related disciplines are encouraged to participate. Team Size: Minimum 2 and maximum 3 members. Inter-college teams: Allowed. Participants from different colleges or institutions may form a team. Inter-specialization teams: Allowed. Participants from different academic branches, specializations, or technical backgrounds may collaborate. Each participant may belong to only one team. Each team must nominate one team leader responsible for registration, coordination, and final submission. Participants should possess basic technical knowledge relevant to their chosen solution. Competition Structure and Format: Number of Problem Statements: 1 overarching problem statement covering IoT, Full Stack, and AI/ML. Competition Format: Single-round project submission and evaluation. Round 1: Prototype Development and Submission Participants must develop and submit a working prototype addressing the official problem statement. The submission must demonstrate how the proposed system collects or simulates patient data, processes information, identifies risks, generates alerts, and enables caregiver responses. Submission Deadline: 24 October 2026 Participants must submit their solution through the official Wooble challenge page. Round 2: Evaluation and Results: All eligible submissions will be evaluated by the designated reviewers based on predefined technical and practical evaluation criteria. There is no separate live presentation or physical evaluation round specified. Results Announcement: 31 October 2026 Winners will be selected based on their overall evaluation scores and compliance with the competition guidelines. Problem Statement: Build an Intelligent Home Healthcare Monitoring and Response System Design and develop a software-based healthcare monitoring solution that demonstrates how a patient's home can operate like a small, intelligent hospital ward. The proposed solution should illustrate the following workflow: Patient Data → Monitoring Platform → Risk Assessment → Alert Generation → Caregiver Response Participants may address one or more of the following challenges: Patient Monitoring: Simulate and monitor patient vitals such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, and temperature. Caregiver Monitoring: Develop mechanisms to track caregiver attendance, activity, and response to alerts. details_text: Overview Presented by Code Variant — Build Different. Every game begins with an idea. In OUT OF BOUNDS, your team gets 12 hours to turn yours into a playable browser-based experience. OUT OF BOUNDS is an online web game development hackathon that brings together developers, designers, and creative problem-solvers to build original games. Choose your own genre, mechanics, and theme. The goal is to create an experience that people can actually play. Event Format The competition has two rounds. Paid event with a registration fee of ony ₹19 Round 1 — Idea Submission Submit your game concept as a PowerPoint presentation or PDF. Maximum length: 5 slides. Your submission should explain the game overview, core gameplay, originality, player experience, and technical feasibility. Entries will be evaluated using the Round 1 judging criteria. The 50 highest-scoring teams will qualify for Round 2. PPT Submission Deadline: 21 November 2026 Round 2 — The 12-Hour Build Date: 29 November 2026 Time: 9:00 AM – 9:00 PM IST Shortlisted teams will develop and submit a playable web game during the 12-hour build period. The game must run in a modern web browser. A hosted, playable game URL is mandatory. Desktop browser compatibility is required. Mobile compatibility is encouraged. Any game genre or theme is allowed. The submitted game must remain accessible to the judges. Teams must substantially develop their game during the official build period. The Surprise Mechanism At the six-hour mark of the event, a special mechanism will be revealed. Teams must adapt to the additional challenge or rule announced during the event. Team & Registration Rules Team size: 1–4 participants. Registration fee: ₹19 Each participant may belong to only one team. Team composition is locked after registration. Team changes are not allowed. Participants must provide accurate registration details. Final Submission Requirements Teams must submit: A publicly accessible hosted game URL. A source-code repository accessible to the judges. A README explaining the game objective, controls, technologies, instructions, and known limitations. Team name and registered participant details. Disclosure of significant AI assistance, reused code, and third-party assets. An optional 1–3 minute demo video showing actual gameplay. The hosted, playable game is the primary deliverable. A demo video does not replace a functioning game link. Judging Round 1 — Idea Submission (100 points) Originality and differentiation: 25 Gameplay concept and core mechanics: 25 Clarity of the idea: 20 Feasibility within 12 hours: 20 Player appeal and engagement potential: 10 The top 50 teams, ranked by score, advance to Round 2. Round 2 — Final Game (100 points) Gameplay and player experience: 25 Creativity and originality: 20 Technical execution and functionality: 20 Game design and mechanics: 15 Visual design and usability: 10 Completeness and polish: 10 Round 1 scores are not carried forward. Judges evaluate the actual playable game, not just the idea. Prizes & Recognition 1st Place: ₹10,000 2nd Place: ₹1,000 3rd Place: ₹500 Top 10: Excellence certificates Top 50: Shortlisted-team recognition All participants: Participation certificates Tools & Originality AI tools, frameworks, libraries, game engines, and other development aids are allowed, subject to applicable licences. Significant AI assistance, reused code, and third-party assets must be disclosed. Plagiarism, misrepresentation, cheating, sabotage, and fraudulent submissions may result in disqualification. Participants are expected to behave respectfully and professionally. Build Something Different Bring your idea, build your game, and see how far you can take it. OUT OF BOUNDS — Same browser. Bigger worlds. Organised by Code Variant | Build Different.

It provides participants with a platform to brainstorm, design, and develop innovative solutions in domains such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Web3, the Internet of Things (IoT), HealthTech, environmental innovation, and education. HackNova encourages creativity, teamwork, and experiential learning, empowering participants to transform their ideas into practical solutions that create a meaningful impact on society, industry, and the environment. Why Participate in HackNova? Solve Real-World Problems Work on meaningful challenges that address real issues affecting society, industry, and the environment. Promote Social and Environmental Sustainability Embrace the principle of "Real Problems, Real Solutions" by developing innovative approaches that support healthy, sustainable, and thriving communities. Build. Transform.

title: Haven Ahmedabad
description: About the Event Welcome to Haven Ahmedabad , a beginner-friendly, 24-hour problem-solving game jam tailored specifically for high school students . Scheduled for November 14th to 15th , this event invites programmers,…
details_text: About the Event Welcome to Haven Ahmedabad , a beginner-friendly, 24-hour problem-solving game jam tailored specifically for high school students . Scheduled for November 14th to 15th , this event invites programmers, artists, and engineers to spend 24 immersive hours together building fun computer games . Following in the footsteps of major gatherings like Daydream and Campfire Ahmedabad (which was hosted at Ahmedabad University on February 28, 2026, as part of Hack Club's worldwide network of 100 concurrent events and 7,000 attendees) , Haven brings the vibrant energy of global hackathons right to your doorstep. Organized under Hack Club—a 501(c)(3) nonprofit empowering over 50,000 teenagers worldwide to code —this is your space to innovate, create, and collaborate. Our Mission Our mission is to inspire the next generation of makers across Gujarat and beyond by introducing you to game development in a fun, collaborative, and low-stakes environment . Working in teams, you will tackle exciting challenges and build incredible projects that enhance your creativity, collaboration, and innovation skills . For us, hacking is all about problem-solving, making cool projects, and forging lifelong friendships with fellow coders, makers, and artists . Whether you are writing your first line of code or designing your next masterpiece, Haven is designed to help you discover the joy of creating . Why Ahmedabad? Ahmedabad is the ultimate home for Haven . As India's first UNESCO World Heritage City and home to world-class institutions like IIT Gandhinagar, CEPT, and NID, the city has always been a buzzing hub of innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity . Rooted in the local spirit of jugaad (innovative problem-solving) and collaboration—from our historic textile mills to today's thriving startup ecosystem—young makers across neighborhoods from Navrangpura and Satellite to Maninagar and Vastrapur are brimming with potential . Haven Ahmedabad brings together young creators from all over to learn, build, and grow together . What to Expect Beginner-Friendly Atmosphere: No prior game jam experience? No problem! Dive into coding and design in a supportive, low-stakes environment . 24 Hours of Creation: Spend an intense, fun-filled day and night building games, learning from peers, and bringing your ideas to life . Community & Mentorship: Connect with fellow high school coders, artists, and engineers, draw inspiration from your peers, and build lasting friendships . Requirements Demographics: The event is open to high school students (almost all under 18) who are excited to code . Technology: Attendees need to bring their own devices and setup to code, with Wi-Fi and power outlets provided at the venue to support participants . Safety & Permissions: Attendees must follow the official Code of Conduct . Leaving the premises is restricted except during designated, parent-approved outdoor activities with the appropriate parental waiver signed . Join us, build something amazing, and help shape the future of tech in Ahmedabad!

title: Drone Soccer | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A drone soccer competition where teams pilot custom-built, caged drones through an obstacle-filled arena to score points by flying through a circular goal ring. Matches are conducted as timed sprints focusing on agility, defense, and scoring precision.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 5 members; cross-college teams are allowed.
requirements: Custom-built or configured drones with protective cages (no standard RTF models) and the use of only one main drone model.
details_text: Rules & Guidelines: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 members . Cross-college teams are allowed—participants from different institutions can team up. Model Regulations: Each team must use its own custom-built or custom-configured drone wrapped in a protective cage/exoskeleton; exchanging models or components between teams during match rounds is strictly prohibited. Standard RTF (Ready-To-Fly) commercial consumer drones are not allowed, though pre-programmed flight controllers and stabilization boards are permitted. Only one main drone model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams will receive a 2-minute warm-up/trial period before Round 2 matches. Lifting or repositioning the drone manually during active gameplay is strictly prohibited. A drone that crashes and is unable to take off within the allotted restart window immediately forfeits that specific attempt or round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on all match rules, scoring disputes, and safety calls. Event Structure: Round 1: Drone Soccer Arena Showdown: Obstacle & Defender Navigation: Teams must pilot their caged drones through an active arena featuring physical obstacles and designated opponent defense zones. Goal Scoring Task: Teams must navigate their drone past defensive barricades and maneuver it cleanly through the elevated circular Goal Ring to score points. Each successful goal scored within the match time earns points based on precision and execution. If a goal attempt fails, misses, or bounces off the goal frame, no points are awarded, but no negative penalty is incurred. Teams can immediately reset and attempt another run. Match Execution: Matches are conducted in timed sprints where agility, mid-air defense, collision recovery, and scoring accuracy determine the final winners.

title: Multirotor | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A two-round drone competition where teams navigate through rings and obstacles to complete a payload delivery task. Participants must fly custom-built drones to score points through precision maneuvering and QR code identification.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 6 members; inter-college teams are permitted.
requirements: A custom-built drone (no RTF models) equipped with an onboard camera for QR scanning.
details_text: Rules: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 6 members. Participants from different colleges can form a team. Model Regulations: Each team must have its own custom-built drone; exchanging models between teams is strictly prohibited. RTF (Ready-To-Fly) models are not allowed, but pre-programmed boards can be used. Only one model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams can have a 2-minute trial before Round 2. Lifting the drone manually to improve position during any round is not allowed. Any failed landing attempt that does not result in a score immediately ends the round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on any disputes. Event Structure: Round 1: Teams must fly their drone through 5 circular rings placed at varying heights (between 1 meter to 2.5 meters). Each ring carries different points based on difficulty. Teams must avoid touching the rings to earn points. Skipping a ring results in no points but does not incur a penalty. Maximum time for completion: 8 minutes. Qualification Criteria: Teams with the highest scores will advance to Round 2. Round 2: Obstacle Navigation: Teams must maneuver through multiple obstacles, which will be disclosed on the spot. Payload Task: The onboard camera scans a QR code to identify a specific payload. If scanning fails, teams can receive the QR details manually but will lose detection points. The identified payload must be dropped into a designated area. No penalty for unsuccessful drops, but no points are awarded either.

details_text: Overview DATANYX'26 is Telangana’s flagship 24-hour datathon, now in its third edition. It is organized by AWS Student Builder Group MJCET and IEEE SMC MJCET. It is a 24-hour event where you take raw data and turn it into a working prototype. You start from scratch. The problem statements, datasets are given to you on the first day. DATANYX started in 2024 as the first 24 hr datathon in Telangana. In 2025, it grew into a national event. This year, every problem is linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. So what you build can help solve real problems in the world. Domains: AgroTech (SDG 2, 12, 13, 15) EdTech (SDG 1, 4, 8) Urban Tech (SDG 6, 7, 9, 11) MedTech (SDG 3, 5, 10) Event Details: Dates: 28th and 29th November 2026 Venue: Ghulam Ahmed Hall, MJCET, Hyderabad Mode: Offline Event Structure: Phase 1 - Shortlisting Round (Online): In the first phase, teams are required to submit a unique problem statement of their own creation, accompanied by a solution abstract with a presentation that aligns with their selected domain. Teams must choose from one of the following domains: Med Tech, Urban Tech, Agro Tech or EdTech. The proposed presentation should reflect originality and innovation within the chosen domain.All submissions must be completed online on the provided PPT Template before the designated deadline. The DATANYX'26 PPT TEMPLATE & the DOMAIN DESCRIPTION are attached below . Phase 2 - Finals (MJCET): The top 15 teams from each domain will qualify for the final phase, held in person at MJCET, Hyderabad. Here, teams will be given a new problem statement revealed on the spot along with a sample dataset. They will then have 24 hours to brainstorm, design, implement, build, and submit their final solutions. This phase tests the teams' ability to think critically and collaborate effectively under pressure, turning ideas into impactful solutions within a limited timeframe. Shortlisted teams are required to pay a participation fee of ₹1000. Step 1: Getting Started: Click the Unstop link for Datanyx. Find the "Register" button and click it. Step 2: Sign In (Super Easy!): Choose your sign-in option: Google (fastest!) LinkedIn Email Enter your details: Phone number Email Wait for the OTP on your phone and enter it. Step 3: Your Basic Info: Fill in the following details: Your name School or workplace Course details Graduation date Country of residence Step 4: Team Formation: If you’re the Team Leader: Create your team: Choose a team name. Add teammates' emails. Remind them to check their email for the "View Opportunity" link. Watch for teammates' names to turn GREEN once they join! If you're joining someone’s team: Find the team name. Click "Send Request". Wait for the team leader to add you. Step 5: PPT Submission: Download the PPT template Create your PPT with the team Submit your PPT in the PPT  Submission box in PDF format . Step 6: Final Check: Find the "View Details" button. If it's GREEN = You’re all set! If it's RED = Someone still needs to confirm. Pro Tip: Make sure everyone confirms their participation—green names mean your team is ready! title: The Last Daemon
description: Overview The Last Daemon — Capture The Flag (CTF) by Beunwrapd Join the Official WhatsApp Community: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EpDiRs3oQ1t6riNwVgGJqF About the Competition The digital world is full of secrets,…
details_text: Overview The Last Daemon — Capture The Flag (CTF) by Beunwrapd Join the Official WhatsApp Community: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EpDiRs3oQ1t6riNwVgGJqF About the Competition The digital world is full of secrets, vulnerabilities, and hidden information. Are you ready to uncover them? The Last Daemon is a cybersecurity Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organized by Beunwrapd , designed to challenge aspiring ethical hackers, cybersecurity enthusiasts, and students through hands-on security problems. Participants will test their technical knowledge, analytical thinking, investigative abilities, and problem-solving skills across multiple cybersecurity domains. From decoding cryptographic messages to investigating digital evidence and uncovering web vulnerabilities, every challenge will push participants to think critically and approach problems creatively. Whether you are an experienced CTF player or a beginner exploring cybersecurity, The Last Daemon invites you to test your skills and compete against other participants. No teams. No shortcuts. Just you, your skills, and the challenge. Competition Domains Participants can expect challenges across the following cybersecurity domains: Web Security: Identify vulnerabilities and solve web-based security challenges. Cryptography: Decode encrypted messages and uncover hidden flags. Digital Forensics: Investigate files, metadata, and digital evidence. OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Analyze publicly available information to uncover clues. Reverse Engineering: Analyze programs and uncover their underlying logic. Miscellaneous: Solve unconventional technical puzzles requiring creativity and logical reasoning. Challenges may vary in difficulty, allowing participants to demonstrate their skills and learn through practical problem-solving. Eligibility and Participation Guidelines The competition is open to students and cybersecurity enthusiasts interested in ethical hacking and information security. Participants from all colleges, universities, academic disciplines, and specializations are welcome. Participation Mode: Solo Only. Every participant must compete individually. Team formation and team registrations are not permitted. Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are not applicable because this is an individual competition. Every participant must register individually through the official Unstop listing. Participants must use their own registered accounts to access challenges and submit flags. Beginners are welcome. A basic understanding of computers and cybersecurity concepts may be helpful. Competition Format Competition Type: Capture The Flag (CTF) Participation Mode: Individual / Solo Format: Challenge-based cybersecurity competition Challenge Domains: Web Security, Cryptography, Digital Forensics, OSINT, Reverse Engineering, and Miscellaneous Number of Challenges: To be announced through the official competition platform. Competition Duration: The confirmed date, start time, end time, and total duration will be communicated through the official event listing or organizer announcements. How It Works Register: Complete your individual registration through Unstop. Access the Platform: Follow the instructions provided by the organizers. Solve Challenges: Investigate and solve problems across the available cybersecurity domains. Capture the Flags: Find hidden flags and submit them through the designated platform. Earn Points: Gain points for correctly solving challenges according to their assigned values. Climb the Leaderboard: Compete individually against other participants. Final Results: Rankings will be determined according to the official scoring and tie-breaking rules. All challenges must be solved independently. Collaboration on solutions and sharing flags with other competitors during the competition are prohibited. Rules and Regulations Individual Participation: Every participant must compete independently. Team participation and joint submissions are prohibited. Fair Play

title: AI Sovereignty: Can India Own Its AI Future Workshop - Session Pass
description: About the opportunity Artificial intelligence is becoming strategic infrastructure, shaping productivity, public services, national security and economic power. India brings real strengths: digital public…
details_text: About the opportunity Artificial intelligence is becoming strategic infrastructure, shaping productivity, public services, national security and economic power. India brings real strengths: digital public infrastructure, a deep technology talent base, demand across many languages, and a growing AI ecosystem backed by the IndiaAI Mission. Yet dependence on others for advanced chips, large-scale computing, long-term capital and proprietary platforms forces difficult choices. Sovereignty is not isolation. It is the freedom to choose, build, deploy and govern AI on India’s terms. What the session will cover The AI stack: which parts of chips, compute, cloud, data, models and applications India must control Build or partner: whether complete self-reliance is realistic, or whether resilient interdependence is a better goal India’s edge: where Indian-language, domain-specific and population-scale AI can lead globally Economics of scale: affordable compute, research depth, patient capital and reliable energy Trust and governance: protecting data, security and public trust while encouraging competition and innovation The next 3–5 years: the decisive moves by government, industry and academia that can’t wait until 2047 Who should attend: Working professionals and business leaders, founders, faculty and policy enthusiasts, and UG/PG students from any institute. Format: A talk or moderated dialogue, followed by audience Q&A. What you get: Entry to the session with live Q&A, and networking with PGPEM executives, alumni and students from 150+ institutes. Rules: Carry a valid photo ID for campus entry; registration is confirmed only on Unstop; seats are allotted first come, first served; please be seated 10 minutes early; the schedule may change.

title: The Human Imperative: Purpose, Creativity and Agency in the Age of AI Workshop - Panel 1 - Day 1
description: Overview Artificial intelligence is moving beyond assistance into creation, analysis and increasingly autonomous action. As machines write, design, code, advise and act, the challenge is no longer only what technology…
details_text: Overview Artificial intelligence is moving beyond assistance into creation, analysis and increasingly autonomous action. As machines write, design, code, advise and act, the challenge is no longer only what technology can do, but what it means for people to exercise judgment, find meaning and make an original contribution. This Drishti 2026 panel asks a bigger question than whether AI will replace jobs: what kind of work, leadership, culture and society should India deliberately build alongside capable machines on the path to 2047? What the panel will discuss Human agency, judgment and accountability — which decisions must remain human as AI moves from advising to acting Purpose, identity and the dignity of work as roles and careers are redefined Imagination, culture and originality in a world of machine-generated content Education, skills and cognitive independence without dependence on AI The decisive moves leaders and policymakers must make by 2035 Who should participate Working professionals and business leaders Founders and entrepreneurs Faculty, researchers and policy enthusiasts UG/PG students from any institute Format & schedule Moderated panel discussion with four leaders: a CHRO, an AI ethicist, an organisational behaviour researcher and an AI company leader Audience Q&A What you get Entry to the session with live audience Q&A High tea Networking with PGPEM executives, alumni and students from 150+ institutes Eligibility & rules Open to working professionals, founders, faculty and UG/PG students from any institute. details_text: Note: Mandatory Registration on : https://techfest.org/workshops/prompt-engineering All further updates will be  from Techfest website only ,its mandatory to register in the website . All that you need to know about Techfest Prompt Engineering Workshop Prompt Engineering Workshop: Prompt Engineering is the practice of turning a raw AI model into a precise, reliable tool  structuring instructions well enough to get accurate, consistent, and usable output every single time. It sits at the intersection of human intent and AI systems, going far beyond "how to talk to ChatGPT" to cover grounding prompts in real data, multimodal inputs, and prompt security  the exact standards enterprise AI teams work with in 2026. Today, this skill is being demanded across every function, not just tech roles: software, finance, healthcare, marketing, legal, and education are all pairing domain expertise with the ability to drive AI effectively, a combination that pays a premium over either skill alone. From building multi-step reasoning chains to structuring content so AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude actually cite it (Generative Engine Optimization, the AI-era equivalent of SEO), businesses now run on well-engineered prompts, not lucky guesses  and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across two intensive offline days at IIT Bombay, you'll go from foundational prompt structures to a real, evaluated prompt system you'll design, test, and refine yourself  no prior AI or coding background required. Workshop Content Foundations of Prompt Engineering Prompt Structuring & Response Shaping Context, Memory & RAG Domain-Specific & Multimodal Prompting Zero-Shot & Few-Shot Learning Advanced Prompting: Chaining & Reasoning Patterns Adaptive & Self-Optimizing Prompt Systems Prompt Security & Evaluation AI Search & GEO Capstone: Build & Test Systems + Certification

description: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline…
details_text: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline (Concept Sessions, Live Demos & Hands-On Practice) Limited Seat available: About the Workshop Agentic AI represents the biggest paradigm shift in applied artificial intelligence since basic chatbots. Modern enterprise solutions are rapidly evolving from simple single-turn systems to fully autonomous, tool-using agents capable of planning, deciding, and acting. This intensive 2-day hands-on workshop covers the entire agent lifecycle—from core reasoning loops and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to multi-agent orchestration, safety guardrails, and real-world deployment. Participants will build functional agents from scratch using industry-standard frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Why You Should Attend: Master Next-Gen Tech: Deep-dive into the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—the open standard for connecting models directly to enterprise tools and data. Hands-On Experience: Build, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end agents with real-world execution. Framework Mastery: Gain direct technical exposure to LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and vector database integrations. Production-Grade Design: Learn memory management, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoints, system safety, and token-cost optimization. Workshop Syllabus & Core Topics: Agentic Foundations & Architectures: Transition from chatbots to autonomous agents, master the Sense-Think-Act-Reflect loop, explore operational autonomy levels, and identify failure mitigation strategies. LLM Integration & Prompting: Optimize context windows, implement function calling with JSON schema structured outputs, design production-grade system prompts, and analyze model speed/cost trade-offs. Reasoning & Planning Patterns: Implement multi-step reasoning patterns including ReAct, Reflexion, and Tree-of-Thought alongside automated task decomposition and Orchestrator-Worker routes. Tool Execution & Safety Checkpoints: Design robust tool schemas for deterministic APIs, handle errors with auto-retries, optimize execution (parallel vs. sequential), and integrate Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) safety checks. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Build, connect, and sandbox custom MCP servers using standard Host/Client/Server architecture, primitives, and transport mechanisms (stdio vs. HTTP/SSE). Memory Management & RAG Pipelines: Architect dynamic short-term context and persistent long-term memory using vector databases, context engineering, dynamic session state, and high-retrieval RAG. Multi-Agent Systems & Frameworks: Construct peer-to-peer and hierarchical agent topologies using state handoffs, while comparing leading frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Capstone Build & Deployment: Hands-on experience building, debugging, benchmarking, and applying guardrails to deploy a production agent as an API, Web App, or Chat Interface.

title: Truss-T The Process
description: Design Smart. Build Strong. Bear the Load. Competition Description: Think you have what it takes to design a bridge that can withstand the ultimate load test? Welcome to TRUSS-T , a team-based structural engineering…
details_text: Design Smart. Build Strong. Bear the Load. Competition Description: Think you have what it takes to design a bridge that can withstand the ultimate load test? Welcome to TRUSS-T , a team-based structural engineering challenge where creativity, calculations, and construction come together! Teams must design and construct a bridge using ice cream sticks within the specified dimensions of 25 cm × 10 cm . The bridge must follow a truss structure, with the design, geometry, and arrangement of members decided by the team members themselves. Once construction is complete, the bridge will be mounted on the designated supports, and weights will be gradually suspended from its centre to test its load-bearing capacity. The real challenge lies in achieving maximum strength with a limited set of materials. Can your truss design withstand the greatest load without structural failure? Design intelligently. Build precisely. Prove your engineering. Competition Format: Participation: Team-based Duration: As announced by the organizers Construction Material: Ice cream sticks and organizer-approved joining materials Bridge Dimensions: 25 cm × 10 cm, as specified by the organizers Structural Type: Truss bridge Testing Method: Incremental loading at the centre of the bridge Winning Criteria: Maximum load sustained before structural failure Rules and Regulations: Each team must design and construct a bridge using ice cream sticks within the prescribed dimensions. The bridge must incorporate a recognizable truss structure, with the arrangement and geometry of the truss members decided by the team. Only materials approved by the organizers may be used for construction. Teams must complete their bridges within the allotted time. The completed bridge must satisfy the specified dimensional and support requirements before testing. During testing, the bridge will be placed on standardized supports, and weights will be suspended from its centre using the designated loading arrangement. Loads will be increased gradually according to the organizers' testing procedure. Participants must not touch, adjust, or reinforce the bridge once load testing begins. The maximum load sustained before structural failure will determine the team's performance. All participants must follow the organizers' safety instructions during construction and testing. The organizers' decisions regarding dimensional compliance, structural failure, and final results will be binding. Judging Criteria: Load-Bearing Capacity: Maximum load sustained before structural failure. Design and Structural Integrity: Effectiveness of the truss arrangement and load distribution. Dimensional Compliance: Adherence to the specified bridge dimensions. Rule Compliance: Use of permitted materials and adherence to construction and testing procedures. Winner Selection: The team whose bridge sustains the highest load before structural failure will be declared the winner, provided it satisfies all competition requirements. In case of a tie, the organizers may use the bridge's self-weight and load-to-weight ratio as secondary criteria, provided these are announced before the competition. Prizes and Certificates: The organizers will award prizes and certificates to winning teams, with certificates of participation for eligible participants. What to Expect: TRUSS-T challenges participants to apply the principles of truss mechanics, force distribution, tension, compression, and structural stability in a hands-on engineering environment. Every joint, member, and connection can influence the final result. Can your bridge carry the weight of your engineering?

details_text: About the Case: TrueFan AI: The Synthetic Scale-Up is a strategic business case challenge under the Founders’ Office, Executive Operations & Corporate Strategy track, in association with Masters’ Union School of Business. Optimize GPU compute and engineering bandwidth between batch video generation and real-time AI video agents. Evaluate the ₹20 lakh charity-bond Chief of Staff recruitment model, considering its impact on talent quality, brand perception, socioeconomic diversity, and operational effectiveness. details_text: About: The National Aeromodelling Challenge is presented by Techfest, IIT Bombay, for students passionate about aerospace and engineering. Teams design, build, and fly their own fixed-wing electric RC aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads. They first prove their aircraft can carry and land a payload safely, then complete a timed two-trip delivery mission. Ready-made models are not allowed. Bring your aircraft to life at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia’s largest science and technology festival. Structure: The competition has an abstract screening stage, followed by a Qualifier Round and a Main Round at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to school, UG, and PG students. Teams can include students from different colleges or schools. Participants must carry a bona fide certificate signed by their HoD/Dean/Principal and a valid ID card. Team Size: 2 to 4 members. A participant can be part of only one team. Problem Statement: Design, build, and fly a fixed-wing aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads (45 g, 43 mm diameter, supplied by organizers) and completes the tasks in each round. Abstract Submission (Online): Submit an abstract of under 15 pages (A4, 1.5 line spacing) in the official Aeromodelling 2026 Abstract Form format. The abstract should cover the aircraft’s basic design (dimensions, wing area, velocity, etc.) and how it suits the problem. Attach a zip file of 5-10 photographs taken while building the aircraft. Abstracts not following the format will not be evaluated. Round 1 - Qualifier Round: Carry one or more golf balls inside the aircraft, fly for at least 30 seconds within a 3-minute window, and land with the payload inside the designated area. Score = (payload weight x 100) / aircraft weight without payload. Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts. The top 30 teams advance to the Main Round. Round 2 - Main Round: Complete a round trip of payload delivery within 3 minutes: load, take off, fly at least 30 seconds, land, unload, reload, take off again, fly at least 30 seconds, land, and unload. Loading must be hands-free, using transmitter-operated compartment doors. Score = E1 + E2 - C1 - C2 - C3. Each delivered golf ball earns 10 points per trip, and each second spent on the ground during loading and unloading costs 1 point. Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts. Overall Score = 0.25 x Normalized Qualifier Score + 0.75 x Normalized Main Round Score. Ties are broken by a separate round framed by the judges. Design Constraints: The aircraft must be designed and built by the team (no RTF/ARF/BNF models). Maximum weight is 1 kg without payload. Thrust-to-weight ratio must not exceed 1 without payload. Wingspan is up to 1.2 m, with no tolerance. Propeller diameter is up to 13 inches, and metal propellers are not allowed. Electric motors only. Gyroscopes, programmed mission steps, FPV, and any flying support are prohibited. Timeline: Registration Deadline: 25th November 2026 Abstract Submission Deadline: 25th November 2026 Abstract Result Announcement: 1st December 2026 Qualifier Round: 15th-16th December 2026 Main Round: 17th December 2026 Rules: Register online to receive a Team ID. No late entries are accepted. The same aircraft described in the abstract must be used in both rounds. Damaged aircraft can be repaired but not replaced. No modifications to the aircraft are allowed after the thrust-to-weight ratio is measured. A 2.4 GHz radio is required. Any other frequency must be informed to the organizers in advance. Landing must be within the inner boundary, otherwise a 20% penalty applies. Touching or crossing the outer boundary disqualifies the attempt. Teams must be ready at their turn, or they lose it. Teams must not share aircraft components with other teams. Safety violations or misconduct will lead to penalties or disqualification. The judges’ and organizers’ decisions are final and binding. Updates will be posted on the Techfest website and sent to registered teams. For official announceme

title: Tower of Torque
description: Welcome to the Tower of Torque - Organised by Mechanical Engineering Department of Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology, Burla. Think Fast. Build Tall. Beat the Clock. Competition Description Ready to put your…
details_text: Welcome to the Tower of Torque - Organised by Mechanical Engineering Department of Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology, Burla. Think Fast. Build Tall. Beat the Clock. Competition Description Ready to put your creativity, precision, and structural balancing skills to the ultimate test? Welcome to Tower of Torque , an exciting individual challenge where speed meets stability! Participants must construct the tallest possible freestanding tower using just 20 cups in 60 seconds . No tape, glue, or external support is allowed. Your tower must remain standing independently for at least five seconds to qualify. But there’s a twist! In the final stage, participants must build using their non-dominant hand , challenging their coordination, adaptability, and ability to perform under pressure. Do you have the strategy and steady hands to rise above the competition? Step up, beat the clock, and claim the title of Tower of Torque champion! Competition Format Participation: Individual Duration: 1–2 minutes per participant Building Time: 60 seconds Materials Provided: 20 cups per participant Winning Criteria: Greatest height achieved by a valid, freestanding tower Rules and Regulations Each participant will receive exactly 20 cups. Participants must build their tower within the allotted 60 seconds. No tape, glue, strings, or any other external support or fastening material is permitted. The tower must stand independently for at least five seconds after the timer ends. The non-dominant-hand challenge will be introduced in the final stage, as instructed by the event coordinators. Participants may not use their body, clothing, furniture, or other objects to support the tower. Only towers completed within the time limit and satisfying all stability requirements will be considered valid. The organizers' decision regarding measurement, validity, and final results will be binding. Judging Criteria Primary criterion: Maximum height of the valid tower. Stability: The tower must remain standing unsupported for five seconds. Fair play: All participants must follow the same material, time, and construction restrictions. Winner Selection The participant who constructs the tallest valid freestanding tower wins. In case of a tie, the organizers may conduct a sudden-death tiebreaker using the same materials and time limit. What to Expect Get ready for a fast-paced challenge involving spatial reasoning, structural balance, quick decision-making, and hand-eye coordination. Every second counts, every cup matters, and one wrong move can bring your entire tower crashing down!

details_text: Bug Squash is a fast-paced debugging competition where participants must identify and fix bugs in given code snippets within a tight time frame. title: Xplore & Nova Exilaro Article Writing Competition
description: Overview When the Algorithm Makes the Call: Who Owns the Decision? In a world where algorithms increasingly influence business decisions, from hiring and pricing to lending and supply chain management, an important…
details_text: Overview When the Algorithm Makes the Call: Who Owns the Decision? In a world where algorithms increasingly influence business decisions, from hiring and pricing to lending and supply chain management, an important question emerges: When an algorithm makes the call, who takes responsibility for the outcome? NovaExilaro and Xplore, XLRI, invite students across India to participate in an individual article writing competition exploring the intersection of technology, management, leadership, and accountability. As organisations rely increasingly on data-driven recommendations, the role of human judgement is evolving. Managers may still make the final call, but how much ownership do they truly exercise when decisions are shaped by systems they cannot fully question? We invite you to go beyond conventional discussions on artificial intelligence and automation. Develop a distinctive perspective, challenge existing assumptions, and present a well-researched argument on where accountability should lie in an algorithm-driven business environment. Why Participate? Get Published: The winning article will be featured in Xplore Magazine in both digital and print formats. Reach Industry Leaders: Xplore reaches 50+ CXOs per edition and has a cumulative LinkedIn audience of approximately 4 million impressions. Showcase Your Thinking: Present your ideas and insights to an audience of industry leaders, academicians, and management professionals. Get Recognised: Best contributions will receive a cash prize of INR [Amount] and an e-certificate. Who Can Participate? The competition is open to all students currently enrolled in a recognised undergraduate or postgraduate programme in India. Participation is individual, and each participant may submit one article. Submission Guidelines Word Limit: 500–800 words (excluding title, summary line, author details, and references). Format: Microsoft Word (.docx) only. Font: Times New Roman, 12 pt, with 1.5 line spacing. Page Setup: A4 size with 1-inch margins. References: Minimum 3 credible sources, using APA 7 or Harvard referencing style. Originality: Articles must be original, unpublished, and primarily written by the participant. Your article should feature a compelling opening, a clearly developed argument supported by evidence, a counter-perspective, and a conclusion that presents a definite point of view. Important: AI tools may be used for research and language checking but must not be used to write the article. An AI-use disclosure is mandatory. Entries with a similarity score above 20% (excluding references and quoted text) may be disqualified. Judging Criteria Originality and Insight – 30% Argument and Evidence – 25% Relevance to the Theme – 20% Structure and Clarity – 15% Style and Readability – 10% How to Participate Register for the competition through this Unstop page. Develop your article in accordance with the theme brief and submission guidelines. Save your submission as FullName_CollegeName.docx . Upload your article on Unstop before the submission deadline. Don't just describe how algorithms are changing the world. Question who is accountable when they make the decisions. Bring your perspective, make your argument, and let your ideas reach beyond the classroom!

details_text: Overview: Campus Placement Aptitude Challenge 1 is a free, online, individual challenge by CampusFirst India. It has 40 questions on quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, verbal ability and data interpretation, the kind of questions asked in the online aptitude round of campus placements at TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Accenture, Capgemini, Deloitte and other mass recruiters. Please register here: https://www.campusfirstindia.com/compete The competition will take place on our website. How it works: Competition Date: Saturday, 7 November 2026 Start any time between 7:00 and 9:00 PM IST. Everyone gets the full 60 minutes, whenever they start. 40 questions, 60 minutes, one attempt per participant Scoring: each correct answer scores 500 to 1,000 points. The faster you answer correctly, the more points you get. Results at 10:00 PM IST: your score, an all-India leaderboard, and worked solutions for every question What’s covered: Quantitative aptitude: percentages, profit and loss, ratio and proportion, averages, time and work, speed and distance, simple and compound interest, number systems Logical reasoning: series, coding–decoding, blood relations, directions, seating arrangement, syllogisms, puzzles Verbal ability: reading comprehension, sentence correction, error spotting, synonyms and antonyms, para jumbles, fill in the blanks Data interpretation: tables, bar and line graphs, pie charts, caselets Fair for everyone: One attempt each, enforced by our servers Your time is measured on our side, not on your phone Ties on points are broken by number of correct answers, then by total time taken Recognition: The top 10 receive a certificate of merit Who should take part: Final-year and pre-final-year students preparing for campus placements Engineering, BCom, BBA, BCA, BSc and MBA students who want to test their aptitude fundamentals Anyone preparing for the aptitude rounds of off-campus drives and mass-recruiter hiring tests Anyone who wants to check their readiness under real time limits How to take part: Register for Campus Placement Aptitude Challenge #1. You’ll get a confirmation email with a calendar invite, and a reminder 30 minutes before the challenge opens. On Saturday 31 October, sign in and start the challenge any time between 7:00 and 9:00 PM IST. You get the full 45 minutes from when you start. Come back at 10:00 PM IST for your score, the leaderboard and worked solutions. Rules: One account and one attempt per person; multiple accounts lead to disqualification Challenge decisions by CampusFirst India are final Aged 17? Sign up early. A parent or guardian must confirm by email before you can register.

description: About DOOMFORGE DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering. The competition is designed to…
details_text: About DOOMFORGE DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering. The competition is designed to take participants beyond conventional coding challenges. It begins with identifying real-world business problems and market opportunities, followed by hands-on engineering challenges involving existing codebases and open-source development. Participants will have the opportunity to demonstrate their analytical thinking, technical expertise, creativity, and ability to build practical solutions. Eligibility and Team Formation Open to college students. Team size: 1 - 3 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specialisations are welcome to collaborate. Each participant can be part of only one team. All team members must complete the registration process. Competition Structure Round 1: Market Analysis Duration: 4 December – 6 December 2026 Round 1 focuses on business strategy, market research, and problem identification. Participants will be presented with a business-oriented problem or scenario. They must analyse the problem, understand the market landscape, identify opportunities, and propose a feasible solution. What participants need to cover: Problem identification and understanding. Target audience and market analysis. Competitor research and existing solutions. Identification of market gaps and opportunities. Proposed solution, its feasibility, and potential impact. Submission Format: Teams must submit a one-minute video explaining their market analysis, identified opportunity, and proposed solution through Unstop. Evaluation Criteria: Depth of market research. Understanding of the problem. Originality and innovation. Feasibility of the proposed solution. Clarity and effectiveness of presentation. Based on their submissions, selected teams will qualify for the second round. Round 2: Engineering Arena – Open-Source Development The second round is a hands-on engineering challenge in which shortlisted teams will work on one of four dedicated GitHub repositories. Each repository represents a distinct engineering track with its own technical problem space. Participants will be expected to understand the existing codebase, identify areas for improvement, and implement meaningful technical contributions. Potential engineering challenges include: Developing new features and functionalities. Identifying and fixing bugs. Improving application performance and scalability. Implementing security enhancements. Writing automated tests and improving test coverage. Integrating AI/ML-based capabilities. Improving code quality, maintainability, and documentation. Submission Format: All development contributions must be submitted through GitHub Pull Requests (PRs) to the respective repositories. Evaluation Criteria: Functional correctness and completeness. Code quality and maintainability. Technical implementation. Security and reliability. Testing and validation. Innovation and practical impact. Engineering Tracks DOOMFORGE features four specialised engineering tracks, each backed by a dedicated GitHub repository. Participants will work on the repository and technical challenge specified by the organising team. Further details regarding the repositories, technical requirements, and challenges will be communicated to qualified participants. Rules and Regulations Teams must consist of a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 members. Inter-college participation is permitted. Each participant may register as part of only one team. Round 1 submissions must be submitted within the specified deadline, from 4 December to 6 December 2026. Round 1 submissions must follow the prescribed one-minute video format. details_text: Overview: Date: 14th & 15th Nov, 2026 Registrations: Now Open Kickoff Session: 14th Nov (Saturday), 2026 This is a hands-on, build-first hackathon created for individuals who want to launch a real AI product , not just present ideas or mockups. details_text: Innovate. Build. Disrupt.: SINGULARITY is a premier inter-college hybrid hackathon organized by BLITZ, the Computer Science Society of Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University of Delhi. Built for visionary thinkers, coders, and creators, this challenge invites students from colleges across India to collaborate, build, and pitch disruptive, real-world solutions across cutting-edge technology sectors. Registration Fee: 100 Rupee per member of the team For Payment check the SINGULARITY RULEBOOK, fill out the Google Form attached at the end of the ruleboook . Round 1: Online Evaluation: Teams must formulate their ideas and submit a conceptual presentation (PPT) detailing their proposed solution and implementation framework. A specialized faculty panel will evaluate the submissions and shortlist the most promising teams for the grand finale. Round 2: Grand Finale — On-Site Hackathon: The top 10 shortlisted teams will earn their spot in the Reading Room at Keshav Mahavidyalaya for an intense, single-day, in-person hacking and pitching experience. Teams will work on their solutions, demonstrate their innovations, and present their projects to the judging panel. Bring your laptops, choose your track, and prepare to design the technology of tomorrow! Themes & Focus Areas: Select one of the following seven tracks for your project: Cybersecurity: Protecting networks, ensuring data integrity, and securing digital infrastructure. FinTech: Engineering disruptive digital banking, payment solutions, and wealth-tech platforms. Healthcare: Empowering medicine, diagnostics, and patient care through technology. Robotics, IoT & Automation: Designing smart hardware, connected devices, and intelligent automated workflows. Web3: Building decentralized architectures, smart contracts, and blockchain-powered innovations. AR/VR & Immersive Experiences: Architecting virtual spaces and developing next-generation spatial computing interfaces. Open Innovation: Bring your own unique problem statement and develop a creative, technology-driven solution. Important Timelines: Registration Opens: 2 November 2026 Registration & PPT Submission Deadline: 10 November 2026 Round 1 Results: 13 November 2026 Final Offline Hackathon: 17 November 2026 | 9:00 AM – 5:30 PM Important: Ensure that your team completes registration and submits its PPT before the deadline to be considered for the first round. Prizes & Rewards: First Place: ₹5,000 Cash Prize + Goodies Second Place: ₹3,000 Cash Prize + Goodies Third Place: ₹2,000 Cash Prize + Goodies Perks For All Participants: All participants can look forward to event-branded goodies during the offline phase. Ready To Make Your Mark?: Bring your ideas to life, collaborate with brilliant minds, and compete to create solutions that matter. SINGULARITY 2026 — Where Ideas Converge and Innovation Begins. Organized By BLITZ | Computer Science Society | Keshav Mahavidyalaya, University Of Delhi

details_text: QueryQuest is a technical competition organised by HackerRank Campus Crew, NIE Mysuru , designed to test participants' SQL knowledge, database concepts and problem-solving abilities. The challenge provides an opportunity for students to demonstrate their understanding of SQL through practical coding problems and multiple-choice questions across different difficulty levels. Competition Format The competition will consist of 10 questions to be completed within a total time limit of 100 minutes . The question distribution will be: SQL Basic – 4 Questions SQL Intermediate – 3 Questions SQL Advanced – 1 Question SQL Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) – 2 Questions Rules and Guidelines The competition will be conducted online through the HackerRank platform. Participants must complete all questions within the allotted 100 minutes. Participants must use their own HackerRank accounts to access the challenge. All submitted SQL solutions must satisfy the given problem requirements and test cases. Participants must not share solutions, collaborate with other participants or engage in any unfair practices during the competition. The use of external assistance or AI tools during the competition is not permitted. Participants must ensure a stable internet connection throughout the challenge. Tie-breaker: If two or more participants achieve the same score, the participant who completes the assessment in the shortest time will be ranked higher. For example, if two participants achieve the same score, but Participant 1 finishes at 10:00 AM and Participant 2 finishes at 11:00 AM, Participant 1 will be ranked higher. The organisers' decision regarding the results and rewards will be final. Eligibility Open to college students interested in SQL, databases and problem-solving. Participants from all engineering branches and academic years are welcome. Basic knowledge of SQL is recommended. Rewards and Recognition Winner HackerRank Infinity Plan AI Tool Credits HackerRank Mock Interview Credits Certificate of Achievement Runner-up AI Tool Credits HackerRank Mock Interview Credits Certificate of Achievement All Participants HackerRank Mock Interview Credits Participation Certificate Evaluation Process Participants will be evaluated based on the correctness of their submitted solutions and their performance in the competition. The final rankings will be determined based on the competition results.

details_text: All You Need to Know About AGENTIC X 2.0 – AI & Robotics Hackathon | Future Tech Summit ’26 AGENTIC X 2.0 is an AI & Robotics Hackathon held as part of Future Tech Summit ’26, organized by the AI Research Centre (AIRC), Woxsen University, in collaboration with Gentricks and TruScholar. Track 2 – Hardware: Robotics & Autonomous Systems Theme: Intelligent Machines for the Physical World Problem Statement: Intelligent Autonomous Machines for Real-World Physical Challenges Participants can explore robotics, autonomous systems, embedded AI, sensors, computer vision, the Internet of Things (IoT), control systems, and intelligent machines. A working prototype is not mandatory in Round 1, but if you have one, include photos, a short demo video link, or test results. Submissions must be original work by the team. Submissions will be evaluated based on: Innovation and originality Problem relevance Feasibility and technical approach Potential impact Quality of the proposed solution Shortlisted teams will qualify for Round 2. Round 2 – Final Build & Demo Shortlisted teams will advance to the in-person final round at Woxsen University, Hyderabad. Participants will develop or refine their solutions and present their final build or demonstration to the judges. The full Round 2 schedule and participation details will be shared directly with shortlisted teams. Hardware teams should bring their prototype and components. If you need power, workspace, or internet support for your demo, inform the organizers in advance after shortlisting. Internship Opportunities Internship Opportunities for Hackathon Winners! Winning teams will be considered for internship opportunities with startups and AI research centres, providing a chance to gain practical experience, showcase their technical skills, and explore opportunities within the startup ecosystem. Exclusive Benefit for Hackathon Participants Free Access to All Technical Talks at Future Tech Summit ’26! Participants who register for AGENTIC X 2.0 will receive free access to all technical talks at Future Tech Summit ’26, giving them the opportunity to learn from industry experts and explore emerging technologies. This benefit covers technical talks only. Eligibility The hackathon welcomes students, freshers, professionals, and technology enthusiasts interested in AI, robotics, and emerging technologies. Team size: 1–4 members per team (a team leader plus up to 3 members). Relevant fields include: Computer Science and Engineering Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Data Science Electronics and Communication Engineering Robotics and Autonomous Systems Other engineering and technology-related disciplines Event Details Hackathon: AGENTIC X 2.0 – AI & Robotics Hackathon Hackathon Date
