details_text: About GOA BUILDATHON ’27: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is a 36-hour offline hackathon planned for January 2027 in Goa, India. It aims to bring together developers, designers, AI enthusiasts, problem-solvers and innovators from colleges and communities to turn ideas into working solutions. This is where ideas move beyond discussions and become prototypes. Whether you're exploring AI agents, developing web applications, automating everyday workflows or experimenting with emerging technologies, GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is designed to give you the space to build, collaborate and challenge yourself. Our vision is to create an environment where students can experiment with new technologies, solve meaningful problems, learn from experienced builders and connect with people who share the same passion for creating. Not just another hackathon. A place to turn ideas into reality. What To Expect: 36 hours of offline building in Goa Collaboration with developers, designers and innovators Hands-on experimentation with AI, AI agents and automation Web development, software engineering and emerging technology Teamwork, rapid prototyping and practical problem-solving Opportunities to connect with mentors, judges and technology communities Project showcases and opportunities to present your ideas Community partnerships and potential sponsor-led challenges An environment focused on learning, creativity and building real solutions Who Can Participate?: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 welcomes students, aspiring developers, designers, AI builders and technology enthusiasts who want to learn by building. Whether you're an experienced hackathon participant or attending your first hackathon, the focus is on curiosity, collaboration and the willingness to create something meaningful. Bring your skills, find teammates, explore unfamiliar technologies and turn your ideas into something people can experience. What Can You Build?: We encourage projects across a range of technology areas, including: Artificial Intelligence & AI Agents: Build intelligent assistants, agentic workflows and practical AI-powered applications. Web Development: Create websites, platforms and full-stack applications that address real problems. Automation: Develop tools that reduce repetitive work and improve everyday processes. Data Science & Analytics: Turn data into insights, useful tools and better decisions. Software & Developer Tools: Build products that improve workflows, productivity and collaboration. Electronics & Emerging Technology: Explore innovative solutions that connect software with the physical world. The goal is not simply to present an idea, but to make meaningful progress towards a working solution within the hackathon. Why Goa?: Goa offers a distinctive setting for bringing people together to learn, collaborate and create. GOA BUILDATHON ’27 aims to combine the energy of a technology-building event with a community-driven experience where new connections and ideas can grow. We want participants to leave with more than a project: new skills, valuable connections, practical experience and the confidence to keep building. Event Details: Event: GOA BUILDATHON ’27 Format: 36-hour offline hackathon Location: Goa, India Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/goabuildathon27/ Website: https://goabuilds.com/ Contact: hello@goabuilds.com The event dates, venue, registration details, prize pool and other final arrangements will be announced through official channels once confirmed. Be Part Of The Build: We're bringing together people who don't just want to talk about ideas — they want to build them. If you have an idea worth exploring, a problem worth solving or simply the curiosity to create something new, GOA BUILDATHON ’27 is your opportunity to get started. Build > Collaborate > Create real impact Let's build something that matters.

details_text: MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon About the Opportunity MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking. This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas. Eligibility Criteria Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship. Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome. Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed). Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged). No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills. Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions. Team Formation Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members. Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists. Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes. Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact. Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers. Competition Format and Rounds Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes) Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge. Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes) Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies. Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team) Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently. Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team) Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally. Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling. Problem Statements Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas: Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem. Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan. Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model. Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution. details_text: Overview: ELUCode is a fast-paced 2-hour competitive coding contest by EduLinkUp designed to challenge your problem-solving ability, algorithmic thinking, and coding speed. The contest brings together students and developers from across the community to compete on a set of carefully curated problems ranging from logical puzzles to algorithmic challenges. Top performers will be recognised through special achievement badges and certificates within the EduLinkUp ecosystem. Scoring: Each challenge carries a predefined score, based on its difficulty level. A participant’s score for a challenge depends on the number of test cases successfully passed by their submission. Submissions are automatically evaluated against hidden and visible test cases to ensure correctness and efficiency. The overall leaderboard is determined by the total score obtained across all challenges. If two or more participants achieve the same score, the tie will be broken based on the sum of time of the first correct solution for all the problems. The participant who reaches the score earlier will rank higher.

details_text: About: An engaging mix of algorithmic strategy, autonomous decision-making, and competitive resource management, this event puts participants in command of programmable rover fleets competing for dominance on an unpredictable battlefield. Participants must design intelligent controllers to explore unfamiliar terrain, gather resources, defend their territory, and outmanoeuvre rival teams. With mechanics ranging from hidden hazards and tactical combat to resource-driven upgrades and enemy vault raids, every decision can shift the balance of the game. The event tests participants' programming skills, strategic thinking, adaptability, and ability to make optimal decisions under uncertainty. The event will unfold in two stages . Prelims (Online): Format: Submission-based programming round hosted on Unstop. Description: Participants develop and submit autonomous rover controllers to compete in a head-to-head, turn-based strategy game. The round challenges participants to explore a simulated environment, gather resources, and outmanoeuvre their opponents through intelligent decision-making. Algorithmic thinking, tactical planning, and efficient resource management are key to advancing. Finals (Offline): Format: On-site interactive competition conducted at IIT Madras. Description: Shortlisted participants compete in a live, turn-based rover strategy game featuring a free-for-all format. Participants must program their rovers to explore the map, mine resources, raid enemy vaults, engage in combat, and manage upgrades to maximise their score. The finals also introduce a dynamic in-game market, adding an economic dimension where participants must make strategic decisions about resource allocation, purchases, and upgrades. Adaptability, tactical thinking, and intelligent resource management will be crucial to securing victory. Date: To be held during Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras. The event follows a team-based format, with 2–3 participants per team, encouraging collaboration in algorithm design, strategic planning, and resource management. Participants must combine their analytical abilities and technical skills to develop competitive rover controllers and devise effective strategies.

title: Boeing Aeromodelling Competition
description: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs.…
details_text: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs. The abstract should cover the aircraft design, including dimensions, wing area, estimated flight speed, reservoir and mounting, release mechanism, leakage prevention, centre-of-gravity management, and safe operation. The prescribed format must be downloaded from the respective IIT website and submitted by email at least 20 days before the competition. Shortlisted teams will be announced 15 days before the competition. If multiple teams participate from the same institution, their aircraft designs must be distinct, with at least a 2.5% difference in wingspan, chord, and fuselage length; otherwise, the teams will be disqualified. Qualifier Round The Qualifier Round aims to select the top 30 teams with lightweight aircraft capable of safe, controlled flight carrying a 1,000 mL water payload. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds with the full payload, with no water release required. The water must be stored in a sealed, securely mounted, removable reservoir, with the reservoir and release mechanism included in the aircraft’s empty weight. Judges will inspect the system before takeoff, and there must be no visible leakage. Each attempt must be completed within 3 minutes. Failure to maintain 30 seconds of safe flight or any visible leakage before landing results in a zero score. Each team gets two attempts, with the higher score counted, and only teams that safely complete the loaded flight can advance. The top 30 teams qualify for the Main Round and receive ₹5,000 towards material costs, subject to providing the bank details of one designated team member. Main Round In the Main Round, the aircraft must carry 1,000 mL of water in an inspected, sealed, removable reservoir and release it while flying over the designated simulated fire/release zone. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds before release, which must be manually triggered by the pilot using a single transmitter channel; automatic or programmed release is not allowed. Judges will verify that the release begins within the marked zone, which is approximately 40 m from the take-off/landing area, though its location and dimensions may be adjusted based on venue and wind conditions. The amount of water released will be determined by weighing the reservoir before and after the attempt; if leakage before the commanded release cannot be distinguished from the actual release, the attempt scores zero. Each team gets two attempts, with the better score counted, and each attempt must complete the release and landing within 3 minutes. Rules and Regulations The same aircraft must be used throughout all rounds and must match the submitted design; repairs are allowed, but replacement aircraft are not. Teams should carry spare components and be ready when called, or risk losing their attempt or flight time. details_text: One Who Codes 2026 — Online Portfolio Challenge You already built it. Now show the internet you're one who codes. One Who Codes 2026 is an online portfolio challenge for developers who bring their personality, creativity, and craftsmanship to the web. Put your best portfolio on a free ONEWHO address, submit your application link through Unstop, and compete for a total prize pool of ₹30,000. ONEWHO connects a memorable address, such as yourname.isonewho.codes, to the portfolio you have already deployed. Your website stays on its existing hosting platform. Participation and claiming a ONEWHO name are free. The challenge is conducted entirely online. Submit a personal portfolio website that represents your own work. How to Participate 1. Deploy Your Portfolio Build your portfolio using your preferred technologies and deploy it on a supported platform: Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Railway, Render, or Fly. 2. Claim Your ONEWHO Name Visit https://isonewho.codes/ , sign in with GitHub, choose your name, and connect your deployed portfolio URL. Your portfolio will be accessible through an address such as: yourname.isonewho.codes 3. Create Your Competition Entry Link Open the Applications section in your ONEWHO dashboard and add an application with the company name “Unstop.” This creates your submission link: https://yourname.isonewho.codes/a/unstop The application link lets you view recorded judging visits and tracked page activity in your ONEWHO dashboard. 4. Submit Through Unstop Complete your registration and submit both of the following before the deadline: Your ONEWHO application link ending in /a/unstop . The public GitHub source repository for your portfolio. Creating a ONEWHO name alone does not complete your competition entry. Your submission must also be completed on Unstop. Judging Criteria Creativity — 30%: Original ideas, personal identity, and thoughtful customization. Craft — 30%: Layout, typography, motion, visual consistency, and attention to detail. Content — 20%: How clearly your portfolio communicates who you are, what you build, and the work you have done. Performance and Accessibility — 20%: Loading experience, mobile usability, and accessibility. Rules and Guidelines Each participant may submit only one entry. ONEWHO permits one name per GitHub account. The portfolio must represent your own work. Include its public source repository, with development history associated with your GitHub account. Templates and AI tools are permitted. Judging rewards your original contribution; changing only the name on a template will not score well on creativity. You must deploy the portfolio yourself on a supported hosting platform. Portfolios automatically generated by ONEWHO from a GitHub profile are not eligible. Submit the required ONEWHO application link and public source repository through Unstop before the deadline. You may improve your portfolio until submissions close. After the deadline, leave the submitted website unchanged until results are announced. Keep your ONEWHO address connected to your portfolio and publicly accessible throughout judging and until results are announced. All entries must comply with ONEWHO’s acceptable use policy: https://isonewho.codes/acceptable-use . Entries that violate the rules or acceptable use policy may be disqualified. The judges’ decisions are final. Their task is to analyse the code, identify the problems, implement the required fixes, and make the application work correctly. Rules The starter codebase and problem statement will be provided by the organisers at the beginning of the challenge. title: Pixels To Prognosis
description: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different…
details_text: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently. Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema. The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data. Who Can Participate Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science Teams of 1 to 3 members . Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening) This is a case-based quiz on: How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds. Round 2: Model Submission Round Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide, [derived from the BraTS 2021 challenge]. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR. Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set . Rules: Train only on the dataset provided. No external data. All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation . Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants. The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less . Submission requirements: Complete source code (.py / .ipynb) Final trained weights (.pt / .keras) Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv) A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used Evaluation: Segmentation quality is measured with the Dice score and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance for each tumour region. Scoring also covers anatomical consistency, false-positive control, and the quality of your technical report. Finals: Offline Round at IIT Madras Finalists come to campus and receive a new set of MRI scans with real-world problems. These can include motion artefacts, missing modalities, or pathologies your model has never seen. Each team must: Work out what is wrong with the data and why it happened Adapt the model through preprocessing, retraining or other corrective strategies Present the problems they found, the medical reasoning behind them, and how they handled them Evaluation criteria: Problem identification and medical reasoning Model adaptation strategy and outcome Clarity of presentation and understanding Knowing when your model should not be trusted counts in your favour. Flagging an unreliable case for expert review is part of good clinical AI. Prizes & Recognition Cash prizes for the top 3 teams [prize pool: ₹35000] Special Awards for Best Robust Model and Best Diagnostic Reasoning Certificates of Merit for the winners(Hard Copy) Certificates of Merit for all finalists(Soft Copy) Certificates of Participation for all Round 2 participants Important Dates Registration closes: 28th December, 2026 Round 1 (Online Quiz): 5th December, 2026 Round 2 submission window: 9th - 16th December, 2026 Finals at IIT Madras: 4th January, 2027

title: NeuroHack
description: Overview Neurohack is a two-round computational neuroscience hackathon hosted under BIOGEN at SHAASTRA 2027, IIT Madras. Participants will work with real EEG datasets to build pipelines that classify human emotions from…
details_text: Overview Neurohack is a two-round computational neuroscience hackathon hosted under BIOGEN at SHAASTRA 2027, IIT Madras. Participants will work with real EEG datasets to build pipelines that classify human emotions from brainwave signals, combining signal processing, machine learning, and neuroscience in one challenge. Eligibility Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students. Teams of 1–4 members. Participants may be from any discipline and any institute; no prior EEG experience is required, but working knowledge of Python is expected. Target Audience Students interested in: Biotechnology & biomedical engineering Neuroscience and cognitive science Computer science, data science and machine learning Signal processing and electronics Competition Rounds Round 1: Online Quiz An online quiz covering basic neuroscience, EEG principles, brain-wave patterns, and Python for data analysis. Top-scoring teams advance to Round 2. Round 2: 24-Hour Offline Hackathon Selected teams are invited to IIT Madras during SHAASTRA 2027 for a 24-hour hackathon . Participants receive a preprocessed subset of a public EEG emotion dataset and build a complete pipeline to classify human emotions using signal processing and machine learning. Finals at IIT Madras: PPT Presentation Each team presents its problem approach, features, model, results, and insights from the brain signals to a panel of judges, followed by a Q&A session.

title: Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge
description: Competition Overview : The Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge (SARC) is an exciting drone competition that brings together aspiring engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and innovators to test their drone-building skills,…
details_text: Competition Overview : The Shaastra Aerial Robotics Challenge (SARC) is an exciting drone competition that brings together aspiring engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and innovators to test their drone-building skills, flying precision, and technical knowledge. Participants will navigate challenging obstacle courses, perform precise aerial manoeuvres, and compete in time-based challenges that test their control, stability, accuracy, and problem-solving abilities Competition Rounds: Round 0: Preliminary Submission: Teams must submit a flight demonstration video and a technical PDF for initial evaluation. The video must demonstrate: Smooth take-off and stable hovering. Stable flight while carrying a 50 g payload. Navigation through at least one hoop-shaped obstacle without contact. A precise 90° turn. Safe landing at the designated point. The technical PDF must include drone dimensions, total weight, power source specifications, manual control system details, safety mechanisms, and other relevant technical information. Selected teams will advance to Round 1. Round 1: Obstacle Course Challenge Qualified teams must navigate a specially designed obstacle course while maintaining stable, low-altitude flight. The course includes: Semicircular and quarter hoops. Diagonal split rectangular hoops. Sharp 90° turns. Double quarter hoops. Crossover and split semicircular hoops. Triangular and freely hanging circular hoops. T-rod obstacles. Teams must complete the obstacle sequence, cross the finish line, and land at the designated point. Scoring is based on course completion, time bonuses, and penalties for rule violations. Round 2: Checkpoints Challenge The top-performing teams from Round 1 will qualify for this timed challenge. Reach as many checkpoints as possible within the allotted time. Follow the obstacle-course rules applicable to Round 1. Earn 10 points for each successful checkpoint. Avoid unnecessary contacts and unsafe manoeuvres. The number of qualifying teams will be determined by the organisers based on participation. Round 3: Payload Delivery Challenge Teams will carry an organiser-provided payload through the obstacle course and release it onto a marked target area. Scoring would consider course completion, delivery accuracy, time bonuses, and penalties. Rules and Regulations: Drone type: Only multirotor drones, such as quadcopters and hexacopters, are permitted. Control system: Drones must be operated manually using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted.3. Dimensions: The drone must not exceed 1 metre and must not be smaller than 0.3 metre in any direction. Flight altitude: Drones must not exceed a height of 1.5 metres and must follow the prescribed arena boundaries and safety-net restrictions. Flight performance: Drones must demonstrate stable hovering, precise low-altitude flight, and controlled manoeuvrability. Obstacle contact: Contact with hoops, rods, will attract penalties. Ground contact: Touching the ground during the course will attract penalties. Arena boundaries: Exiting the arena boundaries may result in disqualification. Unsafe contacts: Exceeding the permitted number of unsafe contacts may result in disqualification. Drone crashes: A crash that prevents continuation may result in disqualification. FPV camera: An FPV camera is optional and is not mandatory. Arena Specifications: Arena dimensions: 8 m × 11 m × 1.25 m. Clearly marked start and finish points will be provided. Obstacle dimensions and placements will have a tolerance of ±5%. Eligibility: Students, robotics enthusiasts, and teams interested in drone technology, aerial robotics, and engineering innovation are encouraged to participate, subject to the final eligibility criteria announced by the organisers. Participants must ensure that their drones comply with the technical specifications and safety requirements. title: Bazaar: Beat the Markets
description: All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar…
details_text: All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar is where you find out which one you are. Organized by the Entrepreneurship & Incubation Cell (EIC) as part of E-Summit, Bazaar is a live stock market trading competition for students. Fictional companies, simulated markets, virtual capital. The pressure is real. What Makes Bazaar Different? Forget static prediction games and paper quizzes. Bazaar runs on a trading platform built specifically for this event, with live prices, breaking news and timed sessions where every decision counts. You don't just trade one market, you trade two. First you play as a retail investor, reading charts and reacting to news. Then you step up to the institutional level, where your own orders move prices, bots trade alongside you, and the market pushes back. News reaches you from many sources: newspapers, analysts, insiders and finfluencers. Not all of them deserve your trust, and knowing which to believe is half the game. The Grand Finale is held at E-Summit, so you compete in the same venue as founders, investors and innovators. Who Should Apply? Bazaar is for anyone who follows the markets, enjoys fast decisions, data or strategy, and wants to experience trading without risking real money. You don't need prior trading experience. Beginners can learn from the rulebook and strategy hints shared before the Finale, and experienced traders will find plenty to exploit. Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across India. Cross-college teams are welcome. Competition Structure Bazaar runs across two rounds. Round 1 is an Online Quiz on Unstop, covering stock market basics, financial instruments, chart and news reading, and risk-based reasoning. Round 2 is the Grand Finale, held in person at PEC, Chandigarh on 14-15 November as part of E-Summit. Finalists trade on Bazaar's live platform across two stages: Stage 1: Retail. Start with virtual capital. Trade across a range of instruments using technical tools. Trading happens in timed sessions that get tougher as new instruments and news unlock. Stage 2: Institutional. Start fresh with new virtual capital. Now your trades move prices, and bots compete with you for liquidity. Every trade carries a transaction fee, so overtrading will cost you. Teams are ranked on trading performance. General scoring guidelines and a rulebook will be shared with registered teams before the Finale. Team Details Team Size: 2 to 4 members Cross-college and cross-city teams: Fully allowed and encouraged Solo registrations: Not accepted One person registers as Team Leader and adds the remaining members on Unstop Join the WhatsApp Group here.

details_text: Overview Ready to drive the strategic roadmap of an industry giant? Strategy Sprint is the ultimate business case challenge where you step into the role of a C-suite corporate strategist to solve real-world industry transformation puzzles ! Guidelines: Solve High-Stakes Business Case Studies: Analyze major industry shifts, market entry opportunities, and strategic inflection points facing market leaders . Evaluate Strategic Expansion: Weigh key corporate growth decisions like Build, Buy, or Partner —analyzing potential mergers, acquisitions, strategic alliances, or supply chain backward integration . Conduct Deep Financial & Synergies Analysis: Perform cost-benefit evaluations, model expected ROI, assess margin improvements, and justify capital allocations with data-driven financial rigor . Assess Risks & Regulatory Landscape: Map out market risks, technological obsolescence, supply chain vulnerabilities, and policy incentives (like government PLI schemes) . Integrate ESG & Sustainability: Align growth strategies with Net Zero commitments, environmental impact reduction, and long-term ESG performance . Deliver an Actionable Executive Plan: Package your strategic recommendations, 3–5 year implementation roadmap, and quantitative backing into an executive pitch deck ! Platform will be unstop and offline event at IIT Kanpur.

description: This two-round competition challenges participants to build a stock portfolio based on financial analysis and subsequently develop a machine learning model to predict the future prices of those selected stocks.
eligibility: UG and PG college students; teams of up to 5 members.
requirements: Team formation, portfolio construction with financial justification, and machine learning model development.
details_text: Event Structure: Online Round: Portfolio Building & Analysis: All registered teams will receive details of 20 virtual stocks, including their technical and fundamental analysis. Participants must study the stocks and create a portfolio of 8 stocks using a virtual fund of ₹20 lakh. Teams must present a rationale for their selection, supported by financial statements, news articles, or relevant market data. Bonus Challenge: Justify why the remaining 12 stocks were excluded from your portfolio. ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors may be incorporated into the portfolio for additional evaluation. Portfolios will be assessed based on stock performance two years into the future, assuming the investments were made in the current year. Offline Round: Machine Learning-Based Stock Price Prediction: Teams will create a Machine Learning model to predict stock prices for each of the 8 selected stocks in their portfolio. A time series model can be used to forecast future price movements. Historical stock data (till Dec 2024) will be provided for training the model. The model will be evaluated on stock prices from 2025-2026. The team with the best-performing model will win the competition. A bonus round will be held, with further details provided on campus. Guidelines: Team Composition & Registration: Each team can have up to 5 members (both UG and PG students are eligible). A participant cannot be part of multiple teams in the same event. Multiple teams from the same college are allowed to participate. Competition & Evaluation: Only college students will be considered when deciding the winners. Teams must justify their portfolio selections with supporting financial data. Machine Learning models will be tested on real stock data from 2025-2026. Rules & Fair Play: The decision of the judges is final and incontestable. The organizers reserve the right to modify the timeline if necessary.

details_text: About Capture The Flag (CTF): A Capture The Flag (CTF) competition is a cybersecurity-based contest where participants solve a variety of real-world hacking challenges to ﬁnd hidden clues called ﬂags. These ﬂags act as proof of solving a challenge and are submitted on a CTF platform to earn points. Each challenge represents a practical security scenario, encouraging participants to think like ethical hackers while maintaining legal and responsible boundaries. The aim is not just to break systems but to understand, analyze, and defend them that promote both offensive and defensive cybersecurity skills. About the Event: The Capture the Flag (CTF) competition hosted by Tech Society IIIT Bhubaneswar is a cybersecurity challenge designed to test your hacking, analytical, and problem-solving skills in a real-world simulation environment. In this event, participants will face a series of challenges related to ethical hacking domains that include web exploitation, cryptography, forensics, reverse engineering, OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence), steganography, and privilege escalation. Each challenge will test different aspects of cybersecurity knowledge and technical expertise. The event is meant to promote cybersecurity awareness, encourage ethical hacking practices, and create a platform for collaboration among students passionate about security. This event will be conducted offline at IIIT Bhubaneswar, giving participants a chance to interact with cybersecurity enthusiasts, mentors, and experts from different colleges.

details_text: Overview: Techkriti’27, IIT Kanpur, presents Capture the Flag (CTF) — a cybersecurity competition where participants solve practical security challenges in a simulated real-world environment. Identify vulnerabilities, apply technical problem-solving skills, and capture hidden flags to score points. The competition will challenge participants across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and vulnerability exploitation , requiring them to choose the right tools and techniques to solve increasingly challenging problems. Guidelines: Team Composition: Participants can compete individually or in teams of up to 2 members. The contest is team-rated, and participants forming a team must register accordingly. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate students, postgraduate students, and professionals worldwide. Only participants who are currently enrolled as university students will be eligible for prizes. Registration & Prize Eligibility: To claim prize money, participants must register on both the competition platform and the Techkriti website. Fair Play & Disqualification: Any form of malpractice or plagiarism will result in immediate disqualification. Participants must follow all competition guidelines. In case of any dispute, the decision of the Techkriti Team, IIT Kanpur, will be final. Rules & Event Structure: Competition Format: The competition will consist of a single round featuring numerous cybersecurity and cryptographic challenges, approximately 8–10. Each challenge will contain a hidden flag, represented as a string of characters, which participants must discover to earn points. The contest will be conducted online and will have a duration of 6 hours. Each problem will be accompanied by a problem statement and relevant code for participants to analyze and work with. Winners will be determined based on their total score. In case of a tie, the participant/team with the faster submission time will be given preference. Difficulty Progression: The challenges will increase in difficulty as the competition progresses, testing participants' ability to identify vulnerabilities, analyze systems, and apply appropriate cybersecurity techniques. Participants may need to demonstrate skills in penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and related areas of cybersecurity. FAQs: Winner in case of a tie: In case two or more participants/teams have the same score, the one with the faster submission time will be given preference. Negative marking: The marking scheme will be announced before the test. Individual participation: Yes. Participants can compete individually or in a team of a maximum 2 members.

details_text: About the Event: Test your algorithmic trading and game theory skills in Pokerbots, a high-stakes algorithmic bot competition! Teams must code an autonomous Python bot to compete in a custom poker variant designed with modified Texas Hold’em mechanics to prevent the use of public repositories. Technical & Runtime Constraints: Environment: Python 3.11. Allowed Libraries: Standard Python libraries, NumPy , and SciPy only (no pip installations allowed at runtime) . Compute Limits: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, read-only filesystem, and zero network access . Time Bank: Cumulative time bank per match (~60 seconds for 400 hands) with a hard wall-clock kill. Crashes or exhausted time banks result in match forfeiture. Communication Protocol: Bots operate automatically via a predefined stdin/stdout protocol. Tournament Structure & Progression: All matches utilize duplicate deals (playing every deal twice with swapped seats) to mitigate luck and seat advantage. Stage 1 (Swiss Qualifier): Valid bots play 6 rounds of ~200 duplicate deals (400 hands). Match points: 1 for Win, 0.5 for Draw, 0 for Loss . Stage 2 (Top 32 Finals): The top 32 qualifying teams advance to a full round-robin stage (~500 duplicate deals each). Scores reset prior to this stage. Tie-Breakers: Calculated using a capped chips per hand formula. Rules & Regulations: Team Size: Teams must consist of exactly 2 members . An individual can only be on one team. Submissions: Teams can re-upload/overwrite submissions until November 15th at 23:59 IST . Only the last valid upload counts. Fair Play & Code Review: Code copying, collusion, and network calls are strictly prohibited. Winners' source code will undergo a thorough manual review prior to prize payouts. Evaluation Criteria: Duplicate Deal Performance: Match points accrued during the Swiss Qualifier and final standings in the round-robin stage.

details_text: Overview Students of Global Impact — Social Startup Championship India's largest student-driven nation-building initiative The Social Startup Championship, presented by IFSPD Europe (Special Consultative Status, United Nations ECOSOC), invites student founders across India to solve real problems and build the nation. Open to all students, the championship recognizes young changemakers who turn ideas into action — from grassroots community projects to scalable social ventures. Every Founder who applies gets certified. Top founders advance to a fully funded, 3-day residential summit, where they compete for national awards and university certification alongside India's most promising student innovators. Highlights: Open to all students, no prior experience required. Every applicant receives official certification as a Founder. Top-performing founders are invited to a fully funded, 3-day residential summit — meals, stay, and networking included. Winners receive national recognition and a university certificate programme. Get your Founder Pass at PortAhead Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Details of the Opportunity: Students of Global Impact — Social Startup Championship is India's largest student-driven nation-building initiative, presented by IFSPD Europe (Special Consultative Status, United Nations ECOSOC). It invites student founders to design and execute a real-world action project addressing a UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) of their choice — not a hypothetical pitch, but a project actually carried out and independently verified. Every founder who registers and submits a verified project is certified. Verified founders earn points and badges as they progress through five levels — Founder → Rising Founder → District → State → National → Global Founder. Founders who reach the top levels are invited to a fully funded, 3-day residential summit, where they compete for national awards and a university certification. Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to all students, ages 12–21, studying at a recognized school or college in India. Team format: Individual or team entries. All team members must belong to the same college and the same field of specialization — inter-college and inter-specialization teams are not permitted. Team size: Up to confirm max team size, e.g. 4 members confirm max team size, e.g. 4 members . Format: Open-ended — there are no fixed problem statements or timed rounds. Each founder/team selects one real-world problem aligned to any UN SDG and designs their own project to address it. Process: Register for a Founder Pass at PortAhead.com → execute the project → submit for review → project and impact are independently auditor-verified (self-reported claims alone are not accepted) → verified founders earn points/badges and progress through the levels. Duration: The project execution and submission window runs up to the application deadline of 30 September 2026; auditor verification and level progression continue on a rolling basis afterward. Summit eligibility: Founders verified at confirmthreshold,e.g.Nationallevelandaboveconfirm threshold, e.g. National level and above are invited to the fully funded, 3-day residential summit. Rules: One project per founder/team. The project must be original and not submitted to any other competition or platform. The project must be demonstrably linked to at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal. All team members must be from the same college and the same specialization/field of study; no inter-college or inter-specialization teams. Founder Pass registration at PortAhead.com is mandatory before a project can be submitted for verification. All claims of impact are subject to independent auditor verification. details_text: About the Event: Slay CTF is a thrilling, jeopardy-style Capture The Flag competition designed to test your offensive security skills, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Whether you are a beginner looking to break into the world of cybersecurity or a seasoned hacker hunting for complex challenges, Slay CTF offers a dynamic environment to exploit vulnerabilities, crack ciphers, and trace digital footprints. Put your skills to the test, climb the global leaderboard, and prove your mettle in the ultimate battle of bits and bytes! Eligibility & Registration Guidelines: Target Audience: Open to all students (UG/PG/Diploma), early-career professionals, and self-taught security enthusiasts. Inter-College Teams: Allowed and highly encouraged. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed (Open to all branches and backgrounds). Team Size: Participate individually or in teams of [1 - 3 members] . Prerequisites: Eagerness to learn. Challenge Categories (Topics) The CTF will feature a diverse set of challenges scaled from beginner to advanced difficulties across the following domains: Web Exploitation: Uncover vulnerabilities in web applications (e.g., SQLi, XSS, IDOR, SSRF). OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Track down hidden information and piece together digital trails across the public internet. Cryptography: Break encryption schemes, decode ciphers, and analyze cryptographic protocols. Digital Forensics: Analyze memory dumps, network packet captures (PCAPs), and hidden file metadata. Reverse Engineering: Deconstruct compiled binaries and understand their underlying logic. Miscellaneous / Sanity: Brain-teasers, scripting challenges, and out-of-the-box puzzles. Event Format & Process Format: Hybrid (Online + JGEC Campus), Jeopardy-Style CTF. Platform: Challenges will be hosted on our dedicated infrastructure ( CTFd). Duration: The competition will run continuously for 3 hours . Scoring System: Dynamic scoring will be implemented (the point value of a challenge decreases as more teams solve it). Process: Once registered on Unstop, team leaders will receive the platform link and credentials via email 24 hours prior to the event kickoff. Rules & Code of Conduct No Flag Sharing: Sharing flags or solutions with other teams is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification of all involved parties. No Brute-Forcing: Automated brute-forcing of the flag submission platform or challenge infrastructure is forbidden unless explicitly mentioned in the challenge description. No Attacking the Infrastructure: Do not launch Denial of Service (DoS/DDoS) attacks or attempt to compromise the hosting servers. Collaboration: You are free to use Google, AI tools, and public documentation, but collaboration is strictly limited to your own team members. Final Decisions: The organizing team's decisions regarding scoring, disputes, and disqualifications are final and binding. Prizes & Perks Cash Prize, Certification Vouchers and goodies. [NOTE: Cash Prizes and Goodies exclusively for offline participation] Official Certificate of Participation for those who solve at least one challenge.

details_text: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the foundations of an entirely new civilization. Participants are encouraged to think beyond applications and incremental improvements. Every project should solve a meaningful challenge that contributes to rebuilding society—whether through communication, energy, healthcare, infrastructure, education, resilience, exploration, or entirely new approaches that redefine the future. This is not about recreating yesterday. It is about engineering tomorrow. The Mission: Design and develop an innovative solution that would help humanity rebuild after the collapse of modern civilization. Your project may be software, hardware, embedded systems, IoT, AI, robotics, communication systems, cybersecurity, biotechnology, space technology, sustainable engineering, or any interdisciplinary solution aligned with the mission. Projects should focus on solving real-world problems with practical engineering, long-term scalability, and meaningful societal impact. Civilization Pillars: Every project belongs to one of the official Civilization Pillars that represent the essential functions required to rebuild society. The detailed descriptions of all pillars are provided separately. Choose the pillar that best represents the purpose of your solution, not simply the technologies you use. Who Can Participate? Students from any recognized institution are welcome. Participants from all engineering, science, technology, design, management, and interdisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged. Teams must follow the team size specified on the registration page. Innovation thrives when diverse disciplines work together. What Can You Build? We welcome projects across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Embedded Systems & Electronics Internet of Things (IoT) Robotics & Automation Wireless Communication Systems Healthcare & Medical Technologies Renewable Energy Smart Infrastructure Disaster Management Cybersecurity Space & Aerospace Technologies Sustainability Human-Centered Design Frontier & Moonshot Innovations If your solution contributes meaningfully to rebuilding civilization, it belongs here. Submission Requirements: Teams should be prepared to submit: Project presentation Technical documentation Source code repository Prototype or proof of concept Demonstration video (if applicable) Additional submission guidelines and templates will be shared with registered participants. Evaluation: Projects will be assessed on their overall contribution toward rebuilding civilization, including: Innovation Engineering excellence Technical feasibility Scalability Societal impact Resilience Quality of presentation The complete judging rubric is available in the attached documentation. General Rules: All submitted work must be original. Open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools may be used with proper attribution. AI-assisted development is permitted unless otherwise specified. Plagiarism or intellectual property violations will result in immediate disqualification. Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and uphold the event's code of conduct. Decisions made by the organizing committee and judging panel will be final. A comprehensive rulebook is available in the attached resources. Why Participate? DAY ZERO is more than a competition. It is an opportunity to think like the engineers who would shape the first generation of a new civilization. Challenge assumptions. Collaborate across disciplines. Build technologies that matter. Engineer systems that could redefine humanity's future. Tomorrow Begins Here. History remembers the civilizations that were built. The next one starts with your idea.

details_text: Business Analytics Workshop: Business Analytics is the practice of turning raw business data into clear, actionable decisions. It sits at the intersection of business thinking and data tools - using spreadsheets, databases, and visualization platforms to spot patterns, forecast trends, and answer real business questions. Today, this practice is being reshaped by AI: natural-language queries, auto-generated insights, and AI-assisted dashboards are changing how analysts work, making the skill faster to learn and more powerful to apply. From sales and marketing to operations and finance, businesses now run on dashboards, not gut feeling - and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across one intensive day, you'll go from raw, messy data to a real dashboard and a business recommendation you'll actually present - no prior coding or analytics background required. Workshop Content (18 December 2026 ) : Introduction to Business Analytics Excel for Data Analysis & Visualization SQL for Business Analytics Power BI Dashboards & Reporting AI-Assisted Analytics Tools Excel–Power BI Integration Forecasting, Segmentation & KPI Design Capstone Project & Wrap-Up

title: International Conference on Sustainability Through Digital Transformation
description: The International Conference on "Sustainability through Digital Transformation: Insights from Management, Humanities, Science and Social Science" is organized by Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions (MPGI) with…
details_text: The International Conference on "Sustainability through Digital Transformation: Insights from Management, Humanities, Science and Social Science" is organized by Maharana Pratap Group of Institutions (MPGI) with generous grant support from Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Azad Technical University (AKTU), Lucknow. The twin imperatives of our time — achieving sustainable development and harnessing rapid digital transformation — can no longer be addressed in isolation. Emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Internet of Things, and Cloud Computing are reshaping how organizations, governments, and communities pursue economic, social, and environmental goals. At the same time, the pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) demands insights that cut across disciplinary boundaries — from business strategy and public policy to ethics, culture, scientific innovation, and social behaviour. This conference provides a common platform for academicians, researchers, industry practitioners, policymakers, and research scholars from India and abroad to deliberate on how digital transformation can be leveraged as a catalyst for sustainability. By bringing together perspectives from Management, Humanities, Science, and Social Science, the conference seeks to foster interdisciplinary dialogue, encourage collaborative research, and generate actionable insights for building a resilient, inclusive, and digitally empowered sustainable future. Selected papers will be considered for publication in conference proceedings / reputed journals (details to be announced).

title: CAD Competition

details_text: Competition Description: Do you have the creativity, precision, and technical skills to transform an engineering idea into a 3D model under time pressure? Welcome to Speed Modelling, an exciting CAD challenge where engineering design meets speed and accuracy! Participants will be given a mechanical component, reference image, or engineering drawing and must recreate its 3D model using CAD software within the allotted time. The challenge is to interpret the given reference, visualize the geometry, and construct an accurate digital model using appropriate modelling tools and techniques. From basic geometric features to intricate mechanical components, every modelling operation counts. Participants will be evaluated on dimensional accuracy, geometric precision, modelling approach, and completion time. Can you turn a design into a precise 3D model before the clock runs out? Visualize. Model. Conquer! Competition Format: Participation: Individual Duration: As specified by the organizers. Software: CAD software specified by the organizers (e.g., CATIA, SolidWorks, or Fusion 360). Challenge: Create a 3D model of the given mechanical component using the provided reference. Evaluation: Dimensional accuracy, geometric precision, completeness, and time management. Winning Criteria: Highest overall score based on modelling accuracy and completion. Rules And Regulations: Each participant must independently create the assigned 3D model using the designated CAD software. A reference image, engineering drawing, or component geometry will be provided at the beginning of the competition. Participants must complete the assigned model within the allotted time. Only the CAD software and tools approved by the organizers may be used. Participants must work independently. Collaboration, communication with other participants, or external assistance is prohibited. Use of pre-existing CAD models, downloaded files, or ready-made templates for the assigned component is strictly prohibited. Participants must save their work in the designated file format and submit it before the deadline. The model must represent the given component accurately, including its major geometric features and dimensions. Participants must not use mobile phones, the internet, or external references unless explicitly permitted. Any technical issues must be immediately reported to the event coordinators. The organizers’ decisions regarding evaluation, rule violations, and final results will be binding. Judging Criteria: Evaluation Parameter Weightage Dimensional Accuracy 30% Geometric Accuracy and Completeness 25% Modelling Approach and Feature Utilization 20% Time Management 15% File Organization and Final Submission 10% Total 100% Winner Selection: Participants will be ranked based on their cumulative scores across all evaluation parameters. The participant achieving the highest score in the final round will be declared the winner. In case of a tie, the participant who completes the model with greater accuracy in lesser time may be given preference. Prizes And Certificates: Exciting prizes and certificates will be awarded to the winners, with certificates of participation for eligible participants. What To Expect: Get ready to test your engineering visualization, spatial reasoning, CAD proficiency, and design efficiency. This competition challenges you to transform two-dimensional references into accurate three-dimensional models while racing against time. Every sketch, feature, dimension, and modelling operation matters! Can you design with precision when every second counts?

details_text: AstroPixel: The Night Sky Photography Competition The night sky has fascinated people for as long as we’ve looked up. AstroPixel is a competition for people who chase that kind of image. Whether you shoot with a DSLR on a tripod, a mirrorless camera with a fast lens, a tracking mount and telescope, or a smartphone with night mode, you are welcome here. We care about what you capture and how thoughtfully you capture it, not how expensive your gear is. How Entries Are Judged Entries will be judged on creativity (originality, composition and storytelling) and technical skill (focus, exposure, noise control and processing), weighted equally. Rules and Guidelines All work must be your own, captured by you. Each participant may submit up to 1 image. Heavy manipulation, such as adding stars or objects that were not in the original scene, is not allowed. Standard adjustments like stacking, noise reduction, curves and color correction are fine. Include a short caption with each entry: location, date, and camera and lens or telescope used. A brief note on your process is a bonus. Grab your camera, find a dark sky, and show us the universe through your lens.

details_text: ANAVARAN, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is an immersive sustainability investigation and strategy competition that challenges participants to uncover the gap between corporate sustainability claims and ground realities. Teams of four step into the roles of Sustainability Investigators and Corporate Strategists, investigating Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd., a fictional organisation whose green image may not reflect its actual environmental and social impact. Across three challenging rounds, participants will identify greenwashing, investigate hidden contradictions, assess business risks and develop commercially viable sustainability strategies under real-world-inspired crises. From questioning environmental claims to defending strategic decisions before a jury, ANAVARAN tests critical thinking, ESG awareness, analytical ability and the power to build a genuinely sustainable future. ROUND 1 – GREEN OR GREENWASH? Spot the Illusion Teams will receive a collection of fictional ESG claims, advertisements, sustainability statements, corporate announcements and certification claims made by Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. regarding its proposed Hooghly Data Park in West Bengal. Participants must critically examine each of the 10 claims and classify them into one of three categories: Genuine Sustainability Greenwashing Misleading Communication Each classification must be supported by a short justification explaining what is being promised, whether the claim is verifiable, what important information is missing and whether the communication creates an exaggerated positive impression. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop. Format: ESG Claim Classification + Justification Brief. Case: Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. – Hooghly Data Park. Number of Claims: 10. Submission: Each claim must include its classification and a justification of 3–6 lines. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Classification Accuracy – 50% Quality of Justification – 40% Clarity of Expression – 10% ROUND 2 – THE GREENWASH FILES Uncover the Truth The qualifying teams will receive a comprehensive investigation dossier containing public statements, internal technical documents, employment projections, renewable energy plans, community partnership updates and environmental assessments relating to Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. Teams must investigate the contradictions between the company's public sustainability commitments and its internal operational realities. Participants must identify instances of greenwashing, uncover misleading disclosures, assess environmental and social implications, and evaluate the financial, regulatory and reputational risks arising from these gaps. Teams will present their investigation findings and risk assessment before the jury. Round Details: Mode: Offline. Timing: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (as specified in the event brochure). Format: Case Investigation + Jury Findings Presentation. Case: Detailed investigation of Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.'s Hooghly Data Park. Qualification: Top 6 Teams advance to Round 3 (Grand Finale). Key Areas of Investigation: Water consumption, groundwater stress and water-positive claims. Renewable energy commitments and net-zero targets. Employment claims and actual local job creation. Farmer partnerships and treated wastewater utilisation. Green certifications and environmental compliance. Financial, regulatory, reputational and social risks. details_text: KaalDrishti, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is a business analytics competition that challenges participants to step into the role of Data Investigators and uncover the truth behind a company's crisis. Teams of four will work with fragmented financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business information to identify hidden patterns, detect anomalies and establish the real cause of a problem. Across three challenging rounds, participants will investigate an unsolved business crisis, tackle analytical challenges and defend their conclusions through hypothesis testing and a live boardroom presentation. The event tests analytical thinking, data interpretation, statistical reasoning, problem-solving and the ability to convert data into meaningful business decisions. ROUND 1 – THE CRIME SCENE: FIND THE STORY Project Mirage – Uncover the Hidden Truth Participants will receive a business scenario, problem statement and relevant datasets. The case file will contain fragmented information such as financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business evidence. Teams must independently understand the situation, identify relevant patterns and anomalies, determine the root cause of the crisis and develop a hypothesis explaining what went wrong and why. Based on their analysis, teams must propose feasible business solutions while complying with the given constraints. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Open-Ended Data Investigation + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: PDF deck of maximum 10 pages, excluding the Introduction and Closing slides. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Understanding of the problem and root cause analysis. Analytical rigour specific to the dataset. Methodology adopted. Feasibility and quality of the proposed business solution. ROUND 2 – THE LOCKED DATA: UNLOCK THE EVIDENCE Xcelerate – Excel E-Sports The qualifying teams will enter an analytical challenge where they will be provided with a dataset and a problem statement. Participants must analyse the given information and develop an optimised solution or analytical model according to the requirements. Teams will be required to demonstrate their analytical capabilities using Microsoft Excel. They can use Excel charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins to develop and present their solutions. However, the final solution must be presented entirely in Excel. The methodology adopted and the plugins used must be explicitly mentioned. Round Details: Mode: Offline Format: Dataset-Based Analytical Modelling and Excel Challenge. Tools: Microsoft Excel, Excel Charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins. Submission/Presentation: The solution must be presented in Excel only. Qualification: Top 5 Teams advance to Round 3. Evaluation Focus: Analytical reasoning. Data interpretation and modelling. Problem-solving ability. Efficiency and accuracy of the solution. Methodology and effective use of Excel tools. ROUND 3 – THE FALSE TRAIL & THE BOARDROOM TRIAL: DELIVER THE VERDICT Find the Real Cause. Defend It Under Fire. The finalists will be presented with multiple plausible explanations for the company's crisis, each supported by a different set of evidence. Only one explanation will represent the actual cause. Teams must test each hypothesis against the evidence collected in the earlier rounds, identify explanations based on bias, false correlation or manipulated data, and trace the crisis back to its Point of No Return — the exact past decision that set the crisis in motion. Participants will then present their final verdict and business recommendations before a jury acting as the company's Board, which will cross-examine their assumptions and conclusions. Round Details: Mode: Offline – Live Defence, Grand Finale. Format: Hypothesis Testing + Live Verdict Presentation + Jury Cross-Examination. details_text: Overview YUGANTAR, presented by FINNOVATION as part of XAVIESTA 5.0, is an immersive marketing strategy competition that challenges participants to rewrite the destiny of a fictional Indian footwear brand. Through three interconnected rounds, teams will investigate the brand's history, uncover the strategic decision behind its downfall, rewrite a defining moment in its journey, and navigate the consequences of their choices. From analysing fragmented evidence and developing revised marketing strategies to tackling real-time marketing crises, participants must demonstrate their consumer understanding, analytical thinking, creativity and strategic decision-making. Here, every decision shapes the future, and every consequence tells a story. Round 1 – The Archive Decode the Brand Teams will receive a fragmented case archive containing old advertisements, consumer reviews, sales data, competitor movements, internal memos and market research relating to Kadam Footwear, a fictional Indian footwear brand. Participants must reconstruct the brand's timeline, identify the single strategic decision that changed its destiny and support their conclusions with evidence from the provided documents. Each finalist will face a team-specific marketing crisis shaped by the changes introduced in Round 2. Teams must allocate a limited marketing budget across digital marketing, influencers, product, retail, partnerships and consumer research to respond to the crisis. They will then face a CEO-level dilemma, choosing whether to Accept, Alter or Reset the brand's future direction. The challenge concludes with a live boardroom presentation and jury cross-examination, where teams must defend their strategy and decisions. details_text: Date: 21st November Registration fees: 200 per participant Overview PERPLEXED is built around two partner companies whose businesses depend on each other, and both are struggling. Half the teams act as consulting firms hired by Company A, and the other half are hired by Company B. The problems are real within the game, but are not given to teams directly. Teams discover them by interviewing AI chatbots playing company stakeholders, such as the CEO, CFO, operations head, HR manager or disgruntled employee. Each stakeholder knows only part of the story and may have their own agenda, hide or downplay facts, or misremember events. Teams must ask effective questions, connect clues, distinguish facts from spin, and present a clear diagnosis with practical recommendations to judges acting as the client's board. Not everything worth knowing is said out loud: the company portal also holds traces of everyday office life that may quietly support or contradict what stakeholders claim. Neither company's problems can be solved from inside one company: part of every root cause sits with the partner, and employees on each side may be quick to blame the other. Midway through the investigation, each team must find and convince a team working on the other company to form an alliance, combine what both sides know, and present a joint diagnosis. Eligibility: Open to students. Teams of 2-4. Performance Guidelines: Robots or simulated bots must follow arena rules and size limits. Online teams use the provided simulator; on-site teams must pass inspection. Robots may be modified between rounds. Judging Criteria Match results (50%) Strategy (20%) Robot performance (20%) Adaptation between rounds (10%).

title: Math Sprint
description: No opponents, no luck: just you and the questions. Math Sprint is a live online Maths challenge on Mind Race (mindrace.in). Everyone starts together and solves questions one by one, on their own. The questions adapt to…
details_text: No opponents, no luck: just you and the questions. Math Sprint is a live online Maths challenge on Mind Race (mindrace.in). Everyone starts together and solves questions one by one, on their own. The questions adapt to you: get them right and they get harder; get stuck and they get easier. Everyone is tested at their own level, and the leaderboard shows who is really the strongest. When: Saturday, 14 November · 8:00–9:00 PM IST Subject: Mathematics Where: Online at mindrace.in, on your phone or laptop Entry: Free, individual How to take part Register here on Unstop. Important: the event is played on Mind Race, so registering on Unstop alone is not enough. Before 14 Nov, create your free Mind Race account, verify your email and join the event here: mindrace.in/e/FXZNEG?ref=unstop (event code FXZNEG ). At 8:00 PM, open the event and press Start . How it works Answer questions one at a time until 9:00 PM. Each question has its own timer, from 30 seconds for easy ones to 90 seconds for the hardest. Attempt at least 75 questions to be ranked. Skips and time-outs count as attempts. That's under 48 seconds per question, so keep moving. You're ranked by your Mind Score : the skill your answers prove. Hard questions solved count for more, and a careless mistake on an easy one costs a lot. Answering more makes your score more certain, not bigger, so accuracy beats rushing. You can skip at most 1 question in 3. A skip counts as half a wrong answer, and the next question won't be easier. The leaderboard freezes for the last 5 minutes. You can't start after 8:50 PM. Prizes ₹200 · ₹150 · ₹100 Amazon vouchers A certificate of participation for everyone who attempts 75 questions Fair play Solve it yourself: no calculator, AI, search engine or help from anyone. One player, one account, one device. We check the timing and accuracy of every answer. Before winners are announced, top players may be asked to solve a few questions live on Google Meet with camera, mic and screen sharing on. Anyone caught cheating loses their result and prize and is banned from Mind Race for 3 days.

details_text: Consilium, The Consulting and Strategy Club of IIM Kashipur, aspires to promote a culture of in-depth analysis, evidence-based research, and effective presentation to support you in communicating your viewpoints. The Club works to boost students' interest in the consulting sector and give them proper exposure to the business world. To close the gap between business and academics, the group routinely arranges sessions and bootcamps with prominent figures in the consulting and strategy sectors. It also sees it as part of its mission to educate the members and the students on the basic frameworks and matrices employed in the consulting industry. Disquisition : A Pan-India Article Writing Competition that provides students from prominent schools across the country with a platform to showcase their knowledge, perspectives, and ideas on emerging trends and contemporary topics in the Consulting and Strategy domain. It aims to provide valuable insights on current topics while bringing optimal solutions to crack present-day obstacles. Theme: The Next Billion: Unlocking India's Untapped Markets and Consumers Article Topics: The Her Economy: Why Women in Bharat Are India's Most Underestimated Consumers The Gig Wallet: How Informal Income Is Rewriting Credit and Consumption The Language of Growth: Why India's Next Billion Will Speak Vernacular ⁠The Trust Economy: Why Winning Bharat Requires More Than Competitive Pricing Beyond Digital Access: Leveraging India's Digital Public Infrastructure to Create New Economic Opportunities Reimagining the Last Mile: Building Scalable Business Models for India's Underserved Markets Innovation at the Right Price: Rethinking Product Design for India's Value-Conscious Consumers From Data to Demand: Using Consumer Analytics to Discover India's Hidden Markets ⁠Mapping India's Next Growth Corridors: Identifying Emerging Consumer Markets Beyond Metros Insuring the Uninsured: Why Micro-Insurance Keeps Failing on Distribution and Trust, and What an Embedded Model Could Fix Rules and Guidelines: The competition is for individuals/teams (1-2 members). Choose any one of the above-given topics. Plagiarism of any kind will not be tolerated and will be subject to disqualification from the competition (a leading software will be used to identify plagiarism). Please refrain from using AI-generated material. AI-generated plagiarism will also be checked. The article should be an original work of creation, and references should be mentioned wherever necessary. However, there is no limit to creativity. Relevant graphs or data can be added to the article only if the participant makes them. Text font size: 12, font style: Times New Roman, and page limit: 2 pages (standard A4 size on typical word processing software, e.g., MS Word), excluding infographics, charts, tables, and references. You are free to use any design tool such as Canva. The article should be visually appealing, and points for creativity will be given on that basis. There is no upper word limit for the article. However, participants are expected to coherently encapsulate their ideas within 2 A4 pages (typically at least 600 words) excluding visuals, infographics and references. We believe that creativity cannot be bound in words. The cover page should include your name, institute name, course details, and contact number. The conclusion should highlight the writer's views/suggestions/opinions on the respective title. Submission should be in PDF format with the naming convention as TeamName_CollegeName_Topic and should be uploaded through Unstop only. No late submissions will be accepted via e-mail. Your entries will be judged on creativity, content, presentation, and relevance. Rewards: The best article will be featured as the "Consilium Article of the Month" by Consilium, Consulting and Strategy Club of IIM Kashipur. E-certificates for winners and runners-up, along with cash prizes. Submissions other than the winners will also receive E-certificates of Apprec
