details_text: Overview Global Case Masters 2026 , the inaugural edition of the international management case competition hosted by the International Relations Centre , IMT Ghaziabad , brings together students from universities and institutions across India and abroad. Centered around the theme "Navigating Global Business Challenges," the competition provides participants with an opportunity to analyze a business situation, evaluate different alternatives, and develop practical solutions. It challenges teams to apply their classroom learning to business decisions while testing their analytical, strategic, and problem-solving abilities. With participants competing on a common platform, Global Case Masters aims to encourage fresh perspectives, sound business judgment, and well-reasoned recommendations. Case Brief: Aureon Mobility – Growth Across Borders The competition will revolve around Aureon Mobility Group , a multinational automobile manufacturer operating across Asia, Europe and the Americas, with manufacturing facilities in India, Mexico and Poland. As the company plans its next phase of international growth, it faces important decisions concerning market opportunities, manufacturing capacity, investment priorities and supply-chain risks. Participants will take on the role of business advisors and develop a growth strategy for Aureon Mobility. They will need to evaluate the company's expansion options, decide where investments should be directed, and consider how it can manage international business risks while remaining profitable by 2030. The challenge is to develop a clear, practical, and well-supported strategy that addresses the company's long-term business objectives. General Guidelines and Eligibility The competition is open to all undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD students pursuing a full-time degree at institutions in India or abroad. Participants must be currently enrolled as full-time students at their respective institutions. Students can register individually or in teams of 1–3 members . Cross-college teams are not allowed. All members of a team must belong to the same institution. An individual cannot be a member of more than one team. Any deviation from the eligibility criteria or team formation guidelines may result in the disqualification of the entire team. Competition Structure The competition will be conducted in two online submission rounds . Round 1: Preliminary Submission Teams must submit a 2-slide PowerPoint presentation outlining their understanding of the case, the key challenges faced by Aureon Mobility and their proposed course of action. The submission should clearly identify the major business issues and present the team's initial direction for addressing them. Shortlisted teams will qualify for the next round. Round 2: Detailed Presentation Submission Shortlisted teams must submit a 4–5-slide PowerPoint presentation presenting their detailed business strategy. The presentation should explain the key challenges, recommended growth strategy, reasoning behind the proposed decisions, and steps for implementation. Teams are expected to consider relevant market opportunities, investment choices, international operations, and potential business risks. Research and relevant information should be used to support the recommendations. Submission Guidelines The case document and submission instructions will be available on the Unstop competition page. All submissions must be made in PowerPoint format through the respective round's submission link on Unstop. The maximum permitted file size is 50 MB per submission. The team leader must upload the final submission using the Submit option on the platform. Submissions can be changed before the respective deadline by navigating to Submission → Change Submission . No extensions will be provided beyond the announced submission deadlines. Rewards and Recognition Outstanding teams will be recognized for their analysis, strategic thinking, and proposed business solutions. Win

details_text: Event Description: A high-speed, head-to-head robotics competition where custom-built robots face off in a 1v1 mechanical soccer match. Teams design, build, and pilot their manual bots in a purpose-built arena to outmaneuver opponents, defend their penalty zones, and score goals using a mini football. Date: 21st November (Tech Inspection & Pool Stage) / 22nd November (Knockouts & Finals) Registration Fee: ₹800- per Team Registration Process: Participants will have to register on the official Saturnalia registration platform before the deadline mentioned on the platform. Participation may be subject to shortlisting in case of an overwhelming response. Only shortlisted participants, if applicable, will be notified about the further process. Participants must provide the required details and complete all necessary registration formalities within the specified deadline. Participation is exclusively open to college students possessing valid college ID cards for the current academic year. Participants must carry their valid college ID card during the event. The registration fee, if applicable, will be communicated through the official registration platform. Rules & Regulations: Event Overview & Arena Specifications: Mayhem is the premier combat robotics tournament of Saturnalia. Engineering teams design and build wireless combat machines that can deliver active kinetic strikes while withstanding hostile impacts. A robot wins by disabling its opponent through a Technical Knockout (TKO), or by scoring the most points for Aggression, Control and Damage. Arena Specifications & Containment: Enclosure Footprint: 16 ft × 16 ft × 7 ft fully enclosed steel frame High-impact, shatter-resistant polycarbonate safety walls Reinforced perimeter base guards Active Floor Hazard Pit: A 3 ft × 3 ft automated floor pit opens during the final 60 seconds of every match round. Forcing an opposing robot completely into the pit is an instant TKO. Safety & Containment Systems: Dual hard-wired emergency arena kill switches Optical containment screens Active smoke and exhaust ventilation for battery safety Weight Classes, Roster & Eligibility: Every machine must pass formal technical inspection before competing. Weight limits are strictly enforced, with a maximum tolerance of 1%. Weight Classes: Featherweight: up to 8.0 kg (17.6 lbs) Middleweight: up to 15.0 kg (33.0 lbs) Heavyweight: up to 30.0 kg (66.0 lbs) Roster & Structural Rules: Team Roster: 2 to 6 registered members per team. Teams may include members from more than one college, provided everyone’s student credentials are verified. Dimensions: there is no limit on overall dimensions. The fully assembled robot must fit through the 4 ft × 4 ft arena access hatch without disassembly. Walker Bonus: robots using true non-wheeled linear walking mechanisms get an extra 10% weight allowance above their class limit. Cluster Bots: a team may deploy multiple sub-units under one entry. The combined mass and dimensions of all active sub-units must stay within the class limits. Technical, Power & Weapon Regulations: Control Systems & Radio: Radio Protocol: 2.4 GHz digital spread-spectrum systems with frequency-hopping channels. Prohibited Control: tethered remote connections and fully autonomous robots are strictly prohibited. Fail-Safe Requirement: all drive systems and weapon throttles must return to neutral/zero power immediately if the transmitter signal is lost or interrupted. Electrical Power & Battery Shielding: Voltage Cap: electric drive systems only. The potential between any two electrical points must not exceed 36 V DC. Engines: internal combustion engines (ICE) are banned. Battery Containment: every LiPo, LiFe or gel battery cell must be fully enclosed in a rigid enclosure of at least 2 mm steel or aluminium plate, to contain thermal runaway. Mobility & Weapons: Allowed Mobility: Wheels Treads Walking mechanisms Controlled hopping assemblies (maximum height clearance of 6 ft) Prohibited Mobility: Vacuu

details_text: VibeForge – National-Level Hackathon | NIMS Quest 1.0 VibeForge is a national-level hackathon organised by the STEM Department, NIMS University Rajasthan, as part of NIMS Quest 1.0. The hackathon challenges participants to transform innovative ideas into functional prototypes within a three-hour time limit. By combining programming, AI-assisted development tools, and modern coding workflows, participants will develop practical, technology-driven solutions to real-world problems. The competition encourages creativity, innovation, technical execution, and effective problem-solving. Participants must demonstrate their ability to develop a working prototype, explain their technical approach, and communicate the real-world applications of their solutions. Competition Details Date : 25 November 2026 Time : 9:30 AM – 12:30 PM IST Duration : 3 hours Format : Team-based hackathon Competition Level: National Organiser: STEM Department, NIMS University Rajasthan Total Prize Pool: ₹15,000 Eligibility Criteria The hackathon is open to all the undergraduate students or students from colleges and universities across India. Participants must register through the official Unstop listing within the registration period and meet the eligibility requirements established by the organising committee. Team Size: 1-4 Each team must register its members according to the instructions provided by the organisers. Competition Format and Process The hackathon will consist of three evaluation stages conducted within the allotted three-hour duration. Teams will identify a problem, develop an innovative solution, build a functional prototype using programming and AI tools, and present their solution through a final pitch and live demonstration within three hours. Mode: Offline Rules and Guidelines Participants must complete registration and provide accurate information as required by the organisers. Teams must comply with the announced eligibility criteria and team-size requirements. All development and submissions must be completed within the allotted competition duration. Participants must submit original work and must not plagiarise or present another team's work as their own. AI-assisted coding tools and other development resources may be used in accordance with the guidelines announced by the organisers. Teams must be able to explain their solution, implementation, and use of development tools during evaluation. Participants must follow all submission instructions and deadlines communicated by the organising committee. Any attempt to manipulate the evaluation process, misrepresent work, or gain an unfair advantage may result in disqualification. The organising committee's decisions regarding competition administration and disqualification will be final. Evaluation Criteria Innovation and Originality: 20% Functionality and Execution: 25% Problem Relevance: 15% AI and Modern Tool Integration: 15% UI/UX Design: 10% Presentation and Pitch: 10% Time Management: 5% The total evaluation weightage is 100%. Judges will assess submissions based on the published criteria, the functionality of the prototype, and the team's ability to explain its solution. Prizes and Recognition VibeForge offers a total prize pool of ₹15,000. First Prize: ₹7,000 Second Prize: ₹5,000 Third Prize: ₹3,000 Certificates and additional recognition: To all the winners and participants. Prize distribution will be subject to verification of the winners and the conditions announced by the organising committee. VibeForge welcomes aspiring developers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts to collaborate, build functional prototypes, and present creative solutions to real-world challenges. Join the challenge to showcase your technical skills, transform ideas into working solutions, and compete for exciting rewards at NIMS Quest 1.0.

description: Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate, postgraduate, and high school students, as well as working professionals and stock market enthusiasts. No prior finance or trading background is required; concepts are taught from…
details_text: Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate, postgraduate, and high school students, as well as working professionals and stock market enthusiasts. No prior finance or trading background is required; concepts are taught from absolute scratch. Format & Rules Mode: 2-Day Offline Workshop at IIT Bombay Campus. Duration: 12 to 16 Hours total (split across 2 days). Prerequisites: Participants must bring their own laptop (with internet capability), notepad, and pen. Team Structure: Participants must register individually. Inter-College & Inter-Specialization: Allowed for all hands-on group tasks and capstone exercises (participants from any college, stream, or academic background can collaborate). Certification: A Certificate of Training from Techfest, IIT Bombay will be awarded upon attending all sessions. Topics: Stock Market Fundamentals & Structure: Exchanges (NSE/BSE), market participants (FIIs, DIIs, Retail), order execution types, and index dynamics . Fundamental Analysis & Stock Screening: Decoding financial statements (P&L, Cash Flow), key ratios (P/E, ROE, Debt-to-Equity), and building screener filters. Technical Analysis & Chart Reading Basics: Dow theory, dynamic support/resistance, trendlines, and core candlestick patterns (Hammer, Engulfing, Doji). Key Indicators & Trading Signals: Moving averages (SMA vs. EMA), momentum indicators (RSI, MACD), and volume breakout validation. Trading Strategies & Market Psychology: Swing trading, momentum investing, long-term value selection, and emotional discipline. Risk Management & Capital Protection: Position sizing rules, risk-to-reward ratios, stop-loss strategy, and capital allocation. AI Tools for Smart Investors: Leveraging AI assistants (ChatGPT/Claude) for fast quarterly earnings summaries and news breakdown. Live Market Workshop & Mock Trading Simulation: Live breakdown of Nifty 50 stocks, chart setups, and an interactive group portfolio simulation. Speakers Industry practitioners and senior equity analysts with hands-on trading experience in live markets. (Formal mentor profiles and bios will be updated on the portal prior to the event session).

The problems test how well you handle visual hierarchy, information architecture and design systems that still work when they grow. Fee: Free Tool: Figma (required) Team size: 1 to 4 people Prizes: Cash prizes, goodies, certificates and national recognition Who can join Any undergraduate, postgraduate or diploma student with a valid college ID. title: Paper Presentation Competition- Fault Lines: Reporting a Divided World
organiser: Lady Shri Ram College for Women (LSR) University of Delhi (DU)
description: Paper presentation competition Date: 19th november, 2026. Venue: Lady shri ram college for women. Concept note Every society has fault lines: cracks that run along politics, identity, class, language, religion, region,…
details_text: Paper presentation competition Date: 19th november, 2026. Venue: Lady shri ram college for women. Concept note Every society has fault lines: cracks that run along politics, identity, class, language, religion, region, and generation. Most of the time they sit quietly under the surface, and then something shifts, and suddenly everyone can feel the ground move. Journalism is standing right on top of those cracks, and it has been for a long time. It reports on them, sometimes helps people cross them, sometimes pries them wider, and the whole time it is being shaped by the divisions of the people who make the news and the ones who read it. The newsroom is easy to picture as a neutral space where facts simply arrive and get pushed further into the lives of the masses. But in that room sit people. They grew up somewhere, speak some languages but not others, and know some kinds of people much better than the rest. That shows up in who gets hired, which villages ever get a reporter, and whose number is saved as a source. Soon the “neutral” newsroom starts revealing a different picture. Headlines have their own tricks too. one word can tell you who to feel for before you have read a single line. Then your feed steps in and serves whatever keeps you looking, so two people can end up living through the same tuesday and walk away with completely different versions of it. Readers are split in very ordinary ways too. a flood in a small town gets two lines in a national paper while waterlogging in a big city gets a live blog. The same event shows up in hindi, english or bengali, on a tv screen or in a forwarded video, in ten seconds or in five thousand words. Your grandparents and your younger cousin probably trust completely different sources, and each is quietly sure they are the sensible one. put all of that together, and it is fair to wonder whether there is still one public conversation, or just several running in parallel and never quite meeting. Yet media has proved to have its own remedies. Local and regional outlets, independent digital platforms, community radio and citizen reporters have let in voices that older newsrooms rarely did. While social media seems to be the starting point for this storm, a deeper inspection reveals otherwise. The reform-minded and vernacular presses of the nineteenth century were already carrying the divisions of their time, and radio and television did the same. What is different now is the speed. A photograph or a caption gets shared and answered within minutes, which leaves almost no time to think about language, imagery, or who might get hurt by it. anyone who works in or studies journalism ends up circling those questions sooner or later. This competition invites you to look at what happens at these edges. How does the media cover the difference, and who gets left out when it does? How do headlines, framing, and algorithms sharpen divides, and can storytelling still make room for nuance? What does it mean to report on a community you belong to, or one you do not? We also want to hear about divisions closer to home: the gap between urban and rural coverage, english and regional-language media, the newsroom and the people it writes about. For students, these questions carry both practical and theoretical significance. Today's readers will become tomorrow's reporters, editors and producers, and they will carry forward the habits of framing, sourcing and storytelling that they learn now. this competition is a chance to examine those habits, to ask who they serve, and to think about how they might be done differently. Participants can use frameworks, case studies, content or discourse analysis, interviews, field reporting or lived experience to explore where media, society, identity and power meet. Broad areas of exploration may include (but are not limited to): Caste, religion, class and gender in the newsroom. Framing of difference in headlines and television debates. details_text: Dart Browser Ai Opportunity Challenge Top 10 Entries Win Unpaid Winter Internships at Dart Browser The Opportunity: Dart Browser is building a Chromium-based browser focused on privacy, local-first AI agents, and user choice of AI models. We are looking for students who can reason clearly about technology, understand users, and turn research into product decisions. Prize: 10 unpaid winter internship offers. Role: AI Product Strategy & Research Intern. Mode: Fully remote. Commitment: 4–6 hours per week. Timing: Scheduled according to each selected student's availability between November 2026 and February 2027. Exact dates and duration will be agreed with the student. Compensation: Unpaid; no stipend. Focus Areas: User and market research, AI workflow analysis, competitive research, product discovery, and feature prioritisation for Dart Browser. Eligibility: Open to all students currently enrolled in a college or university in India, across disciplines and years of study. Recent graduates are also welcome. MBA and Computer Science backgrounds are preferred, but students from other disciplines are welcome. Individual participation only. Entry is free. The Challenge: The AI Opportunity Thesis As AI makes coding, analysis, and execution cheaper and faster, how can it expand opportunities for software engineers and MBA graduates? What must these professionals do to capture the upside and stay ahead of the curve? Write an original essay, case analysis, or structured argument that makes an evidence-backed case for opportunity creation. Do not assume higher productivity automatically means more jobs: explain the mechanisms, acknowledge displacement risks, and distinguish job numbers from the value of work and the ability to create new products or businesses. Thoughtful qualifications and counterarguments strengthen an entry; optimism alone does not. Address These Five Questions: 1. Where Will New Opportunities Come From? Explain at least two mechanisms through which AI could create new demand, products, markets, businesses, or roles. Show the causal chain rather than listing trends. 2. How Will Engineering and Business Roles Change? Address both software engineers and MBA graduates. Identify tasks AI may automate, responsibilities people retain, and valuable combinations of technical, commercial, and interpersonal skills. You may explore one group in greater depth. 3. What Is the Strongest Objection? Present a credible case that AI could reduce hiring or weaken entry-level career paths. Respond with evidence, state your assumptions, and identify what would make you revise your thesis. 4. What Does This Look Like in a Product? Use Dart Browser or another AI-enabled product as a mini-case. Identify: A target user. A painful workflow. An AI-enabled improvement. The human judgment still required. A privacy or reliability tradeoff. A measurable success criterion. Distinguish observed facts from proposals. Access to Dart's private beta is not required. 5. What Should a Student Do Next? Propose a realistic 90-day plan with skills to learn, something to build or test, and measurable milestones. Include specific recommendations for engineers and MBA graduates. Submission Guidelines: One PDF per participant: an essay, case analysis, or structured argument in English. Word Count: 1,200–1,600 words, excluding references and the AI-use disclosure. Include a title and a short executive summary within the word limit. Cite at least three credible sources, linking to primary research or data wherever possible. Distinguish facts from forecasts. Tables and diagrams are welcome. A slide deck or code submission is not required. No purchase, paid AI tool, or Dart Browser account is required. Submission Deadline: November 10, 2026, 11:59 PM IST. Register and submit on Unstop by the deadline. Upload your essay PDF in the dedicated Essay / Case Analysis Submission (PDF) field. Upload your current résumé separately in the CV/Resume field. details_text: All that you need to know about CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon | Defence Intelligence Summit 2027 Are you ready to build solutions that strengthen the future of digital intelligence and security? Shaastra 2027, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras, in collaboration with the CyberPeace Foundation , invites innovators, developers, AI/ML enthusiasts and content creators to participate in the ISR Innovation Hackathon , a flagship competition of the Defence Intelligence Summit 2027. The competition aims to tackle emerging challenges surrounding AI-generated disinformation, deepfakes and digital manipulation through technology and public awareness. About the Competition The hackathon features two tracks: Track 1: Agentic AI Tools (High Complexity) Build the agent that catches the fake. Develop an autonomous AI agent that monitors simulated social media, messaging and video feeds to detect deepfakes and AI-generated disinformation. Your solution should integrate multiple verification techniques, analyse evidence and generate explainable verdicts with confidence levels. Teams of up to 4 members. Submit a PPT/PDF abstract outlining your proposed solution. Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their working agents at the finale. Track 2: Creator Content (Creative Challenge) Make the reel that teaches the trick. Create an original 30-90 second reel, video or carousel that educates audiences on identifying digital manipulation and misinformation. Choose one theme: Emotional Manipulation Fake Experts Impersonation Manufactured Outrage Forward Before You Think Open to individuals or teams of up to 4 members. Entries can be submitted in any Indian language. Shortlisted participants will take on a surprise live creative brief at the finale. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Preliminary Round Submit your AI agent abstract (Track 1) or original social media content (Track 2). Entries will be evaluated on creativity, originality, accuracy and technical feasibility. Round 2: Offline Finale at IIT Madras The top 10 teams from each track (20 teams in total) will be shortlisted and invited to the IIT Madras campus for the finale. Track 1: Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their AI agents live against a fresh simulated multi-platform feed. Track 2: Shortlisted teams will take on a surprise live creative brief on stage. The finalists will showcase their solutions before a distinguished panel of judges from the CyberPeace Foundation and the defence and technology ecosystem. Key Dates Registrations Close: December 7, 2026 (6:00 PM IST) Doubt Clearance Session: December 10, 2026 Round 1 Submission Deadline: December 13, 2026 (6:00 PM IST) Offline Finale: January 3, 2027 Prizes & Recognition A total prize pool of ₹90,000 is up for grabs! 1st Prize: ₹45,000 2nd Prize: ₹30,000 3rd Prize: ₹15,000 Resources & Guidelines Track 1 participants will work with a simulated multi-platform feed. Live platform scraping and real personal data are not permitted. All submissions must be original. Track 1 solutions must operate within the provided sandbox. Track 2 must not use synthetic media depicting real, identifiable people. AI-generated media must be labelled. Political-party content and material unsafe for general audiences are prohibited. Participants below 18 must provide verified guardian consent. Winning technical systems may be required to be open-sourced. Ready to Make an Impact? Whether you're building an AI agent to detect digital deception or creating content to help people recognise manipulation, this is your opportunity to contribute to a safer digital ecosystem. Register now and be part of the CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon at the Defence Intelligence Summit 2027!

details_text: Robo Sumo is where power, precision, and strategy collide! Teams bring their RC-controlled robotic warriors into the sumo arena, where the objective is simple—push your opponent completely out of the ring. The Tech Fest Council reserves the final authority regarding robot eligibility, technical inspection, match decisions, penalties, disqualification, safety, and interpretation of rules. details_text: Moneyball is a football-themed strategy and management event that combines football knowledge, player auctions, squad building, tactical planning, financial management and negotiation. The event consists of a preliminary qualification round followed by an auction, league stage, transfer market and knockout stage. Prize Pool: Rs. 6000 (Winner : Rs. 4000 + Runner-Up : Rs. 2000) Registration Fee: Rs. 200 Date: 10/12/2026 Event Structure: Preliminary Round (Quiz): Teams participate in a football-based quiz conducted through Mentimeter or pen-and-paper format to shortlist the Top 10 Teams . Player Auction: The shortlisted teams participate in a live football player auction and use their allocated purse to construct a squad of 11–15 players . Teamsheet & Formation: After completing the auction, each team submits its final teamsheet along with the formation in which they want their team to play. The organizing team then constructs the corresponding custom teams in EA SPORTS FC. Round 1 (League Stage): All 10 teams compete in a round-robin league format , where every team plays against every other team. Qualification: The Top 4 teams based on their league-stage performance qualify for the knockout stage. The remaining 6 teams are eliminated from the championship. Transfer Market: After Round 1, a transfer market opens. The Top 4 teams can bid for players belonging to the eliminated teams. The bottom 6 teams can negotiate and sell their players to the team offering the best value. Round 2 (Knockouts): The Top 4 teams play two semi-finals followed by the Grand Final using their updated squads after the transfer market. Best Negotiator Award: Among the eliminated 6 teams, the team that finishes the transfer market with the highest remaining purse wins the Best Negotiator Award. Match Simulation: All football matches will be simulated on EA SPORTS FC in CPU vs CPU mode at Legendary/Ultimate difficulty . Participants will not directly control the players during matches. Winner: The winner of the Grand Final will be declared the Moneyball Champion . Event Specific Rules: Each team must consist of 2-4 players . A team leader must be designated as the official point of contact for the team. The preliminary round will shortlist the Top 10 teams for the main event. Each qualified team will receive an equal starting purse for the player auction. Each team must construct a squad consisting of 11–15 players during the auction. Once the auction is completed, teams must submit their final teamsheet and preferred formation . All 10 qualified teams will participate in the Round 1 round-robin league stage . The Top 4 teams after Round 1 will qualify for the knockout stage. The remaining 6 teams will be eliminated from championship contention but will remain eligible for the Transfer Market and Best Negotiator Award . During the Transfer Market, qualified teams may bid for players belonging to eliminated teams. Eliminated teams have the right to negotiate and decide which offer provides the best value for their player. All transfers must be approved and recorded by the organizing committee before being considered official. Once the Transfer Market closes, no further player transfers will be permitted. The Top 4 teams will use their updated squads for the knockout stage. The knockout stage will consist of two semi-finals followed by a Grand Final . All matches will be simulated using EA SPORTS FC in CPU vs CPU mode . Matches will be played at Legendary/Ultimate difficulty , as determined by the organizing committee. Participants will not be permitted to control players during simulated matches. The winner of the Grand Final will be declared the Moneyball Champion . The eliminated team with the highest final purse after the Transfer Market will receive the Best Negotiator Award . Use of unfair means, manipulation of game settings, unauthorized changes to squads or deliberate exploitation of loopholes will result in disqualification. Judges' and organizing

title: GOVERNIA
description: What happens when a well-crafted policy proposal hits an unforeseen real-world crisis? GOVERNIA puts you and your team in the role of rival policy strategists competing to defend opposing economic and governance…
details_text: What happens when a well-crafted policy proposal hits an unforeseen real-world crisis? GOVERNIA puts you and your team in the role of rival policy strategists competing to defend opposing economic and governance frameworks. But winning isn't just about out-arguing your opponent—it's about how swiftly and intelligently you adapt when the ground shifts. No specialist knowledge of public policy or economics is required. The challenge rewards critical thinking, sharp observation, teamwork, and evidence-based adaptability. THE SCENARIO: THE DILEMMA Two opposing economic philosophies clash over public expenditure: Side A defends universal transfers to eliminate exclusion errors, while Side B advocates targeted assistance to conserve public resources. Midway through, a sudden macroeconomic shock forces both teams to overhaul their models under severe fiscal pressure.

title: CASE CLOSED: THE POLICY CRIME SCENE
description: Case Closed: The Policy Crime Scene puts you in the role of a Special Economic Forensics Officer investigating a fictional government programme that has gone wrong. Examine documents, crack codes, analyse financial…
details_text: Case Closed: The Policy Crime Scene puts you in the role of a Special Economic Forensics Officer investigating a fictional government programme that has gone wrong. Examine documents, crack codes, analyse financial records, connect conflicting statements and determine what actually happened. No specialist knowledge of economics or public policy is required. The challenge rewards observation, reasoning, teamwork and evidence-based conclusions. A fictional government programme received an allocation of ₹100 crore to improve school infrastructure. Records show that ₹72 crore was spent, while several schools claim that promised equipment never arrived. Officials maintain that the programme was implemented successfully. Something does not add up. Your mission is to determine: Where did the implementation process break down? Which records contradict one another? What can the evidence establish - and what remains unverified? What is the most defensible explanation for the failure? All figures, documents and allegations are fictional. A discrepancy alone does not prove fraud or establish individual wrongdoing.

title: Glideator
description: Overview The Glideator is a newly ideated event introduced for the first time at Shaastra 2026, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras. This exciting challenge is designed to test the stability, maneuverability,…
details_text: Overview The Glideator is a newly ideated event introduced for the first time at Shaastra 2026, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras. This exciting challenge is designed to test the stability, maneuverability, and control precision of RC gliders as they precisely navigate through a challenging obstacle course. Participants must rely solely on aerodynamic efficiency and pilot skill — without the aid of powered propulsion — to complete the course with maximum accuracy and control. Competition details: Round 0 - Preliminary Submission: 1) Video Demonstration Each participating team must submit a demonstration video showing : The Glider's control surfaces along with their movement while the glider is at rest. The glider has to be thrown from 3 - 5 metres height without any usage of the control surface and is expected to land safely after at least 10 metres distance. Land safely after a designated spot in a square of radius 2m. The video should consist of measuring the vertical and horizontal distance before and after the launch of the glider. This video demonstrates that the glider possesses sufficient control, maneuverability, and has appropriate range. 2) Technical PDF Submission A detailed technical document must be submitted containing: Glider dimensions and total weight along with a photo of the glider. (The dimensions of any other physical components that are used (like a carbon rod used as a spar) are to be mentioned.) Power source and other electronic components' specifications. Control surface dimensions. Thickness of the balsa wood used for the glider Place the photographs as proofs for each aspect mentioned. A hollow chamber of sufficient size should be arranged in the glider for adding weights in round 2. Round 1 — Glide ratio: Launch: Gliders should cover the greatest horizontal distance possible showcasing their aerodynamic efficiency. Teams must ensure their glider maintains a steady, level flight without erratic movements or stalls. In this round the glide ratio of each team's respective glider would be noted when released from a fixed spot. Round 2 — Obstacle Navigation: In this round, the glider should travel as far as it can and Specified landing zones were positioned at 2-meter intervals from the point of release. Teams were awarded additional points based on the zone in which the glider landed, with the condition that the entire glider must be contained within the designated zone to qualify for the corresponding points. Points were given for distance they travelled and also for landing in the specified zones. Additionally, teams were allowed to add weights (About 5gm each) provided by the organizing team to the glider, earning bonus points based on the number of weights successfully added. Rules and Guidelines Type: Glider(Without any propellor) only. Control System: Manual operation using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted. Dimensions: Wing span should be 70 - 75 cm and the other dimensions should be based on the wing span and aerodynamic parameters. Material to be used: Balsa wood of minimum thickness 3mm and maximum thickness 5 mm. Placing of foam or any other material between the balsa wood at wings or the body for strength or extra weight is strictly restricted. Stability & Maneuverability: The glider must demonstrate stable flight, precise low- altitude flight, and agile directional control. The weight of the glider should range between 350g and 500g. A hollow chamber of sufficient size should be arranged in the glider for adding weights in round 2. Important Dates: Registration Start: 28-10-2026 Registration Deadline: 10-12-2026 Main Event on: 03-01-2027 Venue: Student Activity Center (SAC), Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras Please go through the Problem statement attached below for all the details regarding the competition and for the submissions.

title: Roboceana 2027
description: ROBO OCEANA 2027 – Amphibious Rescue & Recovery Event Overview Robo Oceana 2027 challenges participants to design and operate a self-powered hovercraft capable of navigating land and water to complete a simulated…
details_text: ROBO OCEANA 2027 – Amphibious Rescue & Recovery Event Overview Robo Oceana 2027 challenges participants to design and operate a self-powered hovercraft capable of navigating land and water to complete a simulated flood-rescue mission. Teams must retrieve rescue payloads, overcome obstacles, and transport them safely to designated evacuation zones within the allotted time. Competition Structure Round 0 – Demonstration Teams must showcase their hovercraft's design and demonstrate its ability to maintain stability, navigate, and handle rescue payloads. Further submission guidelines will be announced by the organisers. Round 1 – Main Event Teams will operate their hovercraft in the physical arena to complete the rescue mission through the following stages: Land Navigation: Traverse smooth and rough surfaces and enter the water arena through one of two routes. Water Navigation: Avoid floating obstacles and navigate simulated currents while maintaining stability and control. Rescue & Recovery: Collect standard payloads (table tennis balls) and heavy payloads (golf balls). Evacuation: Return to land and deposit each payload in its designated rescue zone. Arena Specifications Land zone with smooth and rough surfaces. Sloped land-to-water transitions. Water zone with floating obstacles and simulated currents. Two entry routes: a short, narrow route with bonus points and a long, broad route. Designated payload collection and evacuation zones. Access gates that gradually close after a fixed duration. Technical Requirements Maximum dimensions: 50 × 40 × 40 cm Maximum weight: 4.5 kg Power: Completely self-powered. Battery: Insulated and securely enclosed. Control: RC operation permitted; physical tethers and external steering assistance prohibited. Rules & Penalties Follow all vehicle specifications and arena constraints. Deposit payloads into their respective rescue zones. Collisions, incorrect sorting, payloads falling outside designated zones, excessive instability, and exceeding payload limits may attract penalties. The team with the highest overall score in the main event will be declared the winner. In case of a tie, rescue efficiency, time performance, stability, and control may determine the final ranking.

title: Aerofloat Shaastra 2027
description: About the Event AeroFloat is an indoor lighter-than-air (LTA) vehicle competition held under the Aero Fest vertical of Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras . Teams will design, build, and fly a remotely controlled blimp .…
details_text: About the Event AeroFloat is an indoor lighter-than-air (LTA) vehicle competition held under the Aero Fest vertical of Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras . Teams will design, build, and fly a remotely controlled blimp . Because blimps operate in a slow, buoyancy-dominated regime that is highly sensitive to control input, the competition tests both piloting precision and real-time combat strategy . Team & Venue Details Team Size: Up to 3 members per team . Participation Model: Open registration with an online technical check . Venue: Indoor venue at SAC Main Hall, IITM . Event Duration: 1 day . Competition Stages 1. Online Qualification Check Every registered team must submit a single continuous, unedited video demonstrating basic flight competency . The video must show an unassisted take-off, controlled climb and descent, controlled yaw, and an unassisted altitude hold with the vertical-thrust motor switched off . This round is evaluated on a pass/fail basis to grant an on-site Day 1 slot . 2. Round 1: Precision Navigation All blimps must pass a Day 1 technical check to ensure they meet limits, it must fit in a box of dimensions 1m * 0.5 m * 0.5m, helium gas only, a custom-built gondola, and a maximum total weight of 800 g . Teams pilot their blimp through a 3D course of up to 10 suspended hoops within a 3-minute time limit . The top 6 teams from the leaderboard advance to the Grand Finale . 3. Round 2: Aerial Combat (Grand Finale) The top 6 teams compete in a bracket-based, single-duel tournament inside a netted arena . The objective is to use a  5 cm standard pin to puncture the opponent's Mylar/BoPET envelope while protecting their own . A duel is won when the opponent's envelope is visibly punctured and loses lift . Key Rules & Requirements Build Rules: Envelopes must be commercially purchased, while the gondola and electronics must be built from scratch by the team . Propulsion & Control: The blimp must use electric motors with propellers and be controlled via a 2.4 GHz RC; autonomous flight is not permitted . Safety: Helium is the only permitted lifting gas; the use of hydrogen will result in strict and immediate disqualification . Combat Conduct: Ramming with the gondola or contacting an opponent's electronics during combat is prohibited and leads to immediate disqualification .

details_text: Overview Where Strategy Meets Product Can you break down a complex business problem, identify the right strategic opportunity, and build a product-led solution that creates measurable business impact? The competition will take participants through three intensive rounds, testing everything from business fundamentals and strategic thinking to problem-solving, product strategy, and executive-level presentation. details_text: Overview: This is a special market prediction challenge where all participants compete on the same 5 Nifty 50 stocks. Week 37 Format: November 2 - 6, 2026 Same 5 companies for everyone. 5 daily predictions. 25 total calls in 5 days. Rankings based on participation and accuracy. No long-form submission is required. Rewards & Benefits: Winner - 1st Rank: 1:1 mentorship with VC founders Internship pathway with IndiaStox Ambassador program Top Performers - Top 3: Achievement certificate Internship pathway with IndiaStox Platform reputation boost Full Completion: Participation certificate Base points reward For users who vote on all trading days How It Works: The challenge runs from November 2 - 6, 2026 The same 5 Nifty 50 companies remain fixed throughout the challenge. Simple Timing Rule: If you vote before 1:00 PM IST, your prediction is for that day’s close and is scored against the previous trading day’s close. Strengthen your resume and interview profile. Earn certificates, badges, and recognition. Unlock mentorship and internship opportunities. Gain visibility with the IndiaStox team. title: Drishti '26 — Article Writing Competition
organiser: Pannalal Girdharlal Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (PGDAV) College, University of Delhi (DU), Delhi
description: About the Competition Ecolibrium, the Economics Society of PGDAV (M) College, presents Drishti '26, its inaugural Article Writing Competition , inviting undergraduate and postgraduate students to examine the forces…
details_text: About the Competition Ecolibrium, the Economics Society of PGDAV (M) College, presents Drishti '26, its inaugural Article Writing Competition , inviting undergraduate and postgraduate students to examine the forces shaping the global economy critically. Centred around the theme “The Economics of Power in the 21st Century”, the competition encourages participants to explore how nations, corporations, institutions and individuals exercise economic influence through trade, technology, finance, resources and labour. The competition aims to foster original thinking, rigorous economic analysis, and informed perspectives on contemporary global developments. Winning entries will be considered for publication in Arthavistaar , Ecolibrium’s annual economics newsletter. 1. Eligibility & Participation Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across colleges and universities. Individual and team submissions of up to two members are permitted. Each participant/team may submit only one article. Inter-college collaborations are allowed. 2. Theme & Choice of Topic Participants may choose a topic within the following themes or combine multiple themes in their article. Trade & the New Globalisation: Tariffs, protectionism, trade wars, global supply chains, reshoring, friend-shoring and shifting patterns of global economic power. The State of War: Economic consequences of armed conflict, military expenditure, inflation, trade disruptions, wartime economies and post-war reconstruction. Economic Warfare: Sanctions, embargoes, export controls and the use of trade, finance, energy and currencies as instruments of geopolitical influence. Technology, AI & Corporate Power: Artificial intelligence, technological competition, Big Tech, market concentration, productivity, employment and the distribution of technological gains. Resources, Energy & the Green Transition: Energy security, critical minerals, resource dependence, the petrodollar system, greenflation and the economics of sustainable development. Labour, Inequality & Economic Security: Wages, labour markets, bargaining power, income and wealth inequality, social protection and the distribution of economic gains. Topics listed above are indicative rather than exhaustive. Articles should demonstrate a clear economic perspective and engage critically with the chosen subject. 3. Article Specifications & Submission Guidelines Word limit: 1,200–1,500 words Language: English Formatting: Times New Roman, 12-point font. Submissions must be in Microsoft Word (.doc/.docx) format. Author details: Include the article title, author(s)’ name(s), college/university, and contact information. File naming: ParticipantName_CollegeName or TeamName_CollegeName Structure: Articles should have a clear title, coherent arguments, appropriate section headings wherever necessary, and a well-developed conclusion. Tables and figures: All tables, graphs, figures, and images must be properly sourced, with due credit given to the original creators. Sources must be clearly cited. Images used in the article must also be submitted as separate, high-resolution files along with the article via email to ensure print quality . Captions and references for visual materials will not be counted towards the word limit. Language and styling: Italicise and explain non-English terms. Bold formatting may be used for emphasis, and superscripts or asterisks must be explained in footnotes. Referencing: APA style referencing is mandatory. All external sources, quotations, statistics, datasets, and borrowed ideas must be properly acknowledged. 4. Originality & Academic Integrity All submissions must be original, independently written, and previously unpublished. Plagiarism, fabricated data, misrepresentation of authorship, and AI-generated content are strictly prohibited. The organising committee reserves the right to verify originality and disqualify entries that violate these requirements. 5. Evaluation Criteria Submissions will be evaluated

title: Call for Papers: The Arthniti 2026-27
description: About: The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by…
details_text: About: The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by undergraduate students of economics and related disciplines. Every year, the journal publishes research on a specific theme, enriching the scope and suggesting a refreshing strand of thought to pick upon by the students every year across the disciplines of Economics, Finance, Political Science, Psychology, Technology, inter alia, and this year The Arthniti invites abstracts on the theme ‘Emergence’. Theme: Emergence is the process by which interactions among simple underlying components can give rise to complex behaviours and structures. Often, the ultimate outcome observed is neither intuitive nor reducible to those individual components. This theme looks at interdisciplinary ideas as emerging concepts that rarely respect the boundaries of a single field. Emergence therefore, is not merely change, but it further examines what change produces. An understanding of these processes is therefore imperative to not only navigating uncertainty but also building systems that are resilient to adapting for what comes next. This year, The Arthniti tries to capture the essence of its theme, ‘Emergence’ through diverse research papers. Instructions: This post is a call for paper submissions, that is, a complete research paper of up to 6000 words (excluding References and the Appendix) has to be submitted for the entry to be considered. The paper submissions have to adhere to the following guidelines: All in-text citations, references, tables figures, and depictions to be in the American Psychological Association (APA) 7 format and accurately numbered. The font must be Times New Roman with font size as 12. The paper must follow the following structure: • Abstract: A summary of the entire study, including the methods, findings and future outlook under 300 words. • Introduction: A brief overview of the background of your research study, a brief outline of the various fundamental elements that constitute the phenomenon you seek to explain. • Literature Review: A comprehensive review of literature surrounding the chosen subject, using any method of review. • Objectives: The various steps/methods/processes used as part of the study in answering the research question, in brief. • Hypothesis: The primary and secondary research questions that the author of the study seeks to answer, including the hypothesised relationship between the variables of the study. • Methodology: An exhaustive overview of the methods, datasets, models, processes that have been utilised in your research paper. • Policy Recommendations (if applicable): Actionable and empirical policy implications of your study. • Limitations: A transparent declaration of the pitfalls that you encounter in the process, or any information that hampers the validity or scope of the claims being made by the study. • Conclusion: A brief summary of the study. Since the journal is ISSN-indexed, all submissions made must be exclusive to The Arthniti, and any duplicate papers will be regarded as plagiarism. The journal maintains stringent academic standards, and any plagiarism or AI-generated textual usage will lead to disqualification of the submission. Note: Please submit your entries through this form link.

INVESTOMANIA is a portfolio strategy challenge that puts your financial acumen, market understanding and investment instincts to the test. Step into the world of equity markets, build your investment thesis, and make strategic decisions in a dynamic financial landscape. From identifying promising companies to analysing sectors and balancing portfolio risks, every decision matters. Go beyond conventional stock picking and demonstrate your ability to turn market insights into a compelling investment strategy. Whether you're passionate about finance, fascinated by the stock market, or simply eager to test your analytical skills, INVESTOMANIA is your opportunity to experience the challenges of managing an investment portfolio. Can you think beyond the numbers and invest your way to the top? Eligibility Criteria Open to all undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students, irrespective of academic discipline. Students from colleges and universities across India are welcome. Teams must consist of 2–4 members. Inter-college, cross-specialisation and cross-year teams are permitted. For detailed competition guidelines, portfolio requirements, submission instructions and the approved company universe, please refer to the attached documents. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Who can participate in Investomania? Investomania is open to all undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students from recognised colleges and universities across India, irrespective of their academic discipline. 2. What is the team size? Each team must consist of 2–4 members. Inter-college, cross-specialisation, and cross-year teams are permitted. 3. What is the investment corpus for the competition? Each team will manage a hypothetical investment corpus of ₹5 crore (±10%). Teams must utilise the full corpus while constructing their portfolios. 4. Which companies can we choose for our portfolio? Teams must select companies exclusively from the approved universe of 110 NSE-listed companies provided by the organisers. The complete company list is available in the attached document. 5. Is there a limit on the number of companies we can include? No. There is no restriction on the number of companies you can select from the approved list. You may adopt either a diversified or a concentrated investment strategy, provided your decisions are logically justified. 6. What is required for the Preliminary Round? Teams must submit a 3-slide presentation outlining their investment strategy. The presentation should cover portfolio allocation, company and sector analysis, investment rationale, and risk-management approach. The cover slide, thank-you slide, and appendix are excluded from the three-slide limit. 7. What is the submission deadline and format? Submissions must be uploaded through the Unstop platform in PDF format (maximum 10 MB) by 13 November 2026, 12:01 AM IST. 8. How will the Preliminary Round submissions be evaluated? Submissions will be evaluated based on: Fund allocation strategy Company analysis Sectoral outlook Data-backed investment decisions Risk-management approach Presentation clarity 9. How many teams will qualify for the Final Round? The top 15 teams from the Preliminary Round will qualify for the offline Final Round. 10. What happens in the Final Round? Shortlisted teams will present and defend their investment portfolios before a panel of judges at Jadavpur University, Kolkata. The final winners will be determined based on the judges' evaluation. 11. When and where will the Final Round take place? The Final Round will be held on 21 November 2026 at Jadavpur University, Kolkata. 12. Where can we find the detailed rules and approved company list? The detailed competition guidelines, submission requirements, and approved 110-company research universe are available in the documents attached to the Unstop listing. Participants are advised to review them carefully before preparing their submiss

title: MindShift - The Science of Decisions
description: Overview: Why do we remember some things and forget others? How does the brain shape our perception, behaviour and decisions? MindShift is a three-round competition exploring neuropsychology, cognition and human…
details_text: Overview: Why do we remember some things and forget others? How does the brain shape our perception, behaviour and decisions? MindShift is a three-round competition exploring neuropsychology, cognition and human behaviour. Through application-based challenges, scientific research and problem-solving, participants will investigate how cognitive processes influence the way we think and interact with the world. Designed for curious minds across disciplines, MindShift encourages scientific reasoning, critical thinking and evidence-based decision-making. No prior specialisation in neuroscience or psychology is required. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from all academic disciplines. Participants may register individually or in teams of 1–4 members. Competition Rounds Round 1: Brain Basics | Online Quiz An application-based quiz covering foundational concepts in memory, attention, perception, learning, cognitive biases and decision-making. Questions will focus on applying concepts to real-world scenarios rather than relying solely on factual recall. A preparatory reference document will be provided before the round, making it accessible to beginners. Round 2: NeuroDesign | Submission Round Shortlisted participants will receive a challenge brief requiring them to approach an unfamiliar neuropsychological problem through scientific reasoning, research and creative problem-solving. Teams must develop a structured response, justify their approach and consider its feasibility within the given constraints. The challenge will run over two days, with detailed instructions, deliverables and evaluation criteria released at the start of the round. Final Round: Offline Finale | IIT Madras The finalists will participate in an interactive, research-driven neuropsychology challenge at IIT Madras on 2 January 2027 . Teams will investigate a neuropsychological condition, explore its underlying mechanisms using credible scientific literature, and develop an evidence-informed solution or intervention concept. Teams will submit their research and proposed approach with appropriate citations and present their findings to a judging panel. Detailed task requirements and evaluation criteria will be shared with the finalists. Evaluation Criteria: Participants will be evaluated on scientific understanding, analytical reasoning, research quality, creativity, feasibility, problem-solving and communication. Detailed, round-specific judging criteria will be communicated to participants. Prizes Total Prize Pool: ₹35,000 Winner certificates will be provided in hard copy. Finalist and participation certificates will be provided digitally. Why Participate? Explore the science behind human cognition, engage with scientific research and tackle challenging problems that go beyond conventional quizzes. Develop skills in research, critical thinking, scientific communication and teamwork while investigating the fascinating relationship between brain function and behaviour. Think critically. Investigate the evidence. Discover the Science of Decisions.

title: Petri Dish Challenge
description: Overview: Beyond the naked eye lies a universe of chaos, beauty, and hidden potential. Are you ready to decode it? The Petri Dish Challenge invites budding microbiologists to identify an unknown bacterial culture using…
details_text: Overview: Beyond the naked eye lies a universe of chaos, beauty, and hidden potential. Are you ready to decode it? The Petri Dish Challenge invites budding microbiologists to identify an unknown bacterial culture using standard microbiological techniques. Participants will explore bacterial isolation and culture, Gram staining, biochemical tests and antibiotic susceptibility testing. They must analyse experimental data, draw scientific conclusions and present their findings clearly. The event consists of an online quiz round followed by an offline laboratory round at IIT Madras. Participants will be shortlisted for the final round based on their performance in the online round. Target Audience: Students interested in: Microbiology and microbial identification Biotechnology and biomedical sciences Wet-lab techniques, bacterial culture and biochemical analysis Experimental reasoning and scientific interpretation Eligibility: Undergraduate and postgraduate students from all disciplines, including engineering, science, medical, arts, commerce, management and law. Format: Round 1: Online Quiz Platform: Unstop Format: Online quiz covering biotechnology, microbiology and microbiology laboratory techniques Structure: Approximately 30–40 questions Dates: December 12-13,2026 Participants must attempt at least one quiz to be considered for qualification to the offline final round. Final Round: Offline at IIT Madras Location: UG Labs, IIT Madras Dates: January 4–5, 2027 Participants will receive an unknown bacterial sample and conduct laboratory investigations, including: Staining and cell morphology, including cotton blue staining Cell count and viable cell determination Antibiotic susceptibility testing and Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) Lactose fermentation and extracellular enzyme activity/synthesis Motility testing and biochemical characterisation The final round includes hands-on experiments, lab report preparation, live presentations and a viva. Evaluation Criteria: Selection and execution of appropriate laboratory tests Accuracy of observations, recordings and interpretation Scientific reasoning and evidence supporting bacterial identification Quality and clarity of the lab report and presentation Performance during the viva examination

Success is judged based on insight, strategy, and logical reasoning, and shortlisted participants get the opportunity to advance to an engaging offline finale . Gear up to challenge yourself, sharpen your investment instincts, and experience the excitement of making real-time financial decisions Eligibility Criteria: Open to all undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students from any discipline. Students from any college or university across India are eligible. Inter-college, cross-specialization, and cross-year teams are permitted

title: NITRO GP
description: NITRO GP is an adrenaline-fuelled, nitro-powered RC car racing championship hosted at Shaastra, bringing together hobbyists, students, and professional racers from across India to enjoy the thrills of navigating…
details_text: NITRO GP is an adrenaline-fuelled, nitro-powered RC car racing championship hosted at Shaastra, bringing together hobbyists, students, and professional racers from across India to enjoy the thrills of navigating challenging turns, ramps, and rugged terrain in a test of speed, precision, and control. The competition celebrates creativity, engineering expertise, technical craftsmanship and sharp reflexes, pushing both the machines and their drivers to their limits. Competition details: VIDEO SUBMISSION: Each team must submit a clear video showcasing their car's composition, functionality, and performance on a test track. The video should highlight that it is a 1:8 Nitro fuel-based RC car which is functional.It must be submitted before the deadline for evaluation and shortlisting. QUALIFIERS: All teams have to go through a 3-lap time trial round. Each driver’s fastest time in this qualifying round will be considered. The Top 16 proceed to the next round and are slotted according to their positions in this round. ROUND ROBIN: The teams are split into 4 groups and race among themselves in the group. The top 2 of each group directly proceed to the next stage, whereas the third-place team of each group goes into a revival round. REVIVAL: The 3rd-place teams race each other where the first-place team also advances to the semifinals. QUARTER-FINALS: 9 teams are seeded and race out of which 6 teams head to the semifinals. SEMI - FINALS: 2 high-stakes races of 3 cars each; the top 2 of each race proceed to the finals. FINALS: Teams that qualify from the semi-finals will advance to the final race. The final race will be of longer duration.Pit stops are available. Grid positions for the final will be based on the number of laps completed in the semi-final (in the given time). Rules & Guidelines: Open only to Nitro fuel-based 1:8 RC buggies; further specifications regarding the cars are mentioned in the PS. Further rules and guidelines are available in the Problem Statement.

details_text: CTF Website Registration All participants must register through the official CTF platform using the link below. CTF Website: https://dead-drop-ctf-six.vercel.app/ About the Event Organized by The Big O, the coding and cybersecurity club of Acharya Institute of Technology, as part of Tech Habba 2026, this Capture The Flag (CTF) competition challenges participants to investigate, analyze, and solve cybersecurity puzzles in a race against time. Compete in a team and explore challenges across web exploitation, cryptography, digital forensics, reverse engineering, OSINT, steganography, and more. Uncover hidden flags, piece together clues, and navigate an unfamiliar digital world through problem-solving, creativity, and technical skills. Whether you're an experienced cybersecurity enthusiast or a beginner curious about ethical hacking, there's a challenge waiting for you! CTF Website Registration All participants must register through the official CTF platform using the link below. CTF Website: https://dead-drop-ctf-six.vercel.app/ Guidelines Eligibility: Open to students from any college. Participation Format: Team-based participation. Team size must follow the limits specified by the organizers. Challenge Categories: Web exploitation, cryptography, digital forensics, reverse engineering, OSINT, steganography, and other cybersecurity-related challenges. Event Duration: Six hours of active CTF gameplay, with a 30-minute break during which the competition will be paused. Schedule: 11:30 AM: Check-in, introduction, and team settlement. 12:00 PM: CTF begins. During the day: 30-minute break; the CTF timer is paused. 6:30 PM: CTF ends and final scores are verified. Identity Verification: All participants must carry a valid college ID card for verification. Requirements: Each team must bring its own laptop(s) and charger(s). Scoring: Teams earn points by successfully solving challenges and submitting the correct flags. Final scores will be verified by the organizers. Rules Punctuality: Participants must report to the venue by 11:30 AM. Late entries will not be permitted. Competition Duration: The CTF begins at 12:00 PM and ends at 6:30 PM, including a 30-minute break during which gameplay is paused. Identity Verification: A valid college ID card is mandatory for every participant. Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptops and chargers. Authorized Targets Only: Teams may attack and investigate only the challenges and systems explicitly provided for the CTF. Attacking other teams, external systems, or the competition infrastructure is strictly prohibited. Flag Confidentiality: Flags and solutions must not be shared outside the registered team or posted publicly until the event concludes. Fair Play: Teams must solve challenges independently. Unauthorized collaboration, plagiarism, or attempts to manipulate the scoring system may result in disqualification. Respectful Conduct: Harassment, abusive behavior, or deliberate disruption of other participants or organizers will result in disqualification. Scoring Disputes: Any concerns regarding challenge validation, flag acceptance, or final scores must be reported to the organizers during the event or before final results are declared. The organizers' decision on scoring disputes will be final.

title: MED Detective - National Medical Case Study Competition
description: Overview Put your clinical reasoning and diagnostic skills to the test at MED DETECTIVE! Analyse medical case scenarios, identify clinical problems, and develop evidence-based diagnoses and management plans.…
details_text: Overview Put your clinical reasoning and diagnostic skills to the test at MED DETECTIVE! Analyse medical case scenarios, identify clinical problems, and develop evidence-based diagnoses and management plans. Eligibility: Medical and allied medical students from first year to final year, graduates, and postgraduate students/candidates. Team Size: Exactly 2 members per team. Competition Process & Format: Round 1: Teams receive a medical case and prepare a PowerPoint presentation within 45 minutes. The PPT is evaluated by judges, without a live presentation. Round 2: The top 8 teams qualify to analyse a new case, prepare a PPT, present their findings, and participate in a viva. Judging focuses on clinical understanding, reasoning, differential diagnosis, investigations, management, evidence quality, presentation, and teamwork. Rules: Teams must have exactly 2 eligible members. Submit the Round 1 PPT between 10:45 AM and 11:00 AM. Medical claims must be supported by credible, verifiable sources. AI tools may support research and brainstorming, but conclusions must reflect independent clinical reasoning. Case confidentiality, academic integrity, punctuality, and professional conduct are mandatory. Judges' decisions are final, subject to the stated tie-breaker rules. Event Details: Date: 27 November 2026 Venue: NIMS University Investigate, analyse, and demonstrate your clinical excellence at NIMS QUEST 2026!

title: Board Room
description: Event Guidelines Boardroom Battle is a business strategy competition at PEC’s E-Summit 2026, where participants step into the roles of company executives to solve a business challenge. Teams act as a company’s…
details_text: Event Guidelines Boardroom Battle is a business strategy competition at PEC’s E-Summit 2026, where participants step into the roles of company executives to solve a business challenge. Teams act as a company’s leadership, balancing strategy, finance, technology and marketing to develop a practical solution and defend it before a judging panel. Event Details Event dates: 14–15 November 2026; the exact schedule will be communicated to registered teams. Mode: Offline. Venue: PEC Campus, Chandigarh. Team size: 3–4 members. Intercollege teams are allowed: Members may belong to different colleges. Competition Format Briefing and Role Allocation: Teams assign executive roles among their members: CEO: Overall strategy and business decisions. CFO: Budgeting, costs and financial viability. CTO: Technology, product development and operational feasibility. CMO: Marketing, customer acquisition and brand positioning. In teams of three, the CEO also handles the CMO’s responsibilities. Case Reveal and Preparation: Teams receive a common business problem, along with relevant information, constraints and a budget. They must analyse the challenge and prepare a solution covering strategy, finances, execution and marketing. Boardroom Presentation: Teams present their proposed solution to the judging panel. Each member explains the decisions relevant to their executive role and responds to questions. Twist Round: Shortlisted teams receive an unexpected change in the business situation, such as a budget reduction, a new competitor or a shift in customer demand. They must revise their strategy and defend their decisions before the panel. Rules and Regulations Team Participation Each team must consist of 3–4 members. Intercollege teams are permitted. A participant cannot register with more than one team. Executive roles must be assigned before preparation begins and remain unchanged throughout the competition. All members must be present for the briefing and participate in the presentation. Teams must report according to the schedule communicated by the organisers. Case Analysis and Preparation All teams receive the same initial problem statement and preparation time. Solutions must address the stated problem and comply with the provided budget and constraints. Teams may make reasonable assumptions where information is unavailable, but must clearly identify and justify them. Financial estimates, projections and calculations must be explained when questioned. Technical recommendations must be understandable and feasible; coding or a working prototype is not required. Teams must develop their solutions independently. Collaboration between teams or assistance from non-participants is prohibited. The policy on internet access and AI tools will be communicated before preparation begins and will apply equally to all teams. Presentation and Twist Round Every team member must contribute to the presentation and be prepared to answer questions related to their role. Presentation format, preparation time and speaking limits will be communicated during the briefing. Teams must submit any required presentation materials by the announced deadline. Only shortlisted teams advance to the twist round. All finalists receive the same twist and equal time to revise their solutions. Revised solutions must address the new constraints and explain the trade-offs involved. Evaluation and Conduct Teams will be evaluated on problem understanding, practicality, financial reasoning, execution, creativity and coordination. In the twist round, adaptability and the justification of revised decisions will also be considered. Plagiarism, fabricated claims presented as facts, misconduct or disruption may result in penalties or disqualification. The judging panel’s decision will be final.

title: Med IQ - Medical Quiz Competition
description: Overview Challenge your medical knowledge, clinical acumen, and quick-thinking abilities at MED IQ! Compete against other teams in an exciting medical quiz designed to test rapid recall, foundational sciences, and…
details_text: Overview Challenge your medical knowledge, clinical acumen, and quick-thinking abilities at MED IQ! Compete against other teams in an exciting medical quiz designed to test rapid recall, foundational sciences, and advanced clinical diagnosis. Eligibility: Students from first year to final year of medical courses, graduates, postgraduates, and healthcare professionals. Team Size: Exactly 2 participants per team. Competition Process & Format: First Round: 30 time-bound medical questions testing medical knowledge, rapid recall, and clinical diagnosis. Final Round: The top 10 teams advance to answer 10 challenging analytical and rapid-fire clinical questions. The final winner is determined through quiz performance and score evaluation. Rules: Each team must have exactly 2 members; individual participation and teams of three are not permitted. Each team must use one designated digital device throughout each round. Switching devices is prohibited unless authorised due to technical failure. Internet browsing, reference books, handwritten notes, additional devices, and outside assistance are prohibited during live rounds. Answers submitted after the official countdown will not be evaluated. Participants must follow the quizmaster's instructions and all event timings. Rule violations may result in disqualification. Event Details: Date: 26 November 2026 Venue: NIMS University Prizes: First Prize: ₹10,000 Second Prize: ₹5,000 Total Prize Pool: ₹15,000 Think fast, answer smart, and prove your medical IQ at NIMS QUEST 2026!

title: Bargain Battles
description: Event Guidelines Bargain Battles is an auction and sales-pitch competition at PEC’s E-Summit 2026. The competition begins with an online quiz round, followed by an offline auction and pitching round for shortlisted…
details_text: Event Guidelines Bargain Battles is an auction and sales-pitch competition at PEC’s E-Summit 2026. The competition begins with an online quiz round, followed by an offline auction and pitching round for shortlisted teams. Teams bid for imaginative fictional products using virtual money and then persuade a judging panel to buy them. From an eraser that removes past mistakes to a watch that pauses time, every product challenges participants to turn imagination into a convincing sales pitch. Event Details Event dates: 14–15 November 2026. Round 1: Online quiz; the schedule will be communicated to registered teams. Subsequent rounds: Offline at PEC Campus, Chandigarh. Team size: 3–4 members. Intercollege teams are allowed: Members of a team may belong to different colleges. Competition Format Online Quiz: Registered teams participate in an online quiz. Shortlisted teams advance to the offline rounds. Briefing and Auction: Qualified teams receive details of the fictional products, including their abilities and limitations. Teams must purchase at least one and no more than two products. Teams that purchase no products are eliminated. Pitch Preparation: Teams receive 25 minutes to develop their sales pitches, covering target customers, benefits, applications and proposed selling prices. Pitch and Negotiation: Teams present their purchased products to the judging panel, followed by questions and negotiation. Teams purchasing two products must pitch both products. Rules and Regulations Team Participation Each team must consist of 3–4 members. Intercollege teams are permitted. A participant cannot register with more than one team. Only teams shortlisted through the online quiz may participate in the offline rounds. All shortlisted team members must attend the offline briefing and participate in the pitching round. Teams must report according to the schedule communicated by the organisers. Online Quiz Teams must complete the quiz within the announced quiz window. The quiz format, duration and participation instructions will be shared before the round. Collaboration between different teams or assistance from non-participants is prohibited. Teams must ensure access to a stable internet connection. Product and Pitch Rules Each team may purchase a maximum of two products and must purchase at least one product to remain in the competition. Teams that do not purchase any product will be eliminated. Teams must pitch every product they purchase: one product if they buy one, and both products if they buy two. Teams may create their own branding, customer segments and applications, but cannot alter or add to the products’ stated powers or limitations. Slides are not required. Teams must prepare their pitches independently; assistance from non-participants is prohibited. All money used in the competition is fictional and has no real monetary value. Misconduct, disruption or violation of the rules may result in disqualification.

Imagine stepping into a corporate boardroom where critical decisions must be made, challenges arise without warning, and every individual appears to be working toward a common objective. As situations evolve and uncertainty grows, participants must rely on their observation, strategic thinking, communication, and decision-making abilities to navigate the boardroom. Will you recognize the warning signs before it's too late? Can you distinguish a genuine ally from someone quietly influencing the outcome?
