details_text: Date of Event : 20 November 2026 Pitching Requirements PITCHING REQUIREMENTS Team Size 1–4 participants Eligibility Students of Classes 9–12 with valid school/student identification Format Live pitch to a panel of judges Mandatory Document A completed Business Model Canvas covering all nine building blocks Visual Aids (optional) Presentation of up to 8 slides, printed canvas, poster, or simple prototype Equipment Teams bring their own files and materials. KEY ACTIVITIES What must you do to deliver your idea? VALUE PROPOSITIONS What problem do you solve, and why is your solution better? CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPS How will you win and keep customers? Teams will pitch in the order drawn by the organizers. A team that is not ready when called may lose its slot or be disqualified. The pitch should clearly explain the problem, the target customers, the proposed solution, and how the idea can grow into a sustainable business. Each team has a maximum of 6 minutes to pitch, followed by up to 4 minutes of questions. Teams that exceed the time limit may be stopped by the judges and may receive a score deduction. All team members should take part in the pitch or the question-and-answer session. Teams may use a presentation of up to 8 slides, the printed canvas, posters, or a simple prototype as visual aids. Teams must bring their own files and equipment. Teachers, mentors, and parents may not speak for, prompt, or assist the team during the pitch or the question-and-answer session. Ideas must be appropriate for a school-level event. Ideas that are illegal, harmful, hateful, or unsafe are not permitted. Ideas remain the property of the presenting team. Teams should avoid sharing confidential details they are not comfortable discussing in public. Copied content, plagiarism, or deliberately false claims may lead to disqualification. The team with the highest total score will be declared the winner. If scores are tied, the team with the higher Business Model Quality score ranks first, followed by Innovation & Originality. The judges' decision will be final and binding. Judging Criteria: CRITERIA WHAT JUDGES LOOK FOR Problem & Customer Understanding A clearly defined problem and a well-understood target customer. Innovation & Originality A fresh, creative idea developed by the team. Business Model Quality A complete, logical canvas where all nine blocks fit together. details_text: Get ready for an exciting battle of engineering, strategy, and robotic power at ROBO SUMO, one of the thrilling technical competitions of KAUSHALYA 2.0, the annual festival of CSVTU University Teaching Department, Bhilai. Robo Sumo is a competitive robotics challenge in which participants put their engineering skills, creativity, and strategic thinking to the test. The objective is to build and control a robot capable of defeating its opponent in a designated sumo arena by pushing it outside the competition boundary while maintaining its own position within the arena. Participants will experience an exciting combination of robotics, mechanical design, electronic systems, control mechanisms, and real-time decision-making. Competition Highlights Head-to-head robotic battles. Test your robot's strength, stability, and maneuverability. Demonstrate engineering and problem-solving skills. Compete against talented participants from different institutions. General Rules & Guidelines Participants must follow all technical specifications announced by the organizers. Robots must be designed to compete safely within the designated arena. Participants must follow the instructions provided by event coordinators. Any attempt to damage an opponent's robot intentionally or interfere with the competition may result in disqualification. Participants must maintain discipline and follow fair-play practices. The decision of the organizing committee and judges will be final. Important Information Detailed information regarding team size, robot dimensions, weight restrictions, power supply, control mechanisms, match duration, competition format, and scoring criteria will be announced by the organizing team. Join ROBO SUMO at KAUSHALYA 2.0 and showcase your engineering skills in an exciting battle of robots!

title: AdVenture
description: About AdVenture AdVenture is a three-round marketing and brand strategy competition conducted as part of Strategia 2027. The event places participants in the role of an advertising and marketing agency, challenging them…
details_text: About AdVenture AdVenture is a three-round marketing and brand strategy competition conducted as part of Strategia 2027. The event places participants in the role of an advertising and marketing agency, challenging them to develop, defend, and adapt a campaign for a real product from a real brand. The competition tests participants’ ability to understand consumers, identify market opportunities, think creatively, and make strategic decisions under pressure. Across three progressively challenging rounds, teams will develop a campaign strategy, respond to a marketing crisis affecting the same brand, and defend their decisions in an undisclosed live finale. Focus Areas Consumer Insight Brand and Market Relevance Creative Thinking Strategic Thinking Problem Diagnosis Who Can Participate? Any undergraduate (UG) or postgraduate (PG) student currently pursuing their education is eligible to participate. Team Size and Format Team Composition: 2 members. Solo entries are not permitted. Event Format: 3 rounds. Preliminary Rounds: 2 online rounds. Final Round: Offline. Rounds and Competition Structure Round 1: Pulse Check: The Brief (Online) The real product and brand for the case will be announced at the beginning of the round. Teams must develop a campaign concept for the given brand. Participants must submit either a slide deck (PPT/PDF) or a single poster, strictly following the format specified in the round brief. The highest-performing teams, with the number to be announced, will advance to Round 2. Round 2: The Red Alert: Crisis (Online) Teams will receive a marketing crisis or product-related problem connected to the same brand and case used in Round 1. The crisis may involve a public relations setback, declining brand relevance, a repositioning requirement, or a failed product launch. Teams must diagnose the problem and develop a revamped marketing brief containing: Problem Diagnosis and a Fresh Strategic Direction Key Messaging and a Proposed Course of Action This round evaluates the ability to respond to unexpected challenges, rethink campaign strategies, and propose practical, relevant solutions while maintaining brand alignment. Round 3: The Full Throttle (Offline) The final round will be an undisclosed surprise challenge, revealed only when the round begins. Finalists must think on their feet and defend the campaign developed in Round 1 and the crisis response developed in Round 2 before the judging panel. This round tests strategic clarity, adaptability, confidence, and the ability to justify marketing decisions under pressure. The AdVenture Challenge AdVenture goes beyond conventional marketing exercises by challenging participants to think like real-world brand strategists. From building a compelling campaign to navigating a brand crisis and defending their decisions in a live finale, teams must demonstrate creativity backed by strategic reasoning. Bring your ideas, challenge conventions, and prove that you can turn a brand brief into a winning strategy. AdVenture: Brand. Buzz. Boom.

description: About the Opportunity TEJAS Udbhav - Tribal Innovation & Impact Programme is a special initiative under the TEJAS Initiative of the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Mumbai. The programme aims to identify, encourage…
details_text: About the Opportunity TEJAS Udbhav - Tribal Innovation & Impact Programme is a special initiative under the TEJAS Initiative of the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Mumbai. The programme aims to identify, encourage and support promising ideas and innovations that address challenges faced by tribal communities across India. The programme invites tribal youth, students, entrepreneurs and young changemakers/innovators to present innovative solutions that can contribute to inclusive development, community empowerment and sustainable impact. Applicants with ideas addressing challenges in areas such as education, healthcare, technology, environment, culture, tourism and community development are encouraged to apply. The programme seeks startup-oriented business ideas with the potential to evolve into viable, sustainable and scalable ventures, as well as existing startups at the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) or revenue-generating stage. Proposals should demonstrate a clear problem, a feasible business solution and the potential for measurable social and economic impact. Who Can Apply? The programme welcomes applications from: Tribal innovators. Students. Entrepreneurs. Young changemakers and innovators. Ideas addressing challenges faced by tribal communities across India are encouraged. Applicants should demonstrate the relevance of the problem, the innovative nature of their solution and its potential for meaningful impact. Applicants may apply with an early-stage business idea having startup potential or an existing startup that has reached the MVP or revenue-generating stage. General ideas or social initiatives without a viable business or startup model will not qualify. Areas of Innovation Applications may focus on, but are not limited to, the following areas: Education: Improving educational access, learning opportunities and outcomes. Healthcare: Addressing healthcare accessibility and community well-being. Technology: Developing innovative technological solutions to practical challenges. Environment: Promoting environmental sustainability and responsible resource management. Culture: Preserving and promoting tribal heritage, traditions and indigenous knowledge. Tourism: Developing responsible and community-oriented tourism opportunities. Community Development: Strengthening livelihoods, local capabilities and inclusive development. Application Process and Timeline Stage 1: Online Application Interested applicants must submit their applications through the designated online application platform by 5 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST . Applicants should clearly explain the problem they seek to address, their proposed solution, its innovative aspects and the potential impact.

details_text: Official Competition Guidelines Theme: The Things We Don’t Question Organized Collaboratively by: D-LAB, Design Community (IISER Berhampur) with Art Clubs of Other IISERs Overview & Thematic Brief: We navigate daily life governed by unexamined habits, systemic norms, invisible social defaults, and unquestioned cultural agreements. ARTICULATE invites designers to interrogate the familiar challenging viewers to pause, reflect, and ask critical questions about the everyday realities we take for granted. The Theme: The Things We Don't Question: The Things We Don’t Question: Use the medium of graphic design to explore an assumption, belief, behaviour, practice, or system that has become so familiar that we rarely stop to question it. Your poster should make the familiar feel unfamiliar, something that makes people pause, think, and question what they usually take for granted. ARTICULATE invites thinkers, illustrators, graphic designers, and creative minds across India to disrupt this visual complacency. Your artboard is an analytical instrument to surface hidden paradoxes, challenge accepted defaults, and construct visual metaphors that make viewers reconsider their everyday assumptions. Thematic Scope & Satirical Commentary / Critiques: Prohibition on Use of Direct Personalities & Real-World Entities’ Identities. Critique must remain systemic, structural, and conceptual. Use allegory, generic archetypes, visual metaphors, and symbolic representation rather than literal real-world identities. Submissions must maintain ethical design standards, completely avoid personal attacks, hate speech, or defamation, and channel their visual commentary into universal, thought-provoking ideas. Design Specifications & Technical Requirements: Format & Dimensions: Submissions must be exactly A4 size (portrait orientation recommended). Quantity: One original poster submission per registered participant. Thematic Alignment: Every submission must demonstrate a rigorous, creative, and critical interpretation of the theme, The Things We Don't Question. Submission Deliverables: Participants must compile and submit all three mandatory deliverables via the official registration portal: High-Resolution Poster Image: One export in JPG, JPEG, or PNG format (minimum 300 DPI recommended). Source / Editable Design File: The original editable working file in PSD, AI, SVG, or other industry-standard formats. For designs authored in Canva, an unrestricted editable or template share link must be provided. Portfolio & Concept Document (PDF): A single PDF containing: A full-page high-resolution preview of the poster. A structured written rationale (up to 250 words) articulating the conceptual premise, creative methodology, design iterations, and social or moral values reflected within the artwork. Mandatory Social Engagement & Verification: To ensure transparent public exhibition and complete validation of participation, entrants must fulfill all of the following steps prior to the deadline: Follow @design_iiserbpr on Instagram. Post the finalized poster on Instagram as a Collaborator Post with @design_iiserbpr. Include the concept rationale / artist statement within the post caption or in the post itself. Tag the following institutional and partner accounts in the caption: @design_iiserbpr @artclub_iisertirupati Note: Collaboration acceptance and tagging of all partner entities are compulsory requirements for jury review. Prizes & Rewards (Total Prize Pool: ₹10,500) The competition offers a comprehensive prize pool valued at ₹10,500, distributed across direct cash rewards, Amazon gift vouchers, and official honors: Overall Prize Pool: ₹10,500 (inclusive of Cash Prizes & Amazon Gift Vouchers). 1st Place (Winner): ₹3,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence 2nd Place (First Runner-Up): ₹2,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence 3rd Place (Second Runner-Up): ₹1,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence Special Mentions (3 Positions): ₹500 eac

details_text: MOLEQUEST Case Challenge is a competition for people who love to read, think and connect the dots. Teams (1-4 members) will dive into biological puzzles, work out what’s happening at the molecular level, and build solutions that hold up when the evidence takes an unexpected turn. The event is structured in three rounds, each one testing a progressively deeper layer of scientific competence: conceptual knowledge, analytical depth and real-time adaptability. The theme is Epigenetics. So, think like scientists and find what the epigenome is hiding. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students Target Audience: Students interested in Epigenetics and Genomics Molecular Biology Biotechnology Biochemistry Biomedical Engineering Plant and Agricultural biotechnology Competition Rounds: Round 1: Online Quiz This quiz will test grasp of basic molecular biology and epigenetics fundamentals, the toolkit you will need to crack the cases ahead. Be prepared to think fast and be sharp to earn your place in the next round. Round 2: Submission Round In this round, teams will be given a set of cases. Teams pick one of the cases, study the data provided, and submit a written report, answering the questions given in the case document. Finals at IIT Madras: Offline Round Teams arrive with a prepared PPT based on their Round 2 work and will be given a sealed envelope revealing new findings. They are then given 1 hour to rework their PPT adding any changes in their reasoning. They should then defend their Round 2 report and explain what changes and doesn’t change in their reasoning because of the new information to a panel of judges.

details_text: All that you need to know about Robo Run Guidelines: A team shouldn't contain more than 5 members. Bot Dimensions:  Smaller than 20 * 20  cms. Participants are required to build an autonomous (not to be operated by a remote controller) line follower Bot, which can reach the end point of a maze in the shortest possible time. ( The line thickness will be 3-4 cm) Video submission round: This will be a submission round! You will have to prepare a small maze with two curves and show your line-following bot running on it. Shoot a video clip and attach the file. Round -1: In round 1, every team will be given a chance to run through the maze. The top set of teams will be qualified to final round. Shortlisting will be done based on the points you acquire. Refer to the problem statement for scoring criteria. Round -2: In round 2, the maze will additionally contain yellow blocks (10cm*10cm*10cm) directly placed on top of yellow squares. These yellow blocks are to be displaced from the square. The sqaures will act as a checkpoint only if the block is displaced completely. The maze and scoring pattern will be different between the two rounds. Robo Run Description: A Bot shall not be larger in length or width than 20 cm. There are no restrictions on the height of a Bot. A Bot should essentially comprise a drive motor to move it; a steering and turning method; sensors to detect the maze turns; sensors to ignore the action of the rest Bots and a source to provide power. A Bot shall be self-contained (no remote controls). A Bot shall not use an energy source employing a combustion process. Required sensors may be used for identifying the block and the maze line. A Bot shall not leave any part of its body behind while navigating the maze. A Bot shall not jump over, fly over, climb, scratch, cut, burn, mark, damage, or destroy the line of the maze. Judges can debar any machine if it is likely to cause damage to the maze in any way. Important Dates: Registration Start: 28-10-2026 Registration deadline: 01-12-2026 Video submission round deadline: 15-12-2026 Main Event on: 06-01-2027, Venue: Student Activity Center (SAC) , Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras

title: AetherHack
description: AETHERHACK – National Ideathon INNOVISION 2026 | NIT Rourkela Technology Beyond the Horizon: Aetherhack is the national ideathon of INSPIRE, the Science and Research Club of NIT Rourkela, held as part of INNOVISION…
details_text: AETHERHACK – National Ideathon INNOVISION 2026 | NIT Rourkela Technology Beyond the Horizon: Aetherhack is the national ideathon of INSPIRE, the Science and Research Club of NIT Rourkela, held as part of INNOVISION 2026. It gives college students across India a stage where original ideas are heard, questioned, and mentored by professors. Submit a written abstract online, and the top 10 teams move on to pitch live at the offline finale. Themes: Sustainability: Clean energy, waste management, and resource-smart solutions. Robotics: Machines, automation, and assistive systems that solve real problems. Healthcare: Accessible, affordable, and assistive health-tech. Open Track: Any bold idea that does not fit the themes above. Eligibility : • Open to any college student from any institute across India. • Registration is only through the AetherHack page on Unstop. • Each team may submit only one idea. • All team members must attend the offline finale and represent the team. • Finalists must carry a valid college ID card to the finale. Competition Structure: Round 1 – Launch (Online, Unstop) Teams submit one written idea abstract in PDF format. The abstract must state the theme, the problem, the proposed solution, how it works, and its expected impact, within a maximum of 2 A4 pages. Abstracts are screened on innovation, feasibility, and impact, and the top 10 teams are shortlisted and informed through Unstop and email. Round 2 – Orbit (Offline, INNOVISION Finale) Ten finalist teams compete at NIT Rourkela during INNOVISION, and all members of each team must be present and represent the team. Each team pitches the idea shortlisted in Round 1 for 7 minutes, followed by a 3-minute Q&A with the professor panel. Timings are strict. Slides are optional, and demos or prototypes are welcome but not required. Sponsorship & Innovision Registration: INSPIRE will sponsor one participant from each finalist team. All other team members must register separately on the official INNOVISION website to attend. Judging Criteria: • Innovation (25): Originality of the idea and approach • Feasibility (25): Technical soundness and a realistic path to build it • Impact (25): Relevance to the theme and value to real users • Pitch & Q&A (25): Clarity of the pitch and quality of answers Rules & Guidelines: Register only through the official AetherHack page on Unstop. Submit one abstract in PDF format before the deadline. Late, incomplete, or non-PDF submissions are not considered. The idea must be your own work. Copied or plagiarised abstracts are disqualified. Finalist teams must pitch the idea shortlisted in Round 1. Switching to a different idea is not allowed. All team members must attend the offline finale and represent the team. Only one participant per finalist team is sponsored by INSPIRE. Remaining members must register on the INNOVISION website. Report to the venue by the announced reporting time. A no-show forfeits the slot. Bring your slides (if any) along with a backup copy. Any breach of these rules can lead to disqualification at any stage. The decisions of the judges and the INSPIRE organising team are final. Registering for AetherHack means you accept the rules. Rewards & Support: Prize Pool: ₹5,000, shared among all winners (the split is announced at the finale) 3-day INNOVISION experience for winners Mentorship and support from professors to develop your idea further Sponsorship for one participant from each finalist team, arranged by INSPIRE Recognition at a national-level student ideathon

title: Treasure Restoration
organiser: Great Lakes Institute of Management (GLIM), Gurgaon
description: Treasure Restoration Find the forgotten. Fuse the familiar. Create the future. What if yesterday’s failed products could become tomorrow’s breakthrough innovations? Every discontinued product has a story, and every…
details_text: Treasure Restoration Find the forgotten. Fuse the familiar. Create the future. What if yesterday’s failed products could become tomorrow’s breakthrough innovations? Every discontinued product has a story, and every unsuccessful idea holds the possibility of a comeback. Treasure Restoration challenges you to uncover that hidden potential, combine forgotten products, and transform them into innovative concepts with real market potential. This is your opportunity to think creatively, solve problems, and prove that a product’s story doesn’t have to end when it leaves the market. Round 1: The Quiz Test your analytical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills through set of questions: Qualifying participants will advance to the next round. Round 2: The Product Redesign Challenge One forgotten product. One fresh idea. A second chance at success. Choose any one legacy/commercially matured tech innovation (for eg: Pendrive, Landline telephone, CD's, Cassette, etc) of your choice and redesign it into an innovative product concept that offers a unique value proposition and demonstrates real market demand. But there’s a twist: you must choose one target age group and consumer archetype that you would like to target from the below options given below while redesigning your product. Target Age Group: Option 1: Gen Z (aged 14-29 years) Option 2: Gen X (aged 46-61 years) Target Consumer Archetype: Option 1: Value Seekers- those that look for maximum benefits at a reasonable price. Option 2: Premium Spenders- those that are willing to pay more for quality, experience and innovation. Your submission: PPT deck of up to 5 slides Submit your PowerPoint deck on Unstop. Make every slide count! Slide 1: Title slide: Your new product’s name, logo, and tagline. Slide 2: The Legacy & The Opportunity - Identify the original technology and it's purpose, highlighting its limitations, and explain the opportunity to reinvent it for today's market. Slide 3: The Product Reimagined - Showcase the redesigned product through a sketch, digital mockup, 3D render or AI-generated visual.Highlight its key features and technological innovations.Explain its unique selling proposition. Slide 4: Target Audience & Commercial Feasibility- Identify your intended customers, their needs, and the problem your product solves and the pricing strategy. Propose a price and explain why it is reasonable. Slide 5: Go To Market Strategy for your product. Your concept will be evaluated on creativity, relevance to the condition chosen, customer value, feasibility, pricing, and marketing potential. The top teams will qualify for Round 3. Round 3: The Restoration Pitch You’ve built the idea. Now, test whether people believe in it. Shortlisted teams must submit a 30-60 second AI-generated advertisement demonstrating the product concept, its key benefits, and its appeal to the target audience. This round will assess: Creativity: Present your redesigned product in an original and memorable way. Understand Your Audience: Tailor your advertisement to the chosen age group and consumer archetype. Tell a Compelling Story: Capture attention and communicate your message effectively with AI-generated advertisement. Important Guidelines: Follow the condition assigned to your team throughout Round 2. The Round 2 PPT must contain no more than 5 slides . The Round 3 video must be 30-60 seconds long . Obtain permission before recording or using another person's feedback. Explain how both original products contribute to your final concept. Ensure that your proposed pricing and feasibility are supported by reasonable assumptions. Follow the submission deadlines and instructions announced by the organisers. The mission: Don't just bring products back. Restore their purpose, reinvent their value, and give forgotten ideas a future. Are you ready to turn yesterday’s failures into tomorrow’s treasures?

title: Synergy '26: Orion Case Study Competition
description: Overview CRUX – Consulting & Research Undertaking Club at XLRI is proud to present Orion 2026, the flagship case study competition of Synergy 2026, XLRI’s annual fest. Designed to challenge aspiring consultants and…
details_text: Overview CRUX – Consulting & Research Undertaking Club at XLRI is proud to present Orion 2026, the flagship case study competition of Synergy 2026, XLRI’s annual fest. Designed to challenge aspiring consultants and future business leaders, Orion provides a platform to apply strategic thinking, analytical rigor, and creative problem-solving to real-world business challenges. About Orion 2026 Orion 2026 invites participants to step into the shoes of consultants, dissect complex business problems, and develop innovative, data-driven, and actionable solutions. The competition aims to test participants’ ability to structure ambiguous problems, formulate strategic recommendations, and translate ideas into practical business plans that deliver measurable impact. Competition Structure The competition will follow a three-round format, progressively testing participants’ knowledge, analytical abilities, and communication skills. Round 1: Business Quiz Teams will compete in a quiz designed to test their business acumen, analytical thinking, and understanding of business concepts. The top-performing teams will advance to the next round. Round 2: Case Study Submission Qualified teams will receive a real-world business case and be tasked with developing a comprehensive solution. Teams must submit a single-slide (one-pager) summarizing their problem diagnosis, key insights, strategic recommendations, and implementation roadmap in a concise, visually compelling format. Round 3: Case Presentation The top-performing teams will present their solutions to an esteemed jury during a virtual presentation. Each team must prepare a 4 slide presentation and will have 10 minutes to present, followed by a 3-minute Q&A session to showcase their analytical depth, strategic recommendations, and ability to communicate and defend their ideas effectively. Judging Criteria Submissions and presentations will be evaluated on the following parameters: Quality of Solution Practicality and Feasibility Presentation Skills Communication Skills Why Participate? Orion 2026 is an opportunity to challenge conventional thinking, collaborate with talented peers, and tackle business problems that demand more than textbook solutions. Bring your analytical mindset, strategic perspective, and innovative ideas to the table for a chance to earn recognition and win exciting rewards. Think strategically. Solve boldly. Create impact.

title: Prometheus X Next: The ProdMan Case Competition
description: Overview Prometheus ‘26 is a product management competition built around one idea: every great product starts as a spark, a user pain nobody has solved yet. Over three stages, participants test their instincts, frame…
details_text: Overview Prometheus ‘26 is a product management competition built around one idea: every great product starts as a spark, a user pain nobody has solved yet. Over three stages, participants test their instincts, frame the problem, and then forge a full solution. There is no stage and no panel to impress in person. The whole competition runs online, so it comes down to the quality of your thinking on paper. Wear your PM hat, take on a real-world product problem, and see how far your fire carries. Competition Outline: Round 1: Spark (Online Quiz) - Do you think like a PM? A 20-minute MCQ quiz covering product management, product strategy, metrics, UX, and tech fundamentals. Round 2: Forge (Problem Framing Deck) - Shortlisted teams receive the case statement and submit a 2-slide deck giving a sharp overview of the problem. No solution is expected at this stage. Round 3: Flame (Full Solution Deck) - Finalists build on their Round 2 framing and submit a complete, in-depth solution to the same case. General Rules and Regulations: The entire competition is online, with no in-person stage or panel. All work must be original. Copied content or unsourced figures may lead to disqualification. Only publicly available data may be used. Confidential information obtained through employment, internships, or personal contacts must not be used. Claims and figures should be backed by reliable public sources, and assumptions should be stated clearly. AI tools may be used to assist your work but must be disclosed in the submission. Teams remain fully accountable for the accuracy of everything they submit. A participant cannot be part of more than one team. The decisions of the organisers and judges will be final. The organisers reserve the right to modify dates or rules. Any updates will be communicated through Unstop.

title: Xposure'26
description: XPOSURE'26 - National Photography Competition Hosted by: PRISM (Public Relations, Information and Social Media Committee), IMT Ghaziabad See What Others Miss. Capture What Others Can't. XPOSURE’26 returns to celebrate…
details_text: XPOSURE'26 - National Photography Competition Hosted by: PRISM (Public Relations, Information and Social Media Committee), IMT Ghaziabad See What Others Miss. Capture What Others Can't. XPOSURE’26 returns to celebrate the power of photography and the stories captured through the lens. This national-level competition invites participants from across the country to explore their creative vision, interpret the world around them and present their perspectives through photographs. What is XPOSURE? XPOSURE is an annual photography competition that brings together individuals who see the world in different ways. It encourages participants to experiment with their perspectives, find meaning in everyday moments and turn ordinary scenes into compelling visual narratives. Every photograph offers a glimpse into the photographer’s imagination, making XPOSURE a space where unique viewpoints find expression. Theme for XPOSURE’26: “Beyond the Palette” “Beyond the Palette” focuses on capturing a single, vibrant colour against a neutral or black-and-white background. Explore how one colour can stand out, transform a scene and tell a story through contrast. General Rules: Entries : Each participant may submit only one photograph, original or edited. AI-generated images are not allowed. File Format : JPEG, JPG or RAW. File Size : Minimum 0.5 MB and maximum 20 MB per photograph. Recommended Dimensions : 1000 × 1000, 1350 × 1080, 1080 × 1350, 1920 × 1080 or 1080 × 1920 pixels. Authenticity : Participants must submit the original source file, including metadata, to verify the photograph’s originality. Editing Restrictions : Watermarks, borders, excessive post-processing and AI enhancement are not permitted. Submission Guidelines : Originality : All submissions must be original and reflect the participant’s individual creativity. Copyright : Participants must own the rights to their work or have proper authorisation from the copyright holder. Consent : Clear consent must be obtained from identifiable individuals featured in the photograph. Legal Compliance : Entries must comply with applicable laws and respect intellectual property and personal rights. Disqualification Criteria: Entries may be disqualified if they: Violate applicable laws or contain defamatory content. Promote hate speech or violate community standards. Are intended primarily for commercial advertising. Depict harm to any person, animal or property. Important Date: Submission Deadline : 4 November 2026 Waiting for the perfect moment? What if the perfect moment is waiting for you? Pick up your camera, capture your vision and let your story unfold at XPOSURE’26! title: Mantravat - The Flagship Case Competition

details_text: Mantravat is a case study competition (strategy-based) organised by ConsultU,Consulting and Strategy Club of IIM Udaipur, in which students from across the country can showcase their consulting skills and compete against the best minds. The competition will last three rounds and will put all participants' diverse skill sets to the test. At the end of each round, the shortlisted teams will be invited to participate in the subsequent rounds. Round 1: Strat Hunt A quiz that demands a broad analytical mindset and primarily revolves around consulting frameworks and aptitude Round 2: Case Crunch Challenge Teams that advance from the initial round will move on to the second round, where they will be presented with an actual case study challenge provided by a global company. In this phase, teams will be required to thoroughly assess the case and submit their recommendations through a PowerPoint presentation Round 3: Consult Finale Teams that successfully make it through the second round will progress to the final stage, during which they will present their comprehensive case solution to the jury via an online platform. Rules and Guidelines: The competition is open to all students pursuing postgraduate and undergraduate degrees No participant should be a member of more than one team A team can have 3 to 4 members Only one response per team will be entertained You cannot modify your answer post-submission In the event of a dispute, the organizer's and judging panel's decisions shall be final Details of individual rounds: The competition is divided into three rounds , with the first round consisting of a quiz that requires general analytical thinking and is primarily focussed on developing sustainable solutions. The shortlisted teams from round one will compete in the second round, which will feature a real case study problem statement from a global firm. Shortlisted teams from the second round will advance to the final round, where they will present their complete case solution to the Jury. title: Follow The Money: Innovation Challenge Powered by PayU
description: All that you need to know about Follow the Money: Innovation Challenge Powered by PayU Official WhatsApp: https://chat.whatsapp.com/DqZ5BeA0Pd19FODfbdppFI The Follow the Money: Innovation Challenge is a national…
details_text: All that you need to know about Follow the Money: Innovation Challenge Powered by PayU Official WhatsApp: https://chat.whatsapp.com/DqZ5BeA0Pd19FODfbdppFI The Follow the Money: Innovation Challenge is a national innovation competition organised by the Centre for Software and Information Technology Management (CSITM), IIM Bangalore, in partnership with PayU . The challenge invites students from all disciplines to tackle a real-world problem in digital payment security and financial fraud, and to develop innovative, practical solutions that bridge technology, business, policy and human behaviour. Every day, fraudsters find new ways to slip past the systems built to stop them. What if the next solution came from you? Problem Statement: The Bakery That Takes Bets Payment providers onboard thousands of new merchants every day. Some use genuine documents to open accounts, then use them to collect money for banned activities such as illegal betting. How can a payment provider detect and respond to when a merchant's transactions stop matching the business it claims to run, without penalising honest merchants whose sales change for valid reasons? **Full problem statement with background is available in the rulebook.** Eligibility: • Open to college students from all disciplines across India • Team size: 1–4 members per team • Inter-college teams are allowed • Each student may be part of only one team Competition Structure: Round 1 – Online Submission Teams must submit a presentation deck of up to 8 slides (PDF) describing their solution and a video of up to 2 minutes explaining their solution. The video can take any creative format. Submissions will be evaluated on problem understanding, innovation and originality, solution design and approach, feasibility and real-world impact, and presentation and communication. The top teams will advance to the on-campus finale. Round 2 – On-Campus Grand Finale Finalist teams will be invited to IIM Bangalore on 26 November 2026 to present their solutions at a live exhibition. Each team will showcase its solution at its own stall, through a pitch, poster and demo or walkthrough, as judges visit each stall to evaluate the ideas and interact with the team. Displaying a working prototype is mandatory for technical solutions. The event will conclude with the announcement of winners. Note: Finalists must arrange and bear their own travel and accommodation expenses for the on-campus event. Check out the rulebook attached for more details. Submission Requirements: Each team must submit a single Google Drive folder link containing: • Presentation (PDF, up to 8 slides), named TeamName_Presentation.pdf • Video (up to 2 minutes), named TeamName_Video Folder requirements: • Name the folder with your team name, e.g. TeamName_FollowTheMoney • Set the folder's sharing access to "Anyone with the link can view" • Submit only the folder link on Unstop before the Round 1 deadline • Do not edit or add files to the folder after the deadline Presentation requirements: • Maximum length: 8 slides, submitted as a PDF. • Should cover your idea and what makes it distinctive, how the solution works, how it addresses      fraudulent activity, how it could be implemented in practice, and its expected impact. • Should be clear, well structured and easy to follow Video requirements: • Maximum length: 2 minutes • Any creative format, such as a short film, mock advertisement, scenario-based demonstration, animation, storytelling piece or product pitch. Technical teams must also build and demonstrate a working prototype. • Should clearly explain or demonstrate the solution (Optional) • GitHub repository (for technical solutions) • Supporting documents, such as a policy draft, process flow or business model (as a PDF in the folder.) Evaluation Criteria: Solutions will be assessed on: • Problem Understanding • Originality of Idea • Solution Design and Approach • Feasibility • Real-World Impact • Presentation Quality Use of AI: AI tools

title: Capital Quest
description: About the Opportunity Capital Quest is a finance competition organized by Finomina, the Finance Club of IIM Udaipur , as part of Solaris, IIM Udaipur’s Annual Management Fest. The competition tests participants’…
details_text: About the Opportunity Capital Quest is a finance competition organized by Finomina, the Finance Club of IIM Udaipur , as part of Solaris, IIM Udaipur’s Annual Management Fest. The competition tests participants’ analytical thinking, logical reasoning, and financial decision-making through puzzles and portfolio creation. Open to B-School students across the country, it gives participants a chance to apply practical finance concepts and investment skills in a competitive setting. Guidelines: Team Size: 2 members. No changes in team composition will be allowed after registration closes. Participants must follow the submission requirements for each round. All submissions must be the team’s original work. Any form of plagiarism, malpractice, or unfair means will lead to disqualification. Structure and Rounds: Round 1: Puzzles & Aptitude Test Format: Logic and Aptitude Puzzles. Task: Participants will solve a set of logic and aptitude puzzles testing clarity of thought, reasoning ability, and speed. Progression: Top scorers will qualify for Round 2. Round 2: Portfolio Formation Part 1: Portfolio Creation Virtual Capital: ₹100 Crore per team. Task: Teams will allocate the given capital across a set of assets provided by the organizers. Submission: An Excel sheet containing the available assets and their fixed prices will be shared. Teams must enter the amount they wish to invest in each asset and submit the completed sheet. Cash Holding: Teams may keep a portion of the ₹100 Crore as cash for use in Part 2. Objective: Build an optimal and diversified portfolio focusing on growth potential, valuation accuracy, and risk balance. Part 2: Portfolio Rebalancing Task: Teams will revisit and optimize their original portfolio based on updated market conditions and asset prices. Original Portfolio: Teams must first re-enter their previous portfolio with the same assets and capital allocation to view its performance. Reallocation: Teams can reallocate up to 40% of their initial portfolio value , excluding unallocated cash. Changes Allowed: Teams may fully or partially sell previously held assets or add new securities. Rationale: Teams must submit the reasoning behind both their initial investment decisions and their portfolio reallocation in the dedicated sheet. Final Results: Results will be based on asset prices at a cutoff date and time communicated separately. Evaluation Criteria: Teams will be evaluated based on predefined criteria including portfolio diversification, valuation accuracy, risk balance, and returns. Rules: Participants must follow all timelines and submission requirements. Late submissions will not be accepted. Participants must arrange the required internet connection, system, and other technical requirements in advance. Plagiarism, malpractice, unfair means, or external help during quiz or proctored rounds will result in disqualification. All portfolio submissions must be the team’s original work. Teams must follow the specified submission format, including Excel/Sheets for portfolio allocation and PDF/Word wherever applicable. Incomplete or corrupt files will not be evaluated. All official communication will be through the registered email IDs or event platforms. Teams are responsible for regularly checking updates and instructions. Queries should be raised well before the respective deadlines. The decision of the judges and organizers will be final and binding. Requests for re-evaluation will not be entertained. Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and decorum throughout the event.

title: Vitt Sangram
description: About the Opportunity Vitt-Sangram is a finance competition organized by Finomina, the Finance Club of IIM Udaipur , as part of Solaris, IIM Udaipur’s Annual Management Fest. The competition tests participants’…
details_text: About the Opportunity Vitt-Sangram is a finance competition organized by Finomina, the Finance Club of IIM Udaipur , as part of Solaris, IIM Udaipur’s Annual Management Fest. The competition tests participants’ financial knowledge, analytical skills, and strategic thinking through three rounds covering financial concepts, equity research, valuation, and presentation. Guidelines: Team Size: 1 to 4 members. No changes in team composition will be allowed after registration closes. Participants must follow the timelines and submission requirements for each round. title: Gambit 2035: The Great Power Game
description: How the Game Works Leverage Points (LP) Leverage Points are the primary in-game currency. Each nation begins with a different level of power and has a different maximum possible LP score. Final performance is therefore…
details_text: How the Game Works Leverage Points (LP) Leverage Points are the primary in-game currency. Each nation begins with a different level of power and has a different maximum possible LP score. Final performance is therefore measured relative to each nation's own maximum potential, keeping the competition balanced across nations. Secret Agendas Every nation receives a confidential objective that can earn bonus LP. Your Secret Agenda may force you to pursue an objective that conflicts with your nation's obvious interests, creating an additional layer of strategic decision-making. Treaty Registry If it isn't registered, it isn't real. Only agreements submitted through the official Treaty Registry are enforceable. Promises made in private chats are cheap talk unless backed by a registered agreement. PNN: PiE News Network The PNN will deliver breaking developments throughout the game. Expect market shocks, diplomatic leaks, surprise events, rival moves and changing conditions through Discord and Solaris Instagram Stories. Day 1 Scoring Game Performance: 50% Diplomatic Cable: 50% Advancement: The winner of each world + the 4 highest-scoring runners-up advance. 12 teams advance to Day 2. Day 2 Scoring Game Performance + Secret Agenda: 40% Crisis Report: 60% Top 3 teams from each world advance. 6 finalists reach Day 3. Day 3 Scoring 2035 Accord: 30% Summit Address: 40% Press Conference: 30% Participation Team Size: 2 to 3 members Maximum Teams: 48 The 48 teams will be divided into 8 worlds, with 6 nations in each world. If registrations exceed the cap, participants will be shortlisted through a 20-minute entry quiz covering game theory and geoeconomics. WHY PARTICIPATE? GAMBIT 2035 isn't a conventional case competition. You won't receive a case and simply present a solution. You will create the case yourself through your decisions. You will have to: Make decisions with incomplete information Negotiate with competing interests Build and break alliances Understand incentives React to unexpected shocks Quantify economic consequences Read your rivals Apply game theory in real time Defend your decisions under pressure In GAMBIT 2035, there is no fixed solution. There is only the move you make and the world it creates. Enter the game. Shape the world.

details_text: Overview Organised by FINAX and NEXT, XLRI Delhi-NCR , Tollgate: The Monetisation Mandate is a finance case competition that challenges participants to develop a sustainable monetisation and growth strategy for PhonePe. AI tools and other analytical tools may be used but must be disclosed in the submission. Teams remain fully accountable for the accuracy of all figures and claims. Originality and Confidentiality: All submissions must be original work. Confidential information obtained through employment, internships, or personal contacts must not be used. details_text: Competition Description Step into the world of strategy, business, and decision-making, where every choice has consequences and every move can create an opportunity. This competition challenges participants to think critically, understand market dynamics, and make strategic decisions under pressure. Combining a knowledge-based quiz with an immersive bidding and brand-building challenge, it tests both conceptual understanding and practical business acumen. Participants will progress through two rounds, moving from testing their knowledge and reasoning to applying their skills in a competitive business simulation. Think strategically. Bid wisely. Build intelligently. Round 1: Online Quiz The first round is an elimination-based online quiz designed to assess participants' knowledge, logical reasoning, analytical thinking, and decision-making abilities. The quiz will feature a diverse mix of questions covering business and economics concepts, marketing psychology, consumer behaviour, logical reasoning, and real-world business scenarios. Participants will be required to go beyond theoretical knowledge, interpret situations, identify patterns, and choose appropriate solutions under time constraints. Format: 20 questions 30-minute duration Multiple-choice, logical reasoning, and scenario-based questions No negative marking One attempt per team Performance in this round will determine qualification for the next stage. Round 2: The Bidding Challenge The second round takes participants into a competitive business simulation where strategic thinking, resource allocation, and calculated decision-making become essential. Teams will receive a fixed amount of virtual capital and compete to acquire business assets through a bidding process. Each asset offers distinct advantages and trade-offs, requiring participants to balance their ambitions with their available resources. Using their acquired assets, teams must develop a viable business, establish their market positioning, and demonstrate how their resources work together to create a competitive advantage. The challenge extends beyond bidding, requiring teams to justify their decisions, manage constraints, and respond strategically to unexpected market developments. The objective is not simply to acquire the most expensive assets, but to make intelligent investments and build a business capable of succeeding in a competitive market. Teams will be evaluated on their strategic decisions, resource management, business viability, adaptability, and overall performance. Rules and Regulations Participants must register in teams of 3–4 members. Each participant may be part of only one team. Qualification for the offline round depends on performance in the online quiz. Each team is permitted one quiz attempt, submitted by a designated team member. The online quiz must be completed within the stipulated time and in a single sitting once started. No negative marking will apply to the online quiz. Shortlisted teams must participate in the offline round according to the instructions provided by the organisers. During the bidding challenge, teams must operate within their allocated virtual capital. Borrowing and transferring credits between teams are not permitted. Teams must comply with the bidding rules, asset-acquisition requirements, and evaluation criteria communicated before the offline round. Any misconduct, plagiarism, or use of unfair means may result in disqualification. Participants must carry a valid college ID for the offline round. The organisers' and judges' decisions regarding evaluation and competition outcomes will be final and binding.

description: Overview ECOGEN 2026 is a nationwide B-school case competition designed to challenge students with authentic business challenges viewed through an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework. Organised at IMT…
details_text: Overview ECOGEN 2026 is a nationwide B-school case competition designed to challenge students with authentic business challenges viewed through an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework. Organised at IMT Nagpur, the competition brings together participants to demonstrate strategic foresight, analytical depth, and effective communication. The journey begins with an online assessment of foundational ESG knowledge, moves to the analysis of a short business case, and culminates in a live presentation of strategic solutions before an industry professional. Why Participate? Solve realistic ESG dilemmas faced by Indian and global companies. Build skills in strategy, sustainability, and stakeholder analysis. Present your recommendations before industry professionals at the grand finale. Compete for cash prizes and certificates. Strengthen your profile through participation in a national-level B-school competition. Eligibility Open to all MBA/PGDM students across India. Team size: 2–3 members. Intra-college and cross-specialisation teams are allowed; teams must be from the same college. A valid college ID is required for verification. One participant may be part of only one team. Competition Structure The competition consists of three rounds. Teams will first complete an online ESG quiz. Shortlisted teams will then analyse a mini case and submit a concise recommendation deck. Finalists will present their strategic solutions before an industry jury at the grand finale. Round Details Round 1 – ESG Quiz (Online) An objective quiz covering ESG concepts, frameworks, regulations, and current business-sustainability news. Topics may include GRI, SASB, TCFD, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs). The quiz will contain 45 questions to be completed in 30 minutes. There is no negative marking. Round 2 – Mini Case Challenge (Online) Shortlisted teams will receive a 1–2 page ESG case with data exhibits. Teams must submit a recommendation in a deck of no more than 5 slides, in PDF format, within 36 hours. Submissions will be evaluated by a panel of judges. Teams should identify the core problem, analyse stakeholders, compare options and trade-offs, recommend a course of action, and outline risks and implementation steps. Round 3 – Grand Finale (Offline/Online at IMT Nagpur) Finalists will present their solutions live before an industry jury. A new case will be released one day before the competition. Each team will have 10 minutes to present, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A. Travel and accommodation will not be provided. Guidelines Round 1: Quiz Guidelines The quiz will be hosted on Unstop. Attempt limit: one attempt per team, or per member as decided by the organisers. Use only one device per participant and keep the quiz tab in focus. Tab switching may lead to disqualification. In the event of a tie, the time taken will be used as the tiebreaker. External assistance and AI tools are prohibited during the quiz. Round 2: Mini Case Submission Guidelines Submit a maximum 5-slide deck in PDF format. The deck should cover problem identification; key stakeholders and their interests; options considered and trade-offs; the final recommendation; and risks with an implementation plan. Use relevant ESG frameworks and quantify your analysis wherever possible. Plagiarism or AI-copied content will lead to disqualification. Round 3: Grand Finale Guidelines Finalists must carry a valid college ID for the campus event. Travel and accommodation arrangements are the responsibility of participants. details_text: The Commerce Society of Kirori Mal College presents Mark to Market : The Arbitrage Principle, a high-stakes valuation simulation where sharp analysis is your greatest asset and every decision comes at a price. In a market where perception can be misleading and information can change everything, you are handed one challenge: identify what an asset is truly worth before the rest of the market catches on. Step into a world where every asset holds a different promise and every valuation carries a risk. From uncovering the nature of unfamiliar investments to decoding market signals, weighing competing financial attributes, and navigating a live auction, you will work with limited capital, incomplete information, and very little room for error. Here, one wrong assumption can distort an entire valuation, an inflated bid can drain your purse, and an overlooked opportunity can cost you the win. Across a journey of analysis, negotiation, and strategic decision-making, your choices will shape the outcome. You must interpret the market, assess the value beneath the surface, and decide when to commit and when to hold back. This is a test of financial understanding, commercial instinct, and the ability to make calculated decisions under pressure. Will you recognise an undervalued opportunity, or pay a premium for an asset the market has already overrated? Details will be revealed in time. All you need to know is that price and value are rarely the same, information is never the whole picture, and the smartest move is not always the highest bid. Your greatest tools will not just be your calculations, but your judgment, your adaptability, and your ability to read the room. Think like an analyst, bid like an investor, and know the worth of what others overlook. Every assumption, every alliance, and every bid will decide whether your portfolio becomes a masterstroke or an expensive mistake. details_text: The EO Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (EO GSEA) is the premier event for student entrepreneurs worldwide. Student entrepreneurs compete against their peers from around the world in a series of local competitions to qualify for the EO GSEA Global Finals. EO GSEA is an Entrepreneurs’ Organization (EO) program. EO Mumbai chapter is bringing this opportunity to the student community in India. Structure: Application-based screening: The applications received will be filtered out on the basis of the information provided and the top shortlisted individuals will move ahead for the further rounds. EO Mumbai Finals: Shortlisted student entrepreneurs will be participating in the EO Mumbai Finals. Global Finals: All the Finalists from different clusters will then compete in the Global Finals for the ultimate battle. Prizes and Rewards: EO Mumbai Round: INR 5,75,000 EO Global Finals: USD 100,000 (plus a Paid International Trip for all finalists) Eligibility criterion to compete in the Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (GSEA): You must be enrolled for the current academic year in a university/college as an undergraduate or graduate student at the time of application. Full-time enrollment is not required; part-time enrollment is acceptable. You must be the owner, founder or controlling shareholder of your student business. Each company can be represented by only one owner/co-founder - studentpreneur. Your student business must have been in operation for at least six consecutive months prior to the application. Your business must have generated US $500 or received US $1000 in investments at the time of application. You should not have been one of the final round competitors from any previous year’s GSEA Global Finals Competition. The competitor must be 18-30 years of age. Note : Graduate students are eligible to apply only if they have continually enrolled in a university following their undergraduate degree and have not left school to work on their business or to seek other employment. Exceptions can be made for students who have taken up to one academic year off before beginning their postgraduate education.

details_text: Event Description: Pixel2Path is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build a robot that turns digital images into physical drawings on paper, with no human intervention. It combines Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Path Planning, Robotics, and Mechatronics. Online Submission: The teams have to submit the 'Documentation', 'BOM', and 'Video-Demonstration' of the bot. (Non-Eliminatory Round) Round 1 : The robot receives an unseen image (PNG/NPY), processes it, plans an optimized path, and draws it on an A3 sheet within the allotted time. Round 2 (Draw) : Each team gets an image with 40% of its strokes randomly removed. Their trained AI model predicts the missing strokes, and the robot draws the completed image (visible and predicted strokes) on A3 sheet. Round 2 (Predict) : Teams get 10 unseen masked images and predict the originals. Each is scored by SSIM. Teams get 100 image pairs two weeks before the event. On event day they get the full 5,000-pair dataset and a 60-minute window to train their model on Kaggle. Rules: Teams must have 3 to 5 members, with one designated Team Lead for official communication. Teams must bring a fully assembled and tested robot (no on-day mechanical builds), a laptop with all software pre-installed, the trained model weights file, a 12V DC power supply, and a USB cable for Arduino. It must be a 3-axis plotter (X, Y, and a Z pen-lift) with independent control of each axis. The robot must have an Emergency Kill Switch that completely stops all motion. Training must be done in a Kaggle Notebook on event day with GPU acceleration, with Internet toggled OFF. Training must be from scratch, using only the provided 5,000-image dataset. Data augmentation is allowed.

title: EconoNations
organiser: Shaheed Bhagat Singh Evening College (SBSEC), University of Delhi (DU), New Delhi
description: Overview Negotiate. Strategise. Shape the Global Economy. What if you were responsible for running an entire country's economy? Could you manage scarce resources, navigate global crises, negotiate trade deals, and…
details_text: Overview Negotiate. Strategise. Shape the Global Economy. What if you were responsible for running an entire country's economy? Could you manage scarce resources, navigate global crises, negotiate trade deals, and secure economic growth while protecting your nation's interests? EconoNations is an economics-based simulation competition that places participants in the role of national policymakers navigating an interconnected global economy. Through strategic resource trading, negotiations, and responses to changing global developments, teams must make decisions that shape their country's economic performance and long-term prospects. The competition combines economic reasoning, international trade, resource management, geopolitical strategy, and decision-making in a dynamic simulation of the global economy. Structure Round 1: The Economics Quiz Format: Quiz | Elimination Round The competition begins with an economics quiz designed to test participants' understanding of economic concepts, international trade, global affairs, and their real-world applications. Participants will be assessed on their conceptual clarity, analytical thinking, and awareness of the economic forces shaping the world. Objective: Shortlist the 12 qualifying teams that advance to the next stage. Round 2: Nation Allocation and Economic Setup Format: Country Allocation | Strategy Formation The 12 qualifying teams will be assigned countries through a random allocation process. Each team will represent its assigned nation and receive an initial economic profile consisting of resources, financial capacity, and other economic strengths and limitations. Teams must study their country's starting position, identify its comparative advantages and dependencies, and formulate an initial strategy for navigating the global economy. Round 3: The Global News Simulation Format: Three News Rounds | Negotiation and Resource Trading This is the core of EconoNations. Across three rounds, teams will respond to changing global developments that influence resource availability, market demand, trade relations, and economic priorities. Each round will introduce a new news event or global economic situation. Teams must interpret its implications, identify the resources and economic relationships that become more important, and negotiate with other countries to secure their national interests. During each round, teams will have a limited period to negotiate trade deals, exchange resources, manage their financial capacity, and adapt their strategies to the evolving global environment. Every decision carries consequences. A resource that seems less valuable today may become essential tomorrow, while excessive dependence on another country could leave a nation vulnerable to sudden disruptions. Objective: Build a resilient and competitive economy through strategic negotiation, efficient resource allocation, and the ability to adapt to changing global conditions. Final Round: The Future of Nations Format: Strategic Presentation | 4 Minutes per Team The final round moves beyond immediate trading decisions and challenges teams to think about the future of their economies. Each team will deliver a four-minute presentation outlining its country's future economic strategy, based on the position it has built throughout the simulation. Teams should explain how they intend to utilise their available resources, develop economic opportunities, establish strategic international relationships, and strengthen their country's long-term economic prospects. The presentation should demonstrate forward-thinking economic reasoning, a clear understanding of resource interdependence, and the ability to connect present decisions with future outcomes. Objective: Evaluate each team's long-term vision, strategic thinking, and understanding of how resource management and international economic relationships can shape national development.

details_text: Overview Think Strategically. Bid Wisely. Build Solutions. Can you solve a state's most pressing challenges with limited resources, strategic decisions, and economic reasoning? State Craft Challenge is an economics-based case competition that puts participants in the role of policymakers responsible for addressing real-world challenges faced by Indian states. From managing resource constraints to making strategic investments, teams must think critically, allocate resources efficiently, and develop practical solutions under a limited budget. The competition combines economic knowledge, case-study analysis, auction-based resource allocation, teamwork, and presentation skills in an engaging simulation of policymaking. Structure Round 1: The Economics Quiz Format: Online Quiz | Elimination Round The competition begins with an economics quiz designed to test participants' understanding of economic concepts, current affairs, and their practical applications. Participants will be assessed on their conceptual clarity, analytical thinking, and ability to connect economic principles with real-world situations. Objective: Identify the 12 qualifying teams that advance to the next round. Round 2: The State Challenge Format: Case Study + Resource Auction + Presentation The 12 qualifying teams will enter the main competition, where each team will be assigned an Indian state through a chit-based allocation system. Each team will receive a case study outlining a specific problem faced by its assigned state. The challenge could involve issues such as unemployment, inadequate infrastructure, agricultural distress, water scarcity, industrial development, or other socioeconomic concerns. Teams must analyse their case, identify the key challenges, and determine which resources are essential to developing an effective solution. The Resource Auction Participants will then compete in an auction to acquire the resources required to address their state's challenges. Working within a limited budget, teams must decide which resources to prioritise, how much to bid, and how to allocate their available funds efficiently. The auction will test strategic thinking, resource management, decision-making, and the ability to balance competing priorities. The Solution Presentation After the auction, each team will present its proposed solution, explaining how the resources acquired will be used to address the assigned problem. Teams should demonstrate the feasibility of their recommendations, justify their resource allocation decisions, and explain the expected economic and social impact on their state. Prizes 1st Prize: ₹4,000 2nd Prize: ₹2,500 3rd Prize: ₹1,000

details_text: Overview Design an AI-powered urban flood forecast system that Gurgaon's civic body could actually implement — and present it to the officials who can. About the Competition SustainX 2026 is a Delhi NCR inter-institutional hackathon hosted by the Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development at Great Lakes Institute of Management, Gurgaon, as part of the 5th International Winter Conference on Sustainable Business (WCSB 2026). WCSB is one of Great Lakes Gurgaon's flagship events, bringing together researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders each December to examine the intersection of Business and Sustainability. This year's conference theme is "Beyond Automation: AI, Human-Centricity, and Sustainability" — and SustainX is its student-facing counterpart: a solution-focused hackathon designed to turn that theme from conference panels into actionable civic solutions. The Problem We're Solving Every year, MCG releases a 'flood preparedness plan.' Every year, the same underpasses flood, and the same roads become rivers. On September 1, 2025, 133mm of rain in four hours caused a 20km traffic jam and a 51-hour power outage across the city. By late June 2026, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) had completed desilting at just 16 of 36 hotspots against a May 31 deadline with monsoon already underway. MCG has identified 159 waterlogging hotspots across Gurgaon. It has no system that predicts which of them will flood before the rain arrives. This year's SustainX 2026 asks one focused question: Can you design an AI-powered predictive flood management system for Gurgaon that MCG can actually build and operate? Why Participate The judging panel will include officials from Gurgaon's civic administration. Solutions that demonstrate genuine implementability — technically credible, operationally feasible, and grounded in how MCG actually functions — will be formally presented by GLIM-G to civic stakeholders as a policy brief. This is one of the few student competitions where your solution has a realistic path from a slide deck to a government briefing room. Who Should Participate This problem sits at the intersection of analytics, urban infrastructure, civil engineering, public policy, environmental science, and business strategy. We actively encourage interdisciplinary teams. You do not need to be from a business management background, you need to understand the problem and design something that works. Every year, the same underpasses flood, the same roads become rivers, and the same residential sectors report basement damage. No. Teams must choose one of the following industries: aviation, electric two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, or consumer electronics. Is the Excel model compulsory? No. However, judges may use it to verify your buffer model, so preparing it is recommended. Can we use AI tools? Yes. AI tools are permitted, provided their use is disclosed on the data trail slide. Every number must have a valid source. Do slide limits include the cover and data trail slides? No. The cover slide and data trail slide are excluded from the slide limit. Teams may also include up to three appendix slides. Will the final round be online or offline? The format of the final round will be confirmed and communicated later. Whom should we contact if we have questions? Contact details will be provided by the organisers.

details_text: goSTOPS Marketing Case Study – The Road Less Booked ₹30,000 prize pool | Internship opportunities | Real-world marketing challenge What would it take to get young travellers to book a place they wouldn't normally consider? The challenge Option 1: goSTOPS Kasol PLUS The property is located outside Kasol's main market, away from the route most travellers typically follow. How would you turn its offbeat location and mountain views into a reason to book? Option 2: goSTOPS Alibaug Alibaug is often seen as a destination for villa stays and premium weekend trips. details_text: The Last Smartphone — A National Product Case Competition Organised by: Product Management Club, Masters’ Union About the Event What happens when the smartphone becomes obsolete? Welcome to The Genesis , a national-level product management case competition that challenges students to imagine the future of human–technology interaction in the year 2050. In a world where smartphones have disappeared, cybernetic interfaces combine spatial awareness, total memory, instant recall, and agentic intelligence to transform how humans live, learn, work, and connect. But with these advancements come critical questions about privacy, autonomy, accessibility, and the ethical boundaries of technology. As a founding product team, your challenge is to design a cybernetic-interface product that genuinely improves human life—not merely keeps people connected. Identify a real human need, build an innovative product experience, map the technological investments required to make it possible, and define what your product will refuse to do. The Genesis brings together aspiring product managers, innovators, and future founders to solve one of the most exciting product challenges of tomorrow. Competition Structure The competition consists of three rounds , taking teams from an online live quiz to product development and finally to an offline grand finale at Masters’ Union, Gurugram. Round 1: Signal vs Noise — The Live Quiz Mode: Online | Live and Proctored Explore the future of augmented reality, cybernetic interfaces, brain–computer interfaces, and agentic AI through a live, timed quiz. Watch curated clips showcasing futuristic technologies, real-world innovations, and dystopian possibilities. Answer questions testing visual recall, technological awareness, product judgment, and second-order thinking. Compete in timed quiz rounds designed to reward observation, reasoning, and quick decision-making. The top 30 teams advance to the next round. Duration: 45 minutes Round 2: Build the Interface — The Product Challenge Mode: Online | 10-Day Challenge The top 30 teams will receive a unique Seed Constraint defining a specific user, location, and limitation. Teams must use this constraint to design a cybernetic-interface product experience for 2050. Choose one of the following tracks: Body & Longevity: Rethink health, wellness, and human longevity. Mind & Memory: Explore memory, recall, learning, and the right to forget. Learn & Work: Redesign how humans acquire skills and perform work. Access & Ability: Build inclusive technology that expands human capabilities. City & Movement: Reimagine urban mobility, personal safety, and everyday living. Connection & Play: Explore new dimensions of human connection and shared experiences. Submission Requirements: Product Deck: A PDF presentation of up to 12 slides covering the target user, problem, product experience, key use case, roadmap, business model, ethical safeguards, and success metrics. Team Video: A 2–5 minute video in which every team member appears on camera and explains the solution. Decision Log: A one-page document outlining three important decisions the team reconsidered, what changed their perspective, and the final choices they made. Optional Prototype: A clickable prototype, concept film, physical mock-up, or working demonstration can earn up to 5 bonus points. Teams will be evaluated on human impact, product thinking, innovation, feasibility, ethics, scalability, and ownership of their decisions. The top 8 teams will qualify for the Grand Finale. Round 3: The Dais — The Grand Finale Mode: Offline | Masters’ Union Campus, Gurugram The top 8 teams will present their solutions before a jury comprising experienced product leaders, founders, deep-tech investors, accessibility experts, and industry professionals. title: AI & Analytics: From Prediction to Decision

details_text: Overview Build an AI-supported business or system that can withstand the consequences of its decisions. The AI & Analytics track at CaseUnion 4.0 explores how technology can address difficult operational and access problems. The submitted case pack contains four challenges. The Fraud War Room Redesign a bank or payment service provider’s UPI fraud detection and investigation workflow over a 90-day planning horizon. Connect detection to response, prioritise investigation and explain the tradeoffs between missed fraud and incorrectly flagged customers. The Marketplace That Fixed the Wrong End Design a claims-first AI health insurtech. Choose and defend a business model, explain the claims workflow and model its unit economics. Address human review, false rejections, appeals and hospital gaming. The Mandi Decision Design an AI advisor that helps smallholder farmers decide whether to sell, store, transport or contract-sell their harvest. Define the crops, states, delivery channels and revenue model. Model economics at a scale of 100,000 farmers and address the downside when recommendations fail. The Justice Gap Build a focused AI legal services company around one user group, one problem and one business model. Define the role of AI and licensed professionals, select two deployment states and establish a path to break-even within 24 months. Submission Expectations Follow the requirements of the assigned case. Explain the product or system, data requirements, operational workflow, economics and risk controls. Rules Clearly distinguish case inputs, external evidence and assumptions. Justify the relevant tradeoffs and specify where human oversight is required. Process, Format and Eligibility The final case allocation or selection process, rounds, team size, eligibility, deadlines and submission format will be announced in the competition instructions.
