details_text: Overview What happens when a promising business cannot access capital because nobody can measure its risk? Quantico, the FinTech Club's case challenge at CaseUnion 4.0, asks participants to identify an unquantified risk that prevents an industry, sector or group of people from accessing debt or equity funding. Your task is to design a FinTech solution that quantifies, reduces or works around that risk, making it sufficiently understandable for capital to move. The Challenge Identify a specific risk and establish why it blocks funding. Design a mechanism that addresses it using financial instruments, data, technology, human operations or a combination of these. Submission Requirements Your submission must cover: The risk, the affected group, supporting evidence and market size. The solution mechanism, stakeholders and their incentives. Required data sources and operational processes. The business model and potential to reach institutional scale. Applicable regulators, laws and guidelines, including any changes your solution would require. Rules The risk must be genuinely unquantified, rather than simply an underserved opportunity. Incremental improvements to established lending or payment categories do not meet the brief. New data sources and non-technology operations are permitted. Participants may explore solutions beyond current regulatory constraints, but must explicitly identify the regulatory implications. Clearly state assumptions and cite external evidence. Process, Format and Eligibility Round details, team size, eligibility, deadlines and submission format will be announced with the final competition instructions.

title: Marketing in the Age of AI

details_text: Case Union 2026 – The Strategy In a world where everyone can create more with AI, what can a brand truly own? Case Union 2026 , The Marketing Society’s flagship national case competition hosted by Masters’ Union, challenges participants to build an AI-first marketing strategy for an iconic Indian brand that strengthens its differentiation, consumer relationships and long-term competitive advantage. The Challenge Identify how AI is reshaping the brand’s competitive landscape and where it is vulnerable to imitation. Uncover authentic consumer insights and brand truths through primary research. Develop a distinctive, repeatable brand experience, ritual, cultural property or community that competitors cannot easily replicate. Define where AI should contribute and where human judgment must remain in control. Build a feasible, measurable and commercially viable strategy with clear costs, returns and success metric. The round carries 20 marks, with one mark per correct answer and no negative marking. Whether you are a student looking for internships, a fresher searching for your first opportunity, or a professional building industry connections, having a strong and authentic personal brand can significantly strengthen your professional journey. About: The Lok Sabha or House of the People is the lower house of the Parliament of India. Members of the Lok Sabha are elected by direct election under universal adult franchise. As of 2024, there have been eighteen Lok Sabhas elected by the people of India. The Constitution limits the Lok Sabha to a maximum of 552 members. This includes up to 530 members representing states and up to 20 members from Union Territories. Each Lok Sabha is formed for a five-year term. Normally, after five years, it is automatically dissolved. It can be extended by a proclamation of emergency. If this happens, the term may be extended for one year. It can be extended more than one time. The 18th and current Lok Sabha was formed in May 2014.

The teams will then enter a simulated BRICS summit where they will negotiate, collaborate, debate and defend their country's interests around one central idea: Can BRICS reshape the global financial system through de-dollarization? Teams will be required to negotiate and work towards a common agenda or action plan that addresses the central issue. The summit will conclude with the teams attempting to reach consensus and pass a final resolution with the required majority of participating countries. This isn't just a debate. It is a simulation of international diplomacy where every decision, alliance and negotiation can influence the final outcome. We will also conduct one networking track so that all participants can connect with each other and make new friends and connections. What Will You Do? Represent a BRICS member country and understand your country's economic and geopolitical interests Develop a position on de-dollarization and negotiate with other countries Build strategic alliances/Defend your country's interests Participate in diplomatic discussions and negotiations and Present your final strategy and proposed framework Respond to challenges and developments introduced during the simulation What Skills Will You Test? Go beyond textbooks and experience how geopolitics, economics and diplomacy come together in the real world. Develop your strategic thinking, negotiation, research, public speaking and leadership skills while representing a country and making high-stakes decisions. Walk away with a deeper understanding of international relations, global finance and diplomatic decision-making, along with practical experience in teamwork, persuasion and problem-solving. Why Participate? Because this is more than a conventional competition; it is a global competition, where you compete with partipants from different geographies and challenge yourself to upscale. You won't simply answer questions or prepare a presentation. You will step into the role of a country and experience how international diplomacy actually works. Whether you are passionate about economics, finance, international relations, public policy, geopolitics, debating or simply looking for an intellectually engaging experience, this competition gives you a platform to think, negotiate, strategize and lead . Who Can Participate? The competition is open to students and young professionals from across India. Competition Format Round 1 - Country Allocation & Research Participants will be grouped into teams and assigned different BRICS countries. Teams will research their country's economic interests, foreign policy priorities and position on de-dollarization. Round 2 - The BRICS Summit The teams will participate in the mock BRICS summit, engaging in negotiations, diplomatic discussions, strategic alliances and formal presentations. Teams will present and defend their proposed framework for the future of the global financial system, followed by evaluation from the judging panel. The Final Question If the global financial system is changing, what role will BRICS play in shaping what comes next? Come prepared to represent. Negotiate. Strategize. Lead. Round 2 (Startup Showdown): Scored on solution quality, operational feasibility, creativity, and role-specific strategic reasoning. Scores across all team roles are aggregated to determine team ranking. Round 3 (Auction): Judged on budget utilization efficiency, executive team balance, strategic synergy between recruited figures, and the final pitch justification.

details_text: SEVA FIRST – Rashtriya Youth Innovation Challenge (RYIC) 2026 is a national platform that empowers India's youth to identify real problems in their own surroundings and transform them into sustainable, affordable, and implementable solutions. Launched at Delhi Technological University on 19 September 2026, the Challenge brings together students, researchers, educational institutions, industry, government and mentors to take innovations from problem identification and ideation to design, prototyping, validation and implementation. Rooted in the spirit of Seva First, RYIC seeks to nurture innovation, leadership and entrepreneurship while creating solutions that deliver meaningful impact for communities and the nation. Eligibility: The challenge is open to participants across the following categories: School & Vocational: Students from Class X onwards up to ITI level , participating individually or in teams, with appropriate institutional support. (Individuals and groups/teams may participate, subject to the specific eligibility requirements of each challenge) Applicability: The above participant categories are generally applicable to both National-Level and Local-Level Challenges . However, eligibility may vary depending on the specific problem statement and requirements of each challenge. What we expect from you: Registration: Step 1: Confirm your eligibility and select the appropriate regional or participation category. Step 2: Choose either National Level Innovation or Local Community Level Innovation. Step 3: Choose the theme that best matches the challenge you wish to address. Step 4: Select a specific problem statement from the list available under the chosen theme. You may also propose a relevant problem, where permitted. Step 5: Create your team and designate a Team Leader. Step 6: Describe the problem, proposed solution, innovation, technology, beneficiaries, feasibility and expected impact. Registration Phase Ideate: Launch of problem statements and areas of challenge for local-level innovations for registration; awareness campaign; idea submission; local problem identification; online orientation sessions. Choose from any of the 21 problem statements provided, or combine multiple themes into one integrated solution. Participants may also propose their own problem statement rooted in the environmental or community challenges they observe around them. All approaches will be given equal consideration. Theme 1: National Level Innovation: Participants will work on identified challenges and problem statements of national significance, developing innovative, sustainable and scalable solutions with the potential for adoption across India. Innovations should have a starting TRL of 4–6 and are expected to progress towards TRL 7–9 by the end of the Challenge, demonstrating a clear pathway from validated technology to an operational, deployable solution. For each theme, choose either the problem statement we've provided, or propose and solve your own problem within that category given below: Advanced Engineering, Infrastructure, Future Mobility & Transportation Defence, Intelligence, Space & National Security Disaster Management & Resilience Energy & Sustainable Technology & Environment Manufacturing & Electronics, AI, Robotics & Autonomous Systems Theme 2: Local Community Level Innovations – Village / District / State Participants will identify real problems and unmet needs within their own villages, districts or states and develop locally relevant, affordable, sustainable and implementable solutions that directly benefit the community and have the potential to be replicated or scaled in other regions. Innovations should have a starting TRL of 1–3 and are expected to progress towards TRL 6–7 by the end of the Challenge, demonstrating a clear journey from an initial concept or proof of concept to a validated and demonstrable solution. details_text: About the Competition: Quantathon '26 Powered by T.I.M.E Chennai is the flagship joint quantitative competition hosted by Pareto, the Economics Club of IIT Madras , and the Giffen Club of Madras School of Economics (MSE) . This high-intensity online contest pushes participants beyond theoretical economics into core quantitative methods, mathematical modeling, econometrics, and game theory under strict time constraints across two rounds. If you thrive on optimizing payoff matrices and analyzing stochastic models, this is your battleground. Key Topics: The syllabus spans Mathematical economics: Constrained and unconstrained optimization, differential equations, linear algebra, real analysis Econometrics and statistics: Regression models, hypothesis testing, probability distributions, stochastic processes Microeconomics and Game Theory: Nash equilibrium, strategic form games, information economics, general equilibrium analysis Macroeconomic modeling: Growth models, dynamic optimization, quantitative macro principles Structure & Format: Round 1 (Preliminary Qualifier): A 30-minute, 20–25 question MCQ/MSQ test on the Unstop Assessment Platform, testing speed, accuracy, and foundational concepts. Correct answers earn +3 marks, incorrect MCQs carry a -1 penalty, and MSQs require all correct options for credit. Top scorers advance to next Round. Round 2 (Main Final Round): A 45–60 minute test with advanced MCQs, MSQs, and Numerical Value Answer questions, focused on in-depth econometric modeling and multi-step derivation. This round is exclusive to Round 1 qualifiers and determines the final winners. Rewards & Prizes: Winner (1st Rank): Cash Prize of ₹10,000 + Certificate of Excellence 1st Runner-Up (2nd Rank): Cash Prize of ₹6,000 + Certificate of Excellence 2nd Runner-Up (3rd Rank): Cash Prize of ₹4,000 + Certificate of Excellence All Participants will receive Official Certificate of Participation jointly issued by IIT Madras Eligibility & Rules: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any recognized Indian institution. Students from Engineering, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, and Data Science backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Participation is individual ; cross-college and cross-specialization entries are welcome. Timers run continuously once started and cannot be paused. Plagiarism, unauthorized material, or tab-switching leads to immediate disqualification. Ties are broken by submission time, and the organizing committee's decisions are final.

title: Custom Paper Bags: How Small Brands Can Get Better Packaging
description: Custom Paper Bags That Make Sense for Growing Brands: Custom paper bags should work for your product, your customers, and your budget. Whether you're selling candles at a local market, shipping beauty products, or…
details_text: Custom Paper Bags That Make Sense for Growing Brands: Custom paper bags should work for your product, your customers, and your budget. Whether you're selling candles at a local market, shipping beauty products, or preparing for retail shelves, the right bag can make your brand feel more considered without forcing you into an expensive packaging order. The Cheapest Bag Isn't Always the Smartest Choice: Generic paper bags cost less upfront, but they can leave your branding looking disconnected. A coffee shop with premium products and a thin, poorly printed bag sends a mixed message. That doesn't mean you need luxury finishes. You need the right balance of paper quality, size, handles, and printing. Before ordering, check: Does the bag support the actual product weight? Is the size right, or are you paying to ship space? Will the print match your approved brand colors? Can the supplier handle your order quantity without surprise charges? I've seen small brands order thousands of bags before testing one with their actual products. That's an easy mistake to avoid. Choose Paper Bags That Fit Your Selling Channel: Your packaging needs change depending on where customers receive the product. A boutique beauty brand may need sturdy bags with twisted paper handles. A candle company should consider the weight and shape of glass jars. A retail brand preparing for store shelves needs consistent sizing and printing across different product lines. Keep Your First Order Manageable: Here's what actually works for early-stage brands: start with a quantity you can reasonably use, then scale when demand becomes predictable. Alora Packaging: Supports this approach with low MOQs, free design support, and free structural samples. That gives founders room to test a bag before committing to a large production run. No die or plate charges also help avoid costs that weren't part of the original budget. Alora Packaging has shipped for more than 10,000 brands, but the practical lesson is simple: get the size right, test the strength, and make sure the final cost works for your business. If you're planning a new bag order, start with your product dimensions and budget. A quick conversation with Alora Packaging can help you figure out what makes sense before you commit.

description: Mandatory Registration at: techfest.org/competitions/thetashift ThetaShift is a high-octane robotics challenge held as part of Techfest 2026-27 . Participants must design and construct a manually controlled, wireless…
details_text: Mandatory Registration at: techfest.org/competitions/thetashift ThetaShift is a high-octane robotics challenge held as part of Techfest 2026-27 . Participants must design and construct a manually controlled, wireless spherical robot built to navigate dynamic terrain, clear precision-based obstacles, and handle surprise course features . The top 5 teams from the Zonals round will qualify for the Grand Finale at the IIT Bombay campus from December 16–18, 2026 Key Rules & Technical Specifications: Bot Dimensions & Drive: Must be a wireless spherical bot with a diameter between 4 and 10 inches . Control Mechanism: Controlled manually via a joystick/remote or a mobile phone using 2.4GHz WiFi or Bluetooth . SSID format must follow TeamName_TF . Power Constraints: Onboard power supply only (≤ 24V DC for electric setups) . A physical power-disconnect switch is mandatory . Build Constraints: No ready-made Lego parts (ready-made gear assemblies permitted) . Spikes, abrasive materials, or adhesives damaging the track cause immediate disqualification . Arena & Challenge Breakdown: The 3x3m arena features 12 distinct terrain obstacles designed to test control, traction, and task execution : Terra Firma: Rock and sand path (50 Points) The Slalom Ridge: Triangular zig-zag barriers (30 Points) Sawtooth Ridge: Contiguous triangular speed bumps (30 Points) Infinity Circuit: Figure-8 path (60 Points) Domino Planks: Unevenly spaced rectangular planks (40 Points) Incline Overdrive: 10-degree incline ramp (40 Points) The Razor’s Edge: Elevated 7-inch wide track without side barriers (60 Points) Freefall Hairpin: Downhill slope ending in an immediate 90-degree turn (70 Points) The Gridlock: Alternating block grid path (30 Points) The U-Turn: Strict U-turn maneuver (20 Points) Bulldozer Drive: Pushing a block across a line and exiting in reverse (50 Points) Surprise Obstacles: Confidential obstacles introduced during the Grand Finale . Gameplay, Scoring & Time Limit: Time Limit: 6 minutes (360 seconds) per run . Each team gets 1 run . Scoring Formula: $\text{Total Score} = A + T - P$ A: Task Points earned (Max 480 Points) T: Time Bonus = 240 - Time in seconds (for runs under 4 minutes; Max 100 Points) P: Penalties (10 points per arena violation or extra pause time) Pauses & Resets: Two 45-second and one 30-second technical pauses allowed . Off-track bots reset to the start of the current obstacle with a 10-point penalty . Timeline & Rewards: Grand Finale: December 16–18, 2026 at IIT Bombay Campus . Certificates: Certificates of Excellence for the top 5 teams per zonal city and top 3 finale winners . Participation E-Certificates for teams crossing the benchmark score .

AI can help you think, but a copy-paste job will show. Keep it tight - approx 170 words, 2–3 paragraphs. Nobody's reading your essay. Skip the sales pitch - max 10% promo, no "link in bio" energy, no registration links. End with a question - not a "like/share/comment". Let the post earn it. Use these hashtags - #MyLinkedInEra and #BeUnstoppable along with the one for each prompt. Visuals should earn their spot - only add media that actually supports your point. LinkedIn + Unstop have the final say on eligibility and winners. Take On Both. Aim for the Top. Choose either round or go for both. details_text: SEVA FIRST – Rashtriya Youth Innovation Challenge (RYIC) 2026 is a national platform that empowers India's youth to identify real problems in their own surroundings and transform them into sustainable, affordable, and implementable solutions. Launched at Delhi Technological University on 19 September 2026, the Challenge brings together students, researchers, educational institutions, industry, government and mentors to take innovations from problem identification and ideation to design, prototyping, validation and implementation. Rooted in the spirit of Seva First, RYIC seeks to nurture innovation, leadership and entrepreneurship while creating solutions that deliver meaningful impact for communities and the nation. Eligibility: The challenge is open to participants across the following categories: Diploma & Higher Education: Students or teams from Diploma, Undergraduate, Postgraduate, and PhD programmes , including both technical and non-technical institutions. Industry & Government – Open Category: Urban/Rural industries, MSMEs, startups, R&D organisations, and Government laboratories may participate individually or through collaborative teams. (Individuals, groups/teams, and eligible organisations may participate, subject to the specific eligibility requirements of each challenge) Applicability: The above participant categories are generally applicable to both National-Level and Local-Level Challenges . However, eligibility may vary depending on the specific problem statement and requirements of each challenge. What we expect from you: Registration: Step 1: Confirm your eligibility and select the appropriate regional or participation category. Step 2: Choose either National Level Innovation or Local Community Level Innovation. Step 3: Choose the theme that best matches the challenge you wish to address. Step 4: Select a specific problem statement from the list available under the chosen theme. You may also propose a relevant problem, where permitted. Step 5: Create your team and designate a Team Leader. Step 6: Describe the problem, proposed solution, innovation, technology, beneficiaries, feasibility and expected impact. Registration Phase Ideate: Launch of problem statements and areas of challenge for local-level innovations for registration; awareness campaign; idea submission; local problem identification; online orientation sessions. Choose from any of the 21 problem statements provided, or combine multiple themes into one integrated solution. Participants may also propose their own problem statement rooted in the environmental or community challenges they observe around them. All approaches will be given equal consideration. Theme 1: National Level Innovation: Participants will work on identified challenges and problem statements of national significance, developing innovative, sustainable and scalable solutions with the potential for adoption across India. Innovations should have a starting TRL of 4–6 and are expected to progress towards TRL 7–9 by the end of the Challenge, demonstrating a clear pathway from validated technology to an operational, deployable solution. For each theme, choose either the problem statement we've provided, or propose and solve your own problem within that category given below: Advanced Engineering, Infrastructure, Future Mobility & Transportation Defence, Intelligence, Space & National Security Disaster Management & Resilience Energy & Sustainable Technology & Environment Manufacturing & Electronics, AI, Robotics & Autonomous Systems Theme 2: Local Community Level Innovations – Village / District / State Participants will identify real problems and unmet needs within their own villages, districts or states and develop locally relevant, affordable, sustainable and implementable solutions that directly benefit the community and have the potential to be replicated or scaled in other regions. Innovations should have a starting TRL of 1–3 and are expected to progress towards TRL 6–7 by the end

details_text: Overview Put Your Thinking & Deduction Skills to the Ultimate Test! Rules & Regulations Team Size: Teams must consist of 3 to 4 members . Attendance: All rounds will be conducted offline on-campus. Decisions: All decisions made by the quizmaster and organizing panel are final. Evaluation Criteria Prelims: Aggregate team score on the written test. Finals: Speed and accuracy on buzzer-based questions combined with written elements during the live finals.

title: National Economics Olympiad 2026
organiser: Shri Ram College of Commerce, University of Delhi
description: Overview The National Economics Olympiad, conducted by the Economics Society, SRCC, is an initiative to break the monotony of an unquestioning curricular regime among students of classes 11th & 12th and harness the true…
details_text: Overview The National Economics Olympiad, conducted by the Economics Society, SRCC, is an initiative to break the monotony of an unquestioning curricular regime among students of classes 11th & 12th and harness the true potential of the discipline of economics. Economics is a vast subject whose beauty lies as much in theory as in its applicability. Feel the same and think that school exams are too theoretical? The 9th edition of the biggest Economics Olympiad for school students is back to allow kids to look beyond their curriculum and truly ‘Discover the Economist’ in themselves. Prepare yourself for a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity where you will be faced with a unique combination involving the application of various economic concepts, logical reasoning, quantitative skills, current affairs, case studies, as well as data interpretation and rise above many students all over the world! The registration fee is ₹199. General Guidelines for the Olympiad: You would have received the link for the examination on your registered email IDs. That link can be used to access the examination listing and give the examination. Kindly note: The publication of results for the preliminary round will include the e-mail ID you registered for the Olympiad with. By registering for this Olympiad, you acknowledge and agree that you have no objection to your e-mail ID being displayed to the other participants. Structure of the Olympiad: The Olympiad shall consist of four sections as follows: Application of Economic Concepts Logical Reasoning Quantitative Aptitude Current Affairs In Prelims, there will be 50 questions in total. Participants will be provided with a maximum time of 60 minutes for this round of the Olympiad. The structure and details of the Final round will be intimated to the finalists 1 week prior to the final round. The examination is an assessment of a student’s analytical and problem-solving skills. You can refer to the syllabus of NEO 2026 below (Attachments section). No prior preparation is required for the Olympiad. However, a Sample Questions Booklet is provided after the completion of registration to get a brief idea of what the Olympiad entails. About the Institution: Shri Ram College of Commerce is a premier institution when it comes to the fields of undergraduate commerce and economics. The institution stands by its vision of achieving and sustaining excellence in teaching and research and enriching local, national and international communities through its research, the skills of alumni, and the publishing of academic and educational materials. The Economics Society, SRCC is a student-run organisation that works with the objective of fostering social and intellectual activity among students by providing them with a challenging and stimulating environment to test their acumen in a plethora of domains. The Society has seen manifold growth since its inception in the late 1970s. Its objective has always been to facilitate discourse and dialogue on pertinent issues surrounding us. The society has published its research on multiple platforms, including the annual magazine ‘Artha’ and the online publication ‘Ceteris Paribus’, which has seen articles about the economic sphere covering a multitude of topics. What's at Stake? Cumulative cash prizes of ₹1,20,000+ & certificate of excellence for winners. Certificate of merit to all finalists. Certificate of participation to all participants.

description: The International Conference on AI-Driven Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICAIDIET'26) is a premier global conference organized by SNS College of Technology, Coimbatore, in academic collaboration with…
details_text: The International Conference on AI-Driven Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICAIDIET'26) is a premier global conference organized by SNS College of Technology, Coimbatore, in academic collaboration with Yorkville University, Canada. Scheduled for 20–21 November 2026, the conference provides an international platform for researchers, academicians, industry professionals, and students to present original research, exchange innovative ideas, and discuss the latest developments in Artificial Intelligence and emerging engineering technologies. ICAIDIET'26 features keynote lectures by distinguished experts, technical paper presentations, networking opportunities, and collaborative discussions that promote research excellence and real-world innovation. The conference will be conducted in Hybrid Mode, allowing participants to attend either on campus or virtually. Conference Tracks Authors are invited to submit original research papers in, but not limited to, the following areas: Artificial Intelligence & Intelligent Systems Machine Learning & Advanced Analytics Data Science & Decision Intelligence IoT, Edge Computing & Embedded Systems Communication Systems & Network Technologies Cybersecurity & Secure Computing Robotics, Automation & Smart Industry Emerging Technologies, Sustainability & AI Management Eligibility Faculty members Research scholars UG & PG students Industry professionals Scientists and innovators Participants from India and abroad are welcome. Submission Guidelines Submit original, unpublished research work that is not under consideration elsewhere. Manuscripts must follow the official conference template. Paper length should be 10–14 pages. Similarity index must be below 15%. All papers will undergo a rigorous double-blind peer-review process. Papers not meeting the formatting or ethical requirements may be rejected without review. Final publication is subject to successful peer review, registration, and publisher quality checks. Submission Process Prepare your manuscript according to the conference guidelines. Submit your paper through the Microsoft CMT submission portal. Papers will undergo double-blind peer review by domain experts. Accepted authors will receive acceptance notification. Complete registration within the specified timeline. Submit the camera-ready manuscript. Present your work during ICAIDIET'26 in online or offline mode. Important Dates Paper Submission Deadline: 21 September 2026 (The submission deadline may be extended at the discretion of the Organizing Committee based on conference requirements and other relevant factors. Any extension will be announced through the official conference website and communication channels.) Acceptance Notification: 20 October 2026 Early Bird Registration: 22 October 2026 Late Registration: 23–28 October 2026 Final Manuscript Notification: 2 November 2026 Conference Dates: 20–21 November 2026 Publication Accepted and registered papers will be considered for publication in the Wiley Conference Proceedings, with submission for Scopus indexing, subject to publisher policies and indexing requirements. Join ICAIDIET'26 to showcase your research, interact with leading experts, build global collaborations, and contribute to the future of AI-driven engineering and technology. title: One Day workshop on Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques for Supervised Machine Learning using Python 2026
description: This Workshop aims at providing a forum for members of the research and academy community. The Workshop enables the participants to understand the recent technologies in ML Foundations, ensemble techniques such as…
details_text: This Workshop aims at providing a forum for members of the research and academy community. The Workshop enables the participants to understand the recent technologies in ML Foundations, ensemble techniques such as Boosting, Voting, and Stacking, along with their practical implementation using Python. The One-Day Workshop on Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques for Supervised Machine Learning aims to provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts, advanced methodologies, and practical applications of ensemble learning. The workshop will introduce the principles of ensemble modeling and explain how combining multiple base learners can enhance the accuracy and reliability of predictive models. Participants will explore major ensemble techniques, including Bagging, Random Forest, Boosting, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Voting Classifiers, and Stacking.The workshop will emphasize the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of these techniques, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and suitability for different supervised learning tasks. Participants will gain insights into model selection, hyperparameter tuning, feature importance analysis, and performance evaluation using appropriate metrics for classification and regression problems. A hands-on session using Python and machine learning libraries such as Scikit-learn will enable participants to implement ensemble algorithms, experiment with real-world datasets, and compare the performance of individual models with ensemble-based approaches.

title: 4th Edition of Winter School on Biomedical Optics (4th WiSBO)

description: Biomedical optics has become one of the most inevitable field in the recent research in clinical diagnosis and treatment. In this course, we will learn about the fundamentals of biomedical optics, starting from how the…
details_text: Biomedical optics has become one of the most inevitable field in the recent research in clinical diagnosis and treatment. In this course, we will learn about the fundamentals of biomedical optics, starting from how the photon interacts with a single atom, to a diatomic species, and then with polyatomic species such as haemoglobin. You will learn the basics of spectroscopy and different imaging modalities such as fluorescence, UV-Vis-NIR, diffuse optics, polarization, Speckle contrast, and multimodal imaging. You will also learn about fundamental and advances in the field of optical biosensors and various plasmonic resonances. We will also discuss the principles and details along with demonstration of various microscopic imaging such as brightfield, phase contrast, fluorescence and polarization-based microscopy.The Department of Electronics and Communication, IIITDM Kancheepuram is organizing the 4th Edition of Winter School on Biomedical Optics (WiSBO ’26-27) at IIITDM Kancheepuram-Chennai, India between 27th December to 30th December. The participants (about 40 to 50) will be PhD students, Faculty members, and Industry participants working in the field of biomedical optics throughout India.
